items.statement: FY25 RAM share 62.73%
items.quote: RAM percentage, we ha ve given a guidance of 60 to 62% and actually 62.73%.
our CRAR has also improved to 18.49%, as it is 16.25% last quarter. CET has improved to 16.03%. Tier 1, 16.37%.

items.statement: Vehicle loan growth 59% driven by four-wheeler segment
items.quote: The growth is in four -wheeler only. Maximum growth is in four -wheeler and actually, we have revamped our vehicle loan scheme last year.

items.statement: Personal loan growth 46% YoY, entirely to ETB customers
items.quote: This personal loan is totally to ETB customers, number 1. And number 2, there are two components. One, over the salary account holders. 2nd is our pension account holders.

items.statement: Digital active mobile banking users nearly doubled in FY25
items.quote: We have almost doubled our mobile active users.

items.statement: Tab banking enabled across all 3000+ branches for onboarding
items.quote: now in last March quarter we have given Tab to the entire 3 000 plus branches.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio 10,500 crore, fully compliant with RBI guidelines
items.quote: See total gold line portfolio of our bank is 10,500 crore and we are all in compliance with the RBI guidelines of our gold loan portfolio also.

items.statement: Corporate SMA watch list ~700 crore with cash flow issues but no slippage in 1.5 years
items.quote: There are few accounts in the corporate segment around 700 crore which are in our wat ch list which we continue to monitor. Sometimes they come into SMA, sometimes they come out of SMA, but they are continuously paying and playing there are certain challenges with them, cash flow issues are there but these accounts we have seen over a perio d of last 1.5 years, they have not slipped.

items.statement: Co-lending portfolio 2200 crore across 7 partnerships; open to new partnerships based on policy criteria
items.quote: we have already done around 7 co -lending partnerships and our total co -lending port folio under this partnership is 2,200 crores. So given an opportunity in the current financial year also, we'll continue to evaluate the proposals coming to us.

items.statement: FY26 business growth target ~14%, advances 15-16%, deposits 12-13%, CASA ~48% +/-1%, NIM above 3%, gross NPA below 3%, net NPA target 0.45%
items.quote: It will be around 14% growth, that is the top line growth. And then advances, will be around 15% to 16% and deposit growth will be around 12% to 13%. And CASA, we would like to have around 48% because now we are at 49%. And whatever the things that happen and then keeping the market realities, we are targeting at 48% with plus or minus 1%. So NIM also, we always knew that our guidance will be abov

items.statement: FY26 recovery target INR 4,500 crores total, INR 1,500-1,700 crores from technical write-offs
items.quote: last year, we made a total recovery of INR4,062 crores. And in this year, we are eying for INR4,500 crores. M.V. Rao: Last couple of years, our run rate as far as the recovery in write-off is roughly around 4.5%, 5%. This year also, I mean, the technical write-off book now stands at INR35,413.56 crores. And we expect a similar amount, around INR1,500 crores to INR1,700 crores to be recovered durin

items.statement: Expect to touch 1% ROA during FY26
items.quote: at our past 16 quarters ' record, we are quite confident that we should be able to touch 1% ROA during this financial year

items.statement: Digital/technology capex budgeted at INR 300-500 crores for FY26
items.quote: So this year also, we are doing it something around the INR300 crores to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Plan to roll out 250 BC MAXX centers in H1 FY26 after 25-center pilot
items.quote: And already as a pilot, we started in 25 centers, and it is doing well. And having the good experience, we will be rolling out to the 250 centers within this first half year.

items.statement: NIM target maintained above 3% despite Q4 dip; CASA focus to support NIM
items.quote: However, with the thrust that we are laying on not only maintaining our CASA at 49% or 50% plus/minus 1%, we are pretty sure that overall NIM, we should be able to maintain well within our guidance of above 3%.

items.statement: Treasury gains expected INR 600-800 crores additional profit in FY26 from investment sales due to rate cuts
items.quote: As far as our bank is concerned, we are expecting around INR600 crores to INR800 crores additional profit by sale of investment.

items.statement: Retail segment 28.4% of advances, grew 15.72% YoY; home loans 63.32% of retail, grew 18.40%
items.quote: The retail segment, which constitutes 28.40% of our total advances, has seen a Y-o-Y growth of 15.72%. And the home loan portfolio, which constitutes 63.32%, has seen a growth of 18.40% on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: Restructured book INR 5,114 cr (normal INR 2,169 cr + COVID INR 2,945 cr); SMA-2 only INR 93 cr in 9 accounts
items.quote: The restructured book now stands at INR5,114 crores, which includes the no rmal restructuring at INR2,169 crores and the COVID-19 resolution restructured book of INR2,945 crores. As far as the special mention accounts of INR5 crores and above are concerned, the total is INR700 crores in 44 accounts, out of which SMA -2 is only 9 a ccounts of INR93 crores

items.statement: Aviation account 100% technically written off, not on books; any recovery goes to bottom line
items.quote: as far as our books are concerned, it is 100% technically written -off account. It is not accounted in our books right now. It is totally 100% TW account for us

items.statement: CRAR improved to 17.02% (CET1 14.73%), leverage ratio 6.15%
items.quote: The capital adequacy ratio has improved to 17.02% with CET1 at 14.73%, and the leverage ratio has improved to 6.15%.

items.statement: Investment portfolio yield 6.87%; treasury modified duration 3.46% (SLR 3.52%), PV01 13.28%
items.quote: The investment portfolio has seen a very good, I mean, yield with 6.87% being the yield on investment. The treasury M duration is at 3.46% and for SLR, it is 3.52%, and the PV01 for SLR plus non-SLR is at 13.28%.

items.statement: Loan book mix: ~INR 1.72 lakh cr RBLR, INR 70,000 cr MCLR, INR 38,000 cr fixed rate
items.quote: As far as the breakup of our RBLR and other advances is concerned, we have roughly around INR1,72,000 crores book on RBLR, around INR70,000 crores is on MCLR and INR38,000 crores is on fixed rate.

items.statement: Focus on NRI deposits and forex centralization via super app wealth management modules
items.quote: Where after the super app, we will be activating our wealth management modules and then wealth management structure, which is specifically designed to cater to the needs of the HNIs and also centralizing the forex, which has already started working. We'll be focusing on the NRI deposits and the NRI connections.

items.statement: Expect to consume entire DTA (INR 3,145 cr) by March 2026 and move to new tax regime
items.quote: And whatever our internal assessment is that we should be able to consume the entire DTA by March '26 and move to the new tax regime, which would definitely give us some cushion in the tax front coming forward.

items.statement: Deposits grew 7.19% YoY to INR 4.12 lakh cr; CASA grew 4.79%
items.quote: The total business has seen a growth of 10.37%; total deposits at 7.19%; CASA at 4.79%. And we still are able to hold on to our 48.91%, that is close to 49% of CASA share.

items.statement: Corporate credit growth robust in Q4; confident of achieving 14-16% advance growth despite global uncertainties
items.quote: And in the last quarter, you would have seen that our corporate growth has also been very robust. So I don't think that achieving this 14% to 16% growth in the advances should be any issue.

items.statement: Target loan growth of ~20% and deposit growth of 22-23% for FY26
items.quote: But now we want to grow or we are targeting inside the bank to grow opex only by 12% to 13%. So you can see that the bank is putting brakes on opex. It is rather leveraging the same balance sheet, with the same level of opex, we're growing the balance sheet by 20%, 22%.

items.statement: Target opex growth of 12-13% for FY26
items.quote: But now we want to grow or we are targeting inside the bank to grow opex only by 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Expect credit cost of ~1.85-1.90% for FY26, down ~50 bps from FY25
items.quote: So next year, you should expect us to be somewhere in the zone of about 1.85%, 1.90%. Sudhanshu? Sudhanshu Jain: Yes. So on an overall basis, you can expect about a 50 bps reduction in credit cost for next year

items.statement: Expect NIM to decline by ~10 bps from Q4 FY25 level
items.quote: So net-net, blend, we are expecting the NIM to come down by about 10 basis points, all things playing with each other. Over the NIM of Q4 of FY25.

items.statement: Target RoE of 15% from current ~7%
items.quote: Our first stop is to actually move this from 7% to 15%. We really intend to do it. We're serious about that.

items.statement: Board approved CCPS issuance to two investors for ~Rs 7,500 crore, converting to equity
items.quote: Post the quarter end, we had also in the second week of April, announced that the Board has approved issuance of CCPS to 2 marquee investors. These would eventually get converted into equity to the extent of about Rs.7,500 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 25 bps for FY25
items.quote: The Board in its meeting today has recommended a dividend of 25 bps for FY 25. This will be subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: NIM on AUM at 5.95% in Q4 FY25, down 9 bps QoQ due to microfinance book decline
items.quote: The net interest margin on AUM for the quarter is 5.95%. We saw a moderation of 9 basis points vis-a-vis the previous quarter, and this is greatly attributable to the microfinance business, where the book has further come down and hence, the NIM has got impacted.

items.statement: Plan to cut FD peak rates from ~7.90% to ~7.20% to match large banks; SA rate cuts also planned
items.quote: We are paying probably about 70 or 80 basis points more than the large big 4 banks on the fixed deposit side. But we want to literally go down to their rates. So we might see a large cut from our side to go like the peak rate.

items.statement: Blended SA rate at 5.9% in Q4 FY25; further cuts planned for larger ticket sizes
items.quote: It's for the current quarter, it's about 5.9%. As I said, we made some changes in February. The full impact of that would play out into the next quarter. That, coupled with certain other changes which we plan to do, would further bring down the SA rates.

items.statement: GNPA 1.87%, NNPA 0.53% in March 2025; ex-MFI GNPA 1.63% improved 19 bps QoQ
items.quote: The gross NPA of the bank stood at 1.87% at March. And similarly, net NPA is at 0.53%. If we exclude the microfinance book, then the GNPA in fact, is at 1.63%, and this has improved by 19 bps on a sequential basis.

items.statement: MFI SMA 0 down from Rs 275 cr to Rs 152 cr QoQ; SMA 1&2 down from Rs 501 cr to Rs 488 cr
items.quote: But in March '25, it has come down from Rs. 275 crores to Rs. 152 crores, this is a very big development. It just shows that this curve, what we talked about that the microfinance is peaking out in this quarter and coming down.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 99.2% in March 2025 (99.4% ex-Karnataka)
items.quote: We have also seen an improvement in collection efficiency during the quarter, and it stood at 99.2% for March 25. And ex Karnataka, actually, it is at 99.4%.

items.statement: MFI provision coverage ~72% on SMA 1,2 and NPA combined; not 100% on GNPA
items.quote: So during the quarter, we have not released any provision out of that Rs. 315 crores so SMA 1, SMA 2 put together and NPA, we would have a cover of about 72%.

items.statement: Funded assets grew 20.4% YoY to Rs 2.42 lakh cr; mortgage 19%, vehicle 26%, business banking 32%, wholesale 29% YoY
items.quote: If you go through the presentation and we have given more details on Slide 28, the growth was largely led by mortgage segment, which has grown by 19% on a Y-o-Y basis, the vehicle loan segment, which has grown at 26% on a Y-o-Y basis. The business banking, which is largely secured working capital that has grown at 32% on a Y-o-Y basis then the wholesale business has grown by 29% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Credit cards issued >3.5 million, book size ~Rs 7,500 cr; gross spends up 42% YoY; turned operationally breakeven in 4 years
items.quote: The bank has now issued more than 3.5 million credit cards. The book size has reached now Rs. 7,500-odd crores at March. The gross spends on the credit cards grew strongly by about 42% in FY 25. I'm again happy to report that credit card as a business has turned operationally breakeven within 4 years of launch.

items.statement: Repaid Rs 7,000 cr high-cost legacy borrowings in FY25; residual ~Rs 4,800 cr, mostly maturing in FY26
items.quote: We have repaid high-cost legacy borrowings to the extent of about Rs. 7,000 crores in this current financial year. The residual book now is, I would say, small at about Rs. 4,800 crores. And about bulk of it, that is about Rs. 4,500 crores will mature in the next year itself.

items.statement: Credit-to-deposit ratio improved to 93.9% from 98.4% YoY; incremental CD ratio 76.1%
items.quote: We continue to bring down the credit-to-deposit ratio. That is now down to 93.9%. This was 98.4% at March '24. If we compute the incremental credit-to-deposit ratio during last 1 year, then it's at about 76.1%.

items.statement: Branch count crossed 1,000 (1,002 at March 31); opened 31 branches in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Happy to report that our branch count has crossed the 1,000 mark. It was 1,002 at 31st of March. We opened about 31 branches during the current quarter also.

items.statement: CASA ratio stable at ~47%; CASA deposits up 25% YoY; average CASA up 30% YoY in Q4
items.quote: CASA ratio, if you see for us, it has been quite stable around the 47% mark and that CASA deposits have increased strongly by about 25% on a Y-o-Y basis. If you see average CASA deposits for Q4, the increase is 30%, in fact, on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Retail LCR improved from 12% to ~60%, now in line with large private banks
items.quote: Retail LCR, I don't mean the retail deposits as coming from retail branches. I mean retail LCR, we were 12% initially. Today, we are at about 60%, must share with you that we are now in line with large private sector banks, which gives tremendous stability.

items.statement: Implemented new MFIN guardrails from February 2025; MFI disbursements fell to Rs 760 cr in Q4
items.quote: So in terms of the MFIN guidelines, which have come in from April, we had implemented it slightly prior to that. So these guidelines we made effective already from February. So to that extent, we also saw some impact on disbursements that came down to about Rs. 760 crores in the current quarter.

items.statement: FY25 PAT dropped to Rs 1,525 cr from Rs 2,957 cr due to MFI stress; expect recovery in FY26 and winning ways by FY27-29
items.quote: So instead of our PAT going up from Rs. 2,400 crores to Rs. 2,900 crores upwards, we did a downturn this year. I do agree. So it's down to about Rs. 1,500 crores. So I want to share with you that this dip is not that there's any fundamental issue with the bank or the model where it's going to go cutting down this way.

items.statement: New LCR guidelines may have 1-2% adverse impact on LCR due to higher retail TD runoff factor
items.quote: Cumulatively, however, we are seeing a small impact of maybe about 1% to 2%, but that's not material in the overall scheme of things.

items.statement: Microfinance book degrew 28.3% YoY in FY25; infrastructure book now sub-1% of funded assets
items.quote: During the year, we also had a degrowth of 28.3% on the microfinance business because of the challenges going around that sector. Infrastructure book, happy to report, is now sub-1% of the total funded assets.

items.statement: Opex growth moderated sequentially: Q1 21.1%, Q2 17.7%, Q3 16.1%, Q4 12.2% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY 25, our opex grew 21.1% Y-o-Y. In Q2 FY25, our opex grew 17.7% Y-o-Y. In Q3 FY25, it grew by 16.1% Y-o-Y. In Q4 FY25, the quarter just ended, it came down to 12.2% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Core operating profit ex-MFI grew 31% YoY in FY25 and 20% YoY in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Core operating profit for the year, excluding trading gains, that has grown by 17% on a Y-o-Y basis. And we have also given data that if we take out microfinance, then based on our internal reporting, this number has gone up by 31%.

items.statement: Credit card business expected to be profitable by FY28-FY29, spinning cash
items.quote: And we think by FY28, FY29, this should be really, like if I use the word loosely, should be spinning cash.

items.statement: Credit card credit cost lower in FY25 than previous year, expected to further decline next year
items.quote: And for the full year, credit cost on credit card is lower than previous year and we expect it to further come down into the next year.

items.statement: Credit card business net of credit cost expected to be profitable by FY27
items.quote: It is net of credit cost, think of it like FY27, it should be like in the money and a launch year of FY22.

items.statement: Retail liabilities cost ratio improved from 4.2% to 1.2% over 5 years, targeting breakeven in next 5 years
items.quote: We feel that this 4.2% has come down to 1.2% over the 5 years and in the next 5 years, it should become 0.

items.statement: Overall cost-income ratio target of 65% by FY27 with 12-13% opex growth
items.quote: You should expect from us about 12%, 13% opex growth.

items.statement: Credit card cost-income ratio to decline from 100% to ~75% over next 2 years
items.quote: It should dip steeply from here next 2 years to come down to about 75 -odd percent.

items.statement: Retail liabilities cost-income ratio to decline from 171% to 140%
items.quote: And liabilities should dip from 171% to 140%.

items.statement: Loan growth target of ~20% with deposit growth slightly higher to improve LDR
items.quote: We are clear we want to grow this because if you want to grow loan book by 20%, loan deposit will grow by 20% for sure, minimum.

items.statement: LDR target to settle in late 80s from current 93%
items.quote: Yes, we should come down to the, our ratio is late 80s.

items.statement: MFI proportion expected to decline to 3-3.5% of overall loans next year
items.quote: We feel that the MFI proportion may come down to about 3% to 3.5% into the next year.

items.statement: Fee income growth target of 14-15% for next year
items.quote: We feel that we should be able to grow fees at around 14% to 15% even into the next year.

items.statement: Targeting 1% ROA by end of FY26 (Q4)
items.quote: Yes, trying to get there by the end of this year, fourth quarter.

items.statement: No major new businesses needed to achieve 20% growth target
items.quote: We don't have to launch any major new businesses.

items.statement: Credit card average book reached Rs 6,000 crores in FY25 with operational breakeven achieved
items.quote: So therefore, average book for FY 25 has now touched Rs. 6,000 crores, and we have reached operating breakeven.

items.statement: Retail liabilities incremental business very profitable despite 25% book growth
items.quote: The good news is that even though the book is growing by maybe like 25% per year, and which means that the incremental business on this front is really very profitable.

items.statement: Choosing to cut FD rates rather than SA rates to protect CASA ratio and P&L
items.quote: We are choosing to cut FD rates and get the P&L. And SA also we will touch, but we'll do it, like I said, like earlier told you what are the actions we'll take on SA.

items.statement: Cut SA rate for zero to Rs 5 lakhs from 7% to 3% in one shot
items.quote: For example, zero to Rs. 5 lakhs, we cut it straight to 3%. I don't think people expect us to go that far by cutting up 7% to 3%. We did it in 1 shot.

items.statement: Built strong customer experience, technology, culture and UI/UX as competitive moat
items.quote: The experience layer that bank has built for customers, the culture they built within the bank, the technology layer that we build so that the experience layer at the call center, our app, our branches, our VRM, that one to build, the UI/UX, the design, the aesthetics of it, all this and the culture of being soft with customers, it's very hard to build such things.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced from 48% to 11% of total liabilities since merger, targeting ICICI Bank's ~6.5%
items.quote: Borrowings as a percentage of total liabilities was about 48% at the time of merger. Today, it has come down to only 11%.

items.statement: CCPS issued with 8% return, auto-converts if stock stays above Rs 60 VWAP for 45 trading days
items.quote: The terms of the contract are that if the stock stays above Rs. 60 for a period of 45 trading days, then it automatically stands converted. So to make it clear, therefore, we don't have to really exactly wait for 18 months and all that stuff.

items.statement: MFI credit cost for full year at 10.5%, expected to come down next year
items.quote: The credit cost of the full year for microfinance is about 10.5%.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency 99.2% in March (99.4% ex-Karnataka), similar trajectory in April
items.quote: Collection efficiency, as you would have noted that it was 99.2% for March month and ex Karnataka is at 99.4%, and we have seen a good rebounds in, I would say, a month or so, and the same trajectory is broadly holding up in April.

items.statement: Ex-MFI credit cost at 1.76%, performing on expected lines
items.quote: Suffice to say that we are on record in telling you that, that is perfectly playing on plan. It is net of credit cost, think of it like FY27, it should be like in the money and a launch year of FY22.

items.statement: CASA ratio 46-47% with CA at 7-8% and SA at ~40% of customer deposits
items.quote: So CA as a proportion of customer deposits would be about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Current account deposits grown 21-22% YoY to ~Rs 4,500 crores
items.quote: CA has grown by about 21%, 22% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Loan book: 61% fixed rate, 39% floating (30% repo-linked, rest MCLR/T-bills)
items.quote: We have about 61% of the book which is fixed rate, and which means 39% is floating. And within that 39%, about 30% is linked to repo and rest is linked to MCLR, T bills and so on.

items.statement: Monitoring state-level risks like Karnataka for lending strategy
items.quote: We should watch out more and more carefully for the environment, what happened to Karnataka, whether it should happen to any of the state, what is an impact of that on the book?

items.statement: No Y-o-Y PAT growth expected in Q1 FY26 due to MFI impact, meaningful growth from Q2 onwards
items.quote: We do not expect a Y-o-Y growth on PAT at least not in Q1. And then for Q2 onwards, hopefully, we should start delivering Y-o-Y growth meaningfully.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised upward to 25% for FY25 and achieved
items.quote: In quarter 1 '25, we had revised our guidance upwards from 20% to 25% on the revenue growth. For FY '25, we are happy to share that we've achieved that with a revenue of INR 1,847 crores.

items.statement: Digital revenue contribution expected to exceed 25% in FY26
items.quote: In FY '25, digital contributed to 21% of the overall revenue. And we expect this year to exceed to 25% and above, in FY '26.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio target maintained at 25% range for FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead for FY '26, our priorities remain clear , accelerate CASA and deposit growth, enhance digital infrastructure, deepen finance Fintech partnership while maintaining our cost -income ratio in the range of 25%.

items.statement: Loan referral business targets INR300 crores monthly disbursement in first half of FY26
items.quote: Our next target will be to reach INR300 crores, which means INR100 crores a month is something which we aspire to reach in this year, maybe in the first half.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR165 crores driven by core banking migration; FY26 capex expected INR100 crores-plus
items.quote: Capital expenditure for FY '25 stood at INR165 crores, significantly higher year-on-year. This was driven by strategic investment in migration of our core banking system.

items.statement: Incremental INR90-100 crores capex anticipated for SFB technology and operations
items.quote: We anticipate incremental INR90 crores to INR100 crores capex cost on technology and operations for SFB.

items.statement: Next-generation core banking platform with hollow-the-core architecture scheduled to go live this quarter
items.quote: Our next -generation core banking platform, along with the "hollow the core" architecture, is scheduled to go live in this quarter.

items.statement: CASA revenue grew 43% to INR544 crores contributing 30% of total revenue
items.quote: CASA revenue increased 43% to INR 544 crores, including the float income; and now contr ibutes 30% of the full revenue

items.statement: Renewal income grew 48% to INR190 crores
items.quote: Renewal income grew by 48% Y -o-Y to INR190 crores, underscoring the effectiveness of our customer ownership strategy.

items.statement: Average deposits rose 37% to INR1,849 crores with peak deposits crossing INR2,500 crores
items.quote: Average deposits for FY '25 rose 37% to INR 1,849 crores. And average customer balance improved to INR 1,356, supporting higher treasury income through better float utilization.

items.statement: Customer base reached 1.43 crores with 33 lakh new accounts added in FY25
items.quote: Our total customers grew to 1.43 crores, with over 33 lakhs new accounts added in FY '25, including 8.6 lakhs accounts in Q4.

items.statement: Digital throughput increased 70% to INR2.25 lakh crores, now 49% of total throughput
items.quote: Digital throughput increased 70% and touched INR2.25 lakh crores and now accounts to 49% of the total throughput.

items.statement: UPI market share increased from 1.27% to 1.62% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our UPI market share has also increased substantially from 1.27% in quarter 4 last year to 1.62% in quarter 4 '25.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 22% to INR234 crores; PBT increased 26% to INR108 crores
items.quote: Our EBITDA rose by 22% to INR234 crores and PBT increased 26% to INR108 crores, driven by operating leverage and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio improved to 25.6% from 26.5%
items.quote: For FY '25, we closed the year with a cost -income ratio of 25.6%. This vis -à-vis the previous year was 26.5%.

items.statement: Digital segment PBT margin double-digit vs overall 5.9%
items.quote: With its inherently low operating costs, digital segment has materially contributed to structural improvement in our profitability, i.e., at a PBT margin, which has more than doubled from 2.6 % in FY '21 to 5.9% in FY '25.

items.statement: CMS take rate moderated from 0.21% to 0.18%; further moderation expected in FY26
items.quote: Enhanced competition is leading to moderation of take rate, which was 0.18% in FY '25 vis-a-vis 0.21% in FY '24.

items.statement: AePS showed recovery in H2 with Q4 revenue up 23% and throughput up 10%
items.quote: Notably, AePS showed some signs of recovery in second half, with Q4 revenue growing 23% and throughput rising 10% Y -o-Y to INR 8,127 crores.

items.statement: Remittance business impacted by regulatory changes and customer shift to CASA; decline expected to settle next quarter
items.quote: The DE growth is happening, as I mentioned, because of the regulatory thing and the cannibalization of customers per se; and also some other alternate channels which have come up for doing remittances, which we are also planning to launch in this quarter.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 4.2x to INR390 crores, contributing 21% of total revenue
items.quote: Our digital business delivered exceptional performance in FY '25 with revenue growing 4.2x on a year -on-year basis, with a total revenue of INR390 crores.

items.statement: Launched Gullak corporate salary CASA product for MSMEs; opening 7,000-8,000 accounts monthly
items.quote: So that is something which we are now focusing on Gullak. It's we started in the month -- I think November, December last year; and about 7,000 to 8,000 accounts, we are opening per month on account of that.

items.statement: Merchant base expanded to nearly 19 lakh covering 97% of PIN codes; added 1.5 lakh new merchants
items.quote: As of FY '25, we have covered nearly 97% of India's PIN codes through a strong and growing merchant base of nearly 19 lakh merchants. During the year , we added 1.5 lakh new merchants.

items.statement: CMS facing headwinds from MFI sector stress and increased competition moderating take rates
items.quote: While everything seems to be going well, our CMS business, we are seeing some headwinds in the past 2 quarters given the stress in the entire MFI sector in specific and also witnessing take rate issue because of the increased competition per se.

items.statement: SFB application with RBI; good information exchange in last quarter; building operational readiness
items.quote: The application is with the Reserve Bank of India. There has been a good exchange of information in the last quarter or so. Our understanding is that it is moving in the right direction, but end of the day, we will have to wait for the regulator to come back as such.

items.statement: Regulatory advisories on cyber fraud and mule accounts calibrating digital growth
items.quote: There's a lot of regulatory advisories and other things which are happening because of the heightened mule accounts as well as on the digital frauds which are happening, so we are cognizant of that.

items.statement: Cost of funds roughly 2% providing competitive pricing leeway for SFB lending

items.quote: Thirdly, my 80% to 85% of the cost is basically aluminum. So, it's more or less an aluminum metal industry rather than a packaging industry, where the rates of the aluminum are decided by Hindalco every first of the month, which either increases or goes down.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative due to 45-60 day debtor credit and 1-month inventory; plans to optimize
items.quote: Sir, the major reason of the working capital being negative is the amount of cre dit that we are giving to the debtors. So, major reason is credit only. We will try to optimize and bring it down to a reasonable level

items.statement: Current debt INR 20 crore; comfortable up to INR 30 crore; plans to raise INR 10 crore more
items.quote: So, we are currently taking a debt of around INR 20 crores. We are planning more INR 10 crores. So, till INR 30 crores, we are comfortable in this year.

items.statement: Planning preferential allotment of INR 10-15 crore for capex and working capital
items.quote: To meet with it, preference round maybe around a month or two, we are in talks with a merchant banker. And with more debt coming in with our current banker, this may be sorted out.

items.statement: No exports currently; exploring export opportunities this year due to China sanctions
items.quote: We might explore it like directly we are not exporting anything now, but definitely that thing is in plan. We may do this year.

items.statement: 65-70 pharma clients across 14 states; focus on B/B+ category for better terms; expanding geographically to South India
items.quote: We have over 65 to 70 pharmaceutical clients across 14 states in India and we have built a good reputation for customization, quality and reliability.

items.statement: Main listed peers: PG Foils, MMP Foils (backward integrated); Synthiko Foils (similar line); GSM does 2-3x Synthiko volume
items.quote: Ma'am there are two major listed competitors to us. They are one step into backward integration than us, that is PG and MMP. And the peer-to-peer comparison with us would be Synthiko Foil another listed party. We are almost doing like two to three times more volume than them.

items.statement: Pharma packaging industry growing 15-20% (not 4-5%); driven by generics, biosimilars, OTC exports
items.quote: The industry is growing at a much more rate, it's not 4 % to 5%. It may be growing around 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: Food foil segment avoided due to unethical core-weight practices and low genuine margins
items.quote: strong one, one and a half month in this industry a food foil. We are more than willing to start with them, but then I didn't feel it a great thing. To be very frank I don’t find the industry very positive. The reason is there is heavy competition a nd second, sir, to be totally frank with you, these players play with the core that is in it like on a normal, when you buy a food foil, let's say it'

items.statement: Preferential allotment of ₹200 crore planned but delayed due to unfavorable market conditions
items.quote: Yes, the plan is in place, but the current market situation is not very favorable. So, strategically, we will wait for a bit before proceeding.

items.statement: Investing in a solar PV manufacturing company for backward integration; initial capacity 150-200 MW, scaling to 1 GW in two phases
items.quote: Our target is to disclose it in May, and its initial capacity is currently 150–200 megawatts. However, we are also planning to set up a new plant with the company, and then our capacity will increase to 1 gigawatts.

items.statement: Started work on solar cell manufacturing aligned with government plans for 2026-27
items.quote: And let me also tell you one more thing — we've already started working on the government's plans for 2026–27. That means we've also begun work on cell manufacturing for solar panels.

items.statement: H1 order book roughly ₹300-350 crore including 3-4 big orders worth ~₹100 crore and monthly run-rate ~₹100 crore
items.quote: Even if I talk roughly, we've executed 3 or 4 big orders, which are valued at around 100 crore. In addition to that, the monthly business we are doing doesn't require much effort, and that's around 100 crore. So, this means that the total is around 300-350 crore

items.statement: EV charging market guaranteed to grow but 40% of chargers not installed due to DISCOM infrastructure gaps causing payment delays
items.quote: The biggest problem in India right now is that DISCOMS do not have the infrastructure to provide power connections. Because of this, 40% of the chargers that were given are still not installed, and since they haven't been installed, the payments have been delayed.

items.statement: Solar distribution network doubled in last 6 months; monthly revenue increased from ₹7-8 crore to ₹20-25 crore
items.quote: In solar, we have started expanding our distribution and channels, and in the last 6 months, our network has approximately doubled. So, where we were doing business worth 7-8 crores per month, now we are reaching 20-25 crores in monthly revenue.

items.statement: Operational cost-effectiveness significantly improved profitability; inventory minimized, debtors controlled despite slight setback
items.quote: The operationally cost-effective approach has significantly improved profitability. We have minimized inventory, and what you see after the first quarter will look even better. Debtors have been well controlled, but the level of control we've had also had a bit of a setback

items.statement: Debtor cycle time increased slightly due to EV infrastructure issues; inventory minimized and debtors largely controlled
items.quote: Because of this, our debtor cycle time has increased slightly. However, we've made significant overall improvements, so it may not be very noticeable to you. But it has had quite an impact on other marketing companies

items.statement: Shifted focus from EV charging to solar to maintain steady growth amid EV infrastructure challenges
items.quote: To ensure this slowdown does not affect Servotech, we have shifted our focus towards solar. In solar, we have started expanding our distribution and channels

items.statement: EV infrastructure challenges impacting other marketing companies more severely than Servotech
items.quote: But it has had quite an impact on other marketing companies, and the EV charging infrastructure is also still facing challenges.

items.statement: Working on government plans for 2026-27 including solar cell manufacturing under policy push
items.quote: We've already started working on the government's plans for 2026–27. That means we've also begun work on cell manufacturing for solar panels.

items.statement: Appointed Errol Musk to advisory board for strategic and geographical expansion, networking and exposure
items.quote: He's a significant figure, as you are all fully aware of who he is and the exposure we'll gain as a company, as well as the networking opportunities we can create. We are working on that.

items.statement: Investing in a solar PV manufacturing company for backward integration; will disclose details upon conclusion
items.quote: In this process, we are investing in a solar PV manufacturing company, which will also lead to backward integration. This will enable us to cater to more people in a much better way.

items.statement: Signed agreement with France-based Watt & Well to develop and manufacture EV charger components in India
items.quote: Servotech Renewable has signed an agreement with France-based Watt & Well to develop and manufacture EV charger components in India.

items.statement: Launched user-friendly mobile app with CIMSME to accelerate 1 lakh solar homes target by 2026 under PM Surya Ghar Yojana
items.quote: Servotech & CIMSME launched user-friendly mobile app, accelerating 1 Lakh solar homes target by 2026 under PM Surya Ghar Yojana

items.statement: Granted patent for breakthrough peak shaving technology
items.quote: Servotech Renewable granted patent for breakthrough peak shaving technology.

items.statement: Implementing digital roadmap including SAP, Zoho CRM, AI-powered reporting, and IoT-based energy derivatives
items.quote: These insights highlight the fo rward- looking initiatives we’re already implementing, including the rollout of SAP and Zoho CRM systems, AI-powered reporting, and IoT-based energy derivatives

items.statement: K.V. Sridhar joined recently as Chief Financial Officer with rich experience and Board exposure
items.quote: K.V. Sridhar, just as an introduction, he has joined us recently as Chief Financial Officer. And he comes with a very, very rich experience, and he's dealt with Board, and he's been in the system with us for last few days.

items.statement: Management refuses to give volume growth guidance for RACs, says it depends on summer season
items.quote: But it will all depend on the summers. And it's very difficult to gi ve you any kind of guidance as to what kind of percentage growth we'll be able to

items.statement: Unseasonal rains and delayed summer onset hurt consumer sentiment and secondary sales in April
items.quote: There have been some unseasonal rains and thunderstorms in some part of the country and which has brought down the sentiment -- consumer sentiments.

items.statement: Projects segment carry-forward order book exceeds INR6,500 crores as of 31 March 2025
items.quote: As of 31st March '25, the total carry forward order book for the segment is in excess of INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: UCP segment margin around 9-10% range, RAC margin same as previous quarters
items.quote: And if you recollect my previous discussions with you also and the guidance which I had given you, it's been hovering around 9%, 10% all along in the UCP category.

items.statement: Better product mix in air coolers (larger capacity industrial coolers) and room ACs (higher energy-efficient 5-star units) improved profitability
items.quote: Like in air coolers, there is a better demand for the larger capacity industri al kind of coolers, which is more than 100, 120 liters, etcetera, and which is a slightly better margin fetching products

items.statement: Chennai RAC factory commercial production progressing as planned, further capacity scale-up planned at fully backward integrated Chennai facility
items.quote: With our proposed growth plans and vision of leading industry growth in the air conditioner market, we are planning to further scale up our capacity, especially at our fully backward integrated room air conditioner factory in Chennai.

items.statement: Commodity price increases and forex volatility remain challenges for UCP segment
items.quote: Overall, for UCP, increase in commodity prices and the volatility of foreign exchange continue to remain a challenge.

items.statement: No immediate price hike planned; evaluating demand, commodity and forex movements before decision
items.quote: Immediately, I'm not looking at any price hike to be honest. But as the situation demands, we will take appropriate action.

items.statement: Over 60-65 brands now competing in AC segment, making high market share difficult; aim to maintain leadership with reasonable gap to number 2
items.quote: There are more than 60, 65 brands which are fighting for getting this share into the pie. And therefore, it becomes very, very difficult to maintain a very high-level market share.

items.statement: Industry volume around 13-14 million units in FY25; double-digit industry growth expected but exact percentage depends on summer
items.quote: Industry has been hovering about around 13-14 million, approximately.

items.statement: Custom duty demand notice of ~INR25 crores received on copper tubes imported under FTA; evaluating and will respond suitably
items.quote: The notice -- demand notice was on copper as an element, if you're talking about what particular item was it.

items.statement: Domestic projects face collection challenges in certain projects; optimistic of recovery in subsequent quarters
items.quote: However, in domestic business, we face challenges in collections in certain projects. We are relatively optimistic of recovery in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Provision of ~INR40 crores made in Q4 for expected credit loss on international projects in GCC countries due to delayed payments
items.quote: About INR40-odd crores approximately.

items.statement: Commercial Refrigeration revenue grew ~19-20% in Q4 but profitability was marginal due to QCO stock liquidation and demand challenges
items.quote: And going forward, if you were talking about revenue for quarter 4 and we have grown by about overall 19%, 20% in the category, Commercial Refrigeration category. And profitability, we have not done well, to be honest, in this Commercial Refrigeration category.

items.statement: Chennai factory state incentives spread over 15 years; primary objective was proximity to Southern/Western markets to reduce transit time and transport cost
items.quote: Actually, there is a state benefit definitely there, which is going to come as we produce. But it is over a longer period, over the next 15 years, I think 15 years, we are going to get the dividends in -- from this factory.

items.statement: Voltas Beko volume grew 57% in FY25 vs industry single-digit growth; market share reached 8.7% in washing machines and 5.3% in refrigerators (YTD Feb 2025)
items.quote: During the financial year ended March 2025, the industry reported only single-digit growth in washing machines and negligible growth in refrigerators. However, Voltas Beko's performed remarkably well with a volume growth of 57%.

items.statement: Commercial AC and Commercial Refrigeration expected to grow more than double-digit in FY26
items.quote: Very difficult to say on the percentage growth. But yes, we will be -- it will be more than double-digit growth, yes.

items.statement: Global uncertainty from US tariffs, China slowdown, Indo-Pak tensions; global growth projected at 2.8% in 2025, 3% in 2026
items.quote: This will negatively impact economic activity with global growth now projected to drop to 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026, down from the earlier forecast of 3.3% in the earlier years.

items.statement: Strong summer season after 2-3 years drove 36% UCP volume growth and 30% revenue growth in FY25; highest ever 2.5M AC units sold
items.quote: For the year, all products in the air conditioner category experienced good demand, driven by consumers' preference for advanced features and energy-efficient products.

items.statement: UCP segment results grew 29% to INR892 crores in FY25, in line with 30% revenue growth; Q4 segment result INR345 crores vs INR270 crores YoY
items.quote: Overall, for UCP, increase in commodity prices and the volatility of foreign exchange continue to remain a challenge. Our planned consistent inv estments in advertising continued to deliver anticipated results

items.statement: Commercial AC has high order pipeline for retrofit jobs and positive conversion of product sales to AMC jobs
items.quote: With the positive conversion of product sales to AMC jobs and the high order pipeline to retrofit jobs, the vertical is expected to achieve consistent growth.

items.statement: Projects business beneficiary of large orders from group companies like Tata Electronics booked during FY25 for execution
items.quote: our group companies where a lot of new businesses are coming up, Tata Electronics and all, where we have got -- we are beneficiary of large orders booked during the year, which are going to get executed

items.statement: Voltas Beko became second largest in semi-automatic washing machines with 15.3% market share YTD Feb 2025
items.quote: We are delighted to share that our performance in semi-automatic washing machines exceeded the expectations, making us the second largest player in the product category with a year-to-date market share of 15.3%.

items.statement: Voltas Beko aims to localize all refrigerator manufacturing in India to become fully made-in-India brand
items.quote: Leveraging our manufacturing progress, we aim to localize all refrigerator manufacturing in India and become a fully made in India brand.

items.statement: Other income jumped due to interest and mark-to-market gains on investments; other operating income includes PLI-linked incentive accrual
items.quote: This is largely the interest and mark-to-market income on our investments in other income. And this year, it has paid us good dividends. And in other operating income we have accrued PLI linked incentive.

items.statement: PLI incentive included in divisional results but investment income kept unallocated, not in UCP margins
items.quote: While PLI linked incentive is part of divisional results, we don't take investment income it in the divisional margins. This is unallocated -- we show it as unallocated earnings.

items.statement: Gross direct premium grew 1.5x industry on 1/N GDPI basis and 1.6x on full GDPI basis
items.quote: The company ended the year with a gross direct premium of INR8,124 crores and gross written premium of INR8,328 crores, which meant that the company grew at about 1.5x of industry growth on 1/N GDPI basis and 1.6x on full GDPI basis.

items.statement: Combined ratio without 1/N effect improved to 107.85% from 109.9%
items.quote: The full year combined ratio without by 1/N effect was at 107.85 as against 109.9 in the corresponding period.

items.statement: Claims ratio improved to 73.3% from 73.7%
items.quote: The claims ratio for the year stood at 73.3%, lower than the 73.7% in the previous year.

items.statement: Expense of management ratio at 33.14% on 1/N basis and 32.18% without 1/N, below board-approved glide path
items.quote: The expense of management of Chola MS for the year stood at 33.14, which measured without by 1/ N works out to 32.18% and is lower than the glide path approved by the Board way back and presented to the regulator.

items.statement: Return on equity reached 18.5% on average net worth
items.quote: The return on equity on average net worth progressed to 18.5%.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 2.18x as at March 2025
items.quote: The solvency ratio of the company at 2.18x as at March is comfortable.

items.statement: Regulator has not yet called Chola MS for listing discussion; board will decide when turn comes
items.quote: Chola MS was not one of the companies that the regulator had called for a discussion, which I suppose they are first looking at the even larger players at this point in time, and our turn would come in due course, perhaps when the new IRDA Chairman comes and later on as the case may be. The Board of the holding company will take an appropriate call.

items.statement: EOM glide path compliance targeted for FY26; industry seeking regulator clarity on 1/N vs cash basis for long-term products
items.quote: FY 25- 26 is the last year of the glide path. So where we need to achieve that 1.5%, which you are talking about, that all depends on the additional allowances towards insurtech and the rural obligation part. But we are on the path to achieve that glide path level for FY 25- 26.

items.statement: Motor mix: 42% cars, 43% commercial vehicles, 15% two-wheelers; 27% motor premium from new vehicles
items.quote: In motor, the principal line of business, the market share stood at 5.5%. Within motor, the company has a composition of 42% in cars, 43% in commercial vehicles and 15% in 2-wheelers. The company secured about 27% of its total motor premium from new vehicles.

items.statement: Motor OD share increased to 42.7% from 40.6%; Q4 motor OD loss ratio fell to 72.5% from 75.4%
items.quote: If you are to look at even our OD -TP mix, actually, this year, it's almost -- it's moved to about 42.7% of OD. The previous year, it was 40.6%. So there is a 2.1% shift that has happened towards OD in the current year. And in that context, you read the claims ratio of our company in Q4, actually, you will find that it is 72.5% and come down from 75.4% in the previous year.

items.statement: Technology spend increased to INR117 crores from INR91 crores for digital capabilities
items.quote: During the year, in pursuant to its direction on augmenting digital capabilities, the company spent INR117 crores towards technology spend as against INR91 crores in corresponding period.

items.statement: Investment corpus crossed INR18,000 crores; Q4 investment recovery of INR54 crores from Reliance Capital and IL&FS write-offs
items.quote: The investment corpus crossed the INR18,000 crore mark. And in Q4, the company had the benefit of recoveries of INR54 crores from written-off investments in earlier years.

items.statement: PBT at INR195 crores in Q4 and INR680 crores for full year including INR54 crores one-time investment recovery
items.quote: The PBT in the quarter and full year were at INR195 crores and INR680 crores, respectively, which includes this onetime income of INR54 crores.

items.statement: Net worth neared INR3,000 crores with 85% from earned profits
items.quote: The net worth of Chola MS nudged the INR3,000 cror e mark. And as you are aware, 85% of this net worth is by way of earned profits over the years.

items.statement: Board cognizant of holding company discount; will evaluate listing path for subsidiaries at appropriate time
items.quote: I think you've asked the question , as well as you have answered that also. But I think we will definitely look at it. As Sury said, the Board is cognizant of this fact. And there is a path most of the companies have to travel towards listing. So we'll have to wait and see, and we'll come back to you at an appropriate time.

items.statement: Fire business poised to grow with additional reinsurance capacity and higher net worth enabling greater retention
items.quote: Certainly, our fire business is poised to grow from the levels that it is currently in. And in the current year, the company has also secured additional reinsurance capacities. And therefore, we will be in a position to write larger shares. It's also a fact that our net worth has been growing, and therefore, the retention levels towards the property risk is also poised to go up. So we should be st

items.statement: Technology modernization program underway including legacy ERP transition and digitization for channel efficiency
items.quote: the company has been working on its tech development program, so which is operating on multiple fronts. One is the transition from the legacy ERP system where there is progress. The second is the effort and tech spend that is happening on the digitization spend, which is more for modernizing and also to realize the efficiencies in transacting and also c onvenience in transacting for channel partne

items.statement: FY25 asset growth guidance 11-13%; actual 12.8% global, 13.7% domestic
items.quote: As you can see from the asset side, we have given a guidance of growth of 11 to 13% and our asset has grown by 12.8%.

items.statement: FY25 deposit growth guidance 9-11%; actual 10.3% global, 9.3% domestic
items.quote: Coming to the deposit side, our guidance was 9 to 11% growth and happy to say that the total global deposit has grown by 10.3% with international 15.8 and domestic 9.3.

items.statement: FY25 slippage ratio guidance 1-1.15%; actual 0.78%
items.quote: If I take the total slippage ratio, it has gone down from 0.99 to 0.78 and the slippage ratio, our guidance was 1 to 1.15 and we are well within that limit.

items.statement: FY25 credit cost guidance 0.75%; actual 0.47%
items.quote: Credit cost similarly, we have given a guidance of 0.75. However, we are closing our credit cost at 0.47.

items.statement: FY25 NIM guidance revised to 3.05% +/- 5 bps; full-year NIM 3.02%
items.quote: Earlier, the guidance was 3.10 plus minus 5 bps. We revised that to 3.05 plus minus 5 bps.

items.statement: FY26 deposit growth guidance 9-11%; loan growth guidance 11-13%
items.quote: As of today, I'm holding my guidance of 9 to 11 on the deposit, 11 to 13 on the advances with an understanding that if the liquidity prevails the surplus liquidity, possibly we are going to upsize both the guidances.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 global NIM 2.86%, full-year NIM 3.02%; domestic NIM 3.18%
items.quote: Our margin, yield and advances is a little bit down from 8.53 to 8.39 with the obvious reason of easing out of the interest and cost of the deposit is at a little bit on a higher scale. So as a result, our quarterly NIM has declined from 2.94 to 2.86.

items.statement: Expect NIM pressure in Q1 FY26; recovery from Q2, better in Q3-Q4; full-year FY26 NIM at least FY25 level
items.quote: So, we are expecting a much better NIM somewhere in maybe to some extent in Q2, but Q3, Q2, Q4 would be definitely much better. And my sense as on today, although I am not giving a full year guidance, my sense as on today that on a full year basis, all the banks, including us would be able to maintain the NIM margin that we achieved in the previous year, at least.

items.statement: GNPA 2.26%, NNPA 0.58%, PCR 93.29%, slippage ratio 0.78%, credit cost 0.47%, collection efficiency 98.5%
items.quote: Asset quality is a key for us and we never compromise on the asset quality with gross NPA trending down from 2.92 to 2.26. Net NPA similarly is trending down from 0.68 to 0.58. Provision coverage ratio is 93.29%, which is healthy in itself.

items.statement: FY25 slippages lower than FY24; FY25 recoveries higher than FY24; FY25 recoveries exceed slippages
items.quote: The slippage of this year is lower than that of the slippage last year. The recovery of this year is higher than the recovery that of last year. And within the same year, that means 24-25, the recovery is higher than that of the slippage.

items.statement: CASA ratio 39.97% domestic; CASA growth 6.4% YoY
items.quote: Similarly, our CD ratio is maintained at a stable rate of 83.59% and domestic CASA, as we always said, will be maintaining at 40% and it is at 39.97%.

items.statement: CRAR 17.19%, Tier-1 14.79%, LCR 123%; target LCR ~120%
items.quote: The bank enjoys a strong capital base of 17.19% CRAR with tier 1 ranging to 14.79%. And also, we are having a healthy LCR of 123%.

items.statement: Retail advances grew 19.4% (home 17%, mortgage 19%, auto 20%, education 16%, personal loans moderated to 21%)
items.quote: In the retail also, each and every segment has shown a very strong growth with education growing at around 16%, home loan 17%, mortgage 19% and auto loan at 20%.

items.statement: Agri & MSME advances grew 14.2%; corporate advances grew 8.6%
items.quote: Agriculture and MSME has shown a very potential growth of 14.2% and corporate is at 8.6%.

items.statement: Corporate credit demand exists; bank moderating growth to protect margin and avoid fine-priced assets
items.quote: The demand for the corporate credit is there in the market and suppose you want to grow higher, we can very well grow higher. But then again, on a margin sake, we are not trying to get into the fine priced asset in a big way putting the margin under pressure.

items.statement: EBLR loans repriced T+1 after repo cut via ALCO
items.quote: It's actually, in fact, automatic, but then the ALCO is the competent pricing. So, the moment there is a repo cut next day, we have the ALCO to announce. That's why it is T+1, right.

items.statement: Raised infra bonds and other borrowings to manage LCR and funding
items.quote: We also rely on borrowing wherever the funds are available at a cheaper funds, then we go there, we raise infra bonds and others last time.

items.statement: Dividend recommended at Rs 8.35 per share (face value Rs 2) for FY25
items.quote: The board has recommended for a dividend of 8.35 per share with a face value of two for the financial year 24 - 25, subject to approval by the competent authorities.

items.statement: Family pension amortization continued (Rs 290 cr remaining); RBI dispensation ends FY26
items.quote: In any case, that dispensation is going to be over in the current year itself.

items.statement: NIM pressure in Q1 FY26 due to deposit repricing lag; asset yield compression immediate
items.quote: Immediate Q1 would be slightly a challenge because, I mean, in our kind of market scenario, it is an inflection point in terms of the rate stance change between Q1 over Q4 or the liquidity changing between Q1 over Q4.

items.statement: MSME slippages up slightly QoQ but ratio contained; driven by select geographies and aging accounts
items.quote: This 300, 400, 500 crore of MSME, this normally happens based on a selected geography, some of the aging account of which there is a weakness. So, it's no way impacting the overall slippage ratio, the overall slippage ratio is contained

items.statement: Treasury income up ~Rs 600 cr YoY; expect similar run-rate in FY26 given rate outlook
items.quote: The treasury income has been better this year as compared to last year, almost by 600 crore. And going by the current market condition on the bond market or the rate side, I believe this year also going to be a good year for treasury.

items.statement: TWO recovery run-rate Rs 750-800 cr; FY25 included one-off; expect similar normalized + one-off in FY26
items.quote: Our normal run rate earlier also we said, it is almost like 750 to 800 crore. And every year we see there is a one off coming out of NCLT resolution or some other account. So last year also we had one off. FY23, 24 also we had one off. So, with a run rate of around 750, 800 crore, I think again this year going to be a one off, putting our recovery almost at the same level like last year.

items.statement: SR revaluation write-back ~Rs 450 cr in FY25; expect further write-backs as yields fall
items.quote: There was a write back of almost 500 crore last year and there is a write back of almost 450 crore this year on the depreciation front. And going by the rate cycle, I think that again would be a write back going forward because the yields are going down.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio below 48%
items.quote: Cost to income, I think at below 48 is one of the best in terms of the way we look into the market and cost to income over the banks.

items.statement: Target RAM share of 66% in 3 years by adding ~200 bps annually; corporate loan growth to continue at 10%+; RAM growth ~15%
items.quote: Considering the segment wise growth guidance we are giving, we continue to have the same journey, maybe in 3 years' time by adding 200 bps every year we want to achieve 66% in fact.

items.statement: Credit spreads can only be reset at renewal (typically after 3 years) based on internal/external rating deterioration; not a uniform policy
items.value: spread reset at renewal after 3 years
items.quote: For spread resetting, there is a guideline by the regulator and it happens after 3 years only and there are large number of accounts where spread change have happened only at the time of renewal.

items.statement: No savings account rate cut planned despite rate cycle; only 5 bps increase in many years; focus on service and bundling
items.quote: See, I have not increased during the rise. So, why should I reduce during the fall? Actually, there is no case for that.

items.statement: Corporate book Rs 4.11 lakh crore (domestic) + Rs 2 lakh crore (international) = Rs 6 lakh crore total; among largest in PSBs
items.quote: I mean, my corporate book is 4,11,000 crore as in March. In December, it was less and on the international I am running a corporate book of almost 2,00,000 crore. 6,00,000 crore is the corporate book that we run.

items.statement: MSME NPA ~7.5% vs 17% in 2021; lowest among peers; focus on CV/CME, supply chain finance, cash-flow lending; new MSME definition to bring mid-corporate accounts into MSME
items.quote: As far as the NPA as a whole is concerned, I think Bank of Baroda's MSME book is a quality book and we are having below 8% of the NPAs, around 7.5% NPA in MSME book, as compared to 17% which had been in 2021.

items.statement: Renewable energy exposure Rs 18,547 crore; MoUs with IREDA, REC, state governments for co-origination (non-binding, full appraisal required)
items.quote: We have a MoU with IREDA, we entered with MoU with IREDA for the solar I think proposals and this thing. So, and where our exposure is 18,547 crore total in the renewable energy.

items.statement: Loan mix: 34-35% repo-linked, 45-48% MCLR-linked, fixed rate low single digit
items.value: 34-35% repo; 45-48% MCLR; fixed low single digit
items.quote: Our repo link book is 34-35%, MCLR link book is anywhere between 45 to 48% plus minus 2 percentage point, fixed rate is not very large in a very low single digit percentage.

items.statement: CASA grew ~6.5% overall; retail CASA grew ~5%; 76% retail CASA, 24% institutional; CASA rate unchanged (only 5 bps increase in cycle)

items.statement: Q4 FY25 pre-sales INR217 crores (+11% YoY), area sold 70,000 sq ft (+9% YoY)

items.quote: So, if you notice, sir, our margins are more than what is there in the industry average. So -- and because you are a brand, you are able to get premium and because you are getting premium, you are able to make healthy margins. All

items.quote: Also, once you get an LOI, then we need to close the development agreement and opt-in approval, which also takes, on an average, a year after which the society vacates.

items.statement: Land acquisition process takes ~1 year from handshake to closure for both greenfield and redevelopment
items.quote: Normally, once the handshake happens, it takes, on an average, maybe around a year to close the transaction. This is the due diligence and the title search and all the processes involved, the CPs of the condition precedence for the transaction.

items.statement: No projects stalled; all approvals progressing smoothly; Malad project targeting launch in Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, first part to your question is that none of our project is stalled. Forget Malad, none of our project is stalled just for your information. And everything is in smoothly process of approval and we are -- I have mentioned it that we target to launch also this year Malad project.

items.statement: Management focused only on MMR region; no plans for Pune, Bangalore or other cities

items.statement: Aspiring to grow faster than industry CAGR of 15-22% but no specific order book numbers given for FY26/FY27
items.quote: I cannot go with the numbers, but I can give you the assurance that we'll be doing a great job in this year also, because we are having so many opportunities and industry is going so fast and we are having entry barrier at very good level.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 795 bps to 18% in FY25; management aims to maintain current margin levels
items.quote: EBITDA increased to 267% year-on-year to INR 25 cro res, with margins improving 795 basis points to 18

items.statement: Selective tender quoting to protect margins; will not quote projects where margins cannot be secured

We q uote only selective tenders where we find that we'll be in a comfortable position to quote, and we can secure our margins and whatever the expenses are there

items.statement: Government healthcare spending INR98,000 crores in FY25; medical equipment market projected to grow from $11B to $50B by 2030
items.quote: The government has significantly stepped-up invest ments, allocating INR98,000 crores in FY '25 alone, with a special focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Meanwhile, India's medical equipment industry is experiencing unprecedented growth. The m arket was valued at $11 billion in 2022, and is projected to grow to $50 billion by 2030

items.statement: Proprietary products (EP lab, mobile CT, mobile stroke unit, robotic surgery) drive higher margins; 70-75% of turnkey revenue from proprietary products

items.quote: In August 2024, we raised INR29.2 crores through o ur IPO, which is now being used to strengthen working capital and support

items.quote: Basically if you see this INR60 crores order book almost 60% to 70% is from Maharashtra. 10% to 20% you can count from Rajasthan and rest is from Gujarat. This is more turnkey. Trading is somewhat lesser in this INR60 crores.

So I cannot comment on that. But so many companies, they are approaching. And

items.quote: Right now we have orders of almost Rs. 537 crores out of that almost Rs. 450 crores is the target till December 2026 some of the portion also comes from Orion and the contract timeline for that is three year and five years and the orders is for Rs. 110 crore.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target set at Rs. 275-300 crore
items.quote: The turnover target for this year is between Rs. 275 crore to Rs. 300 crore and let us see how much we will achieve.

items.quote: We are trying not to go below 18 but we are trying to increase it more as compared to the last year which was 21%.

items.quote: CAPEX is around Rs. 10 crore, we have CAPEX of Rs. 3 crore. The shed has been built.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow due to government payment terms (60% on supply, 20% on erection, 10% on commissioning, 10% on reconciliation); QIP Rs. 25 crore deployed to working capital
items.quote: We have done QIP now. With this, we will try to make the cash flow positive. We have done QIP that is why. We have raised Rs. 25 crore through QIP.

items.statement: Rajasthan pipeline strong: Rs. 2,000-3,000 crore transmission tenders expected in next year; company bidding Rs. 500-700 crore in next 6 months
items.quote: Tenders worth Rs.2000 crore, Rs. 3000 crore are yet to come in Rajasthan in the next one year only for transmission lines.

items.quote: We get a benefit of 5%- 7% because of being in Rajasthan in terms of the cost of the tender. We are comfortable in that. We have our own CMP and TAC, we do not have to pay rent that cost is also

items.quote: Non-fund is Rs. 25 crores and Rs. 2.5 crore is with Kotak. Rs. 27.5 crore is non-fund based.

items.statement: QIP of Rs. 25 crore completed at Rs. 198/share; further fund raise possible depending on contract wins, no immediate plans
items.quote: We have raised Rs. 25 crore through QIP.

items.quote: We will start manufacturing before March'26 because CAPEX has been done, we have invested more than Rs. 3 crores.

items.statement: >90% work in Rajasthan (35% of India's renewable capacity); also small projects in Haryana, UP, Railway (Balaghat, Kerala); Jost's Engineering JV (Rs. 115 crore in order book)
items.quote: More than 90% of our work is in Rajasthan. Tender is also coming and cutting also happens becaus e of being located in Rajasthan

items.statement: Order inflow success rate >70%; quoted Rs. 180 crore tenders in last 10 days (technical bid opened, price bid pending)
items.quote: Around Rs. 800 crore, Rs. 900 crore, our success rate is more than 70%.

items.statement: Geographic concentration risk acknowledged (90% Rajasthan); management says renewable pipeline ensures sustained demand, working with large players like Adani/KEC
items.quote: There is a lot of work in renewables in Rajasthan regularly. Big players are also coming in like Adani and KEC.

items.statement: Backward integration expected to improve PAT margin by 2-3% once operational (target Q4 FY26)
items.quote: Margin improvement will be on a net basis, around 2% to 3%.

items.quote: We will complete this but order book must be around Rs. 750 crore next year.

items.quote: July-August. IT will come back in July -August. By July -August retention will move to other possessions.
