items.statement: Volume guidance for FY2026 is roughly 1.5 million tons of additional deliveries, mostly in India, with UK flat and Netherlands slightly higher.
items.quote: The volume guidance is roughly 1.5 million tons of additional deliveries. Most of it is in India because UK will be flat, Netherlands will be slightly higher.

items.statement: Coking coal consumption cost expected to be about $10 per ton lower in 1QFY26 for both Europe and India.
items.quote: For coking coal, the guidance is that it will be about $10 per ton lower on a consumption basis, though the coking coal prices have gone up in the last few weeks but on a consumption basis, will be $10 per ton better, both in Europe and India.

items.statement: Iron ore consumption cost in Netherlands expected to be about $10 per ton higher in 1QFY26.
items.quote: Iron ore is relevant only for Europe, specifically for Netherlands, because we've shut the blast furnaces in the UK. Iron ore is expected to be about $10 per ton higher in Netherlands consumption.

items.statement: FY2026 capex guided at Rs. 15,000 crores, focused on raw materials, Kalinganagar completion, and Ludhiana plant (~0.8-1 MTPA).
items.quote: I believe FY 2026 capex guided is Rs. 15,000 crores, which I understand doesn't include any planned new expansion projects in India.

items.statement: Kalinganagar to finish this year at close to 7 million tons (6.8 Mt steel, 7.5 Mt hot metal); full ramp-up and Ludhiana volumes visible next year.
items.quote: This year, we will finish Kalinganagar at close to 7 million tons; 6.8 million tons of steel and 7.5 million tons of hot metal. By next year, we will have a ramp-up because the steel melt shop will be complete.

items.statement: Kalinganagar next phase and Bhushan expansion from 5 to 6.5 MTPA to follow Neelachal; first phase of Neelachal to finish by FY2030-31, not full 35-40 MTPA target by FY2030.
items.quote: What we expect to have by FY2030 is all these projects at different stages. Hopefully, we start the Neelachal project now. At least the first phase will finish, and we can start the other two, which will be a t different degrees of finishing in FY2030 - 31. Yes, we will not have completed capacity by FY30

items.statement: Netherlands EBITDA target €70-80 per ton, aiming eventually for €100 per ton; UK targeting EBITDA neutral/positive on underlying basis by FY2027-28.
items.quote: €70 - 80 per ton is what we are seeing in Netherlands, we will move towards. Eventually, yes, we should be aiming towards €100 per ton but €70 - 80 per ton is what we have basically said we should be chasing. In UK, all things remaining same, just through the cost takeouts etc. we should be EBITDA neutral or EBITDA positive.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin 20-22% in down cycle, 25-28% in medium cycle, 38-40% in up cycle; targeting Rs. 14,000 EBITDA per ton despite lower steel prices ($450-500/t).
items.quote: Maybe 8 - 10 years back, we used to look at $600 per ton as the all-weather steel price and Rs. 14,000 as the all -weather EBITDA per ton . Today, if we cross $500 per ton, we are happy . But we have not changed the EBITDA per ton of Rs. 14,000 per ton , that we always chase.

items.statement: Rs. 4,000 crore cost savings target for India operations in FY2026, focused on conversion costs (stores, repairs, maintenance, fixed cost, vendor development, digital procurement, wage bill reduction).
items.quote: Broadly, this is not just Jamshedpur. This is India operations. When we say Rs. 4,000 crores, there is a lot which we are doing through, for instance, optimi sation of our contracts because we have multiple sites now

items.statement: Netherlands carbon cost impact close to €80 million per year due to reducing allowances and CO2 levy; UK carbon impact zero until EAF starts in FY2027-28.
items.quote: As far as Netherlands is concerned, there is a deficit that happened until last year. It will gradually converge, but there is an increased cost on account of carbon, and that is happening because of the fact that the allowances are reducing, and there is also a CO 2 levy that has been coming in as far as the Netherlands is concerned. So, it is close to about €80 million a year.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt reduced from Rs. 88,000 crores (Sept 2024) to Rs. 82,570 crores; deleveraging to continue in FY2026 while investing in growth.
items.quote: In September 2024, at the peak of the downturn, we were at about Rs. 88,000 crores consolidated net debt. Now, we are at about Rs. 82,570 crores. We've reduced more than Rs. 6,000 crores of debt across entities and geographies in the last six months. We will continue this pathway into FY2026.

items.statement: $2.5 billion infusion is debt rebalancing (not equity), moving overseas debt to India balance sheet; Netherlands near net debt-free, UK to become self-sustaining, Singapore bonds to be repaid by 2028.
items.quote: Not equity. I said that in the beginning that it is not an equity investment, it's rebalancing of debt. We are not putting new money in for new investments or new assets or even for any other purposes, it's essentially putting in money to take that debt out and putting it under the India balance sheet.

items.statement: Safeguard duty of 12% in place (industry asked for 25%); will go back to government if Chinese imports flood; EU-US trade deal needed for Netherlands exports to US.
items.quote: The guidance that I gave is based on things as they stand today on the safeguard duty, which is already there in India and what we've experienced so far in this quarter and what we think we'll experience in the next six weeks.

items.statement: Chinese exports 10 million tons in March-April; concern if US-China tariff deal not reached; Chinese exports diverting to Middle East/Africa reducing pressure on India/SE Asia.
items.quote: We are a bit concerned about the 10 million tons of exports, which continues out of China in March and April that happened and we are expecting that, that number should come down.

items.statement: Long products currently more profitable than flats in India due to Chinese flat exports depressing flat prices; long products 50% supplied by secondary sector with different cost structures.
items.quote: Currently, long product prices are higher in India than flat product prices on a commercial grade basis because most of the 100 million tons of steel China is exporting are flat products, which has depressed inte rnational flat product prices

items.statement: Risk of Chinese import surge if US-China tariff deal fails; private sector capex (Rs. 15,000 crore) needs financially healthy industry; India capacity build limited by land/approval processes.
items.quote: If we, again, see a flood of Chinese imports , we will certainly go back to the government and see what can be done because the private sector investment in India , in some sense , is being led by the steel industry.

items.statement: Net finance cost FY2024 ~Rs. 6,700 crores, FY2025 ~Rs. 6,300 crores; onshoring debt may increase headline cost but lowers effective post-tax cost.
items.quote: The net finance cost for FY2024 was ~Rs. 6,700 crores, and the net finance cost for FY 2025 is ~Rs. 6,300 crores. So, I didn't see any increase in interest costs.

items.statement: Rs. 533 crore exceptional charge for ~1,100 people leaving last quarter; wage bill reduction in Jamshedpur as older workers retire.
items.quote: In fact, we have taken Rs. 533 odd crores of exceptional charge, which is last quarter we had about 1,100 people leaving the company. There is a people reduction cost.

items.statement: UK EAF project £750 million capex committed, spend over next three years; UK to be ready for FY2027-28 with structural change to scrap-based EAF.
items.quote: As far as capex is concerned, we're committed to about £750 million. That has not started yet in a meaningful way. That spend will happen in the future over the next three years.

items.statement: India steel capacity build limited by land acquisition, approvals, public hearings; cannot match China's 50 Mt/year peak; 15-20 Mt/year realistic with 6-8% GDP growth driving 8-10% steel demand growth.
items.quote: Honestly, I don't think so because it's not easy to build steel plants in India. It takes time, assuming you have land. If you are going to start a greenfield site, it takes even longer time. India will never be able to build capacity as fast as China did.

items.statement: Targets 20% year-on-year revenue growth trajectory to meet Pinnacle 345 aspirations by FY30
items.quote: So, at this stage, we are hopeful that we will be able to maintain a 20% year-on-year growth trajectory to meet our Pinnacle 345 aspirations by FY30, at the overall company level.

items.statement: Expects Specialty and Nutrition segments to grow 15-20% year-on-year in coming years
items.quote: So, we are pretty sure that we will be able to maintain almost 15% to 20% growth in these two segments on a year-on-year basis in the coming years, which is very critical to meet our Pinnacle 345 Vision.

items.statement: Plans Rs.600 crore CAPEX in FY26 including spillover from FY25, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead in FY26, we plan to invest Rs.600 crore of additional CAPEX, including some spillover from FY25, which will be largely funded through internal accrual.

items.statement: Targets Rs.100-150 crore incremental cost savings in Phase-II optimization program, mostly in FY26
items.quote: We have now launched Phase-II of our cost optimization program aiming to achieve even higher efficiencies of Rs.100 crore to Rs.150 crore in the coming quarters, thereby further improving our margin.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA growth to outpace revenue growth in FY26 due to portfolio shift and savings
items.quote: EBITDA growth will definitely outpace the growth in revenue predominantly because of the portfolio shift as well as the savings initiatives.

items.statement: Invested Rs.1,745 crore over last three years out of announced Rs.2,000 crore CAPEX plan from FY22
items.quote: To achieve our goals, we have invested Rs.1,745 crore in the last three years out of the announced CAPEX plans of Rs.2,000 crore in FY22.

items.statement: FY25 capital expenditure was Rs.365 crore, primarily funded through internal accruals
items.quote: The capital expenditure incurred during the quarter was Rs.65 crore and Rs.365 crore for the completed financial year, which was primarily funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Plans Rs.600-800 crore annual CAPEX for next 3-4 years to achieve organic Pinnacle 345 targets
items.quote: Over the next 3-4 years, we'll need at least Rs.600 crore to Rs.800 crore of investment every year, to achieve the organic part of that Pinnacle 345 Vision that we have crafted, which means if you take the four years, anywhere between Rs.2,000-2,500 crore of additional investment.

items.statement: cGMP Niacinamide plant at Bharuch commissioned in January with 4,500 tons capacity, targeting 70-80% utilization in 18 months
items.quote: The total capacity is about 4,500 tons. We are hoping that in the next 18 months we will be able to get to 70%, 80% utilization levels.

items.statement: Agro CDMO plant commissioning targeted by end of calendar year, supplies starting by January 2026
items.quote: Yes, the big one we are hoping to commission the plan by end of this calendar year and start the supplies to the customers latest by January, hopefully sooner than that.

items.statement: Added 25-plus new molecules in CDMO funnel in FY25 across pharma, agrochemical and semiconductor
items.quote: In our CDMO business we added 25-plus new molecules in our funnel in FY25 across pharma, agrochemical and semiconductor, thus creating new growth vectors which we hope to scale up in coming quarters and years.

items.statement: Two commercial agro CDMO projects announced, one supplying from current quarter, other by January 2026
items.quote: And we had also announced the second one for which the supplies will go starting this quarter itself.

items.statement: Nutrition EBITDA margin at 14% for FY25, 16% in Q4; steady state target 16-18% on current assets
items.quote: And if you look at last quarter or let's say FY25 overall, we are at 14% while last quarter is at 16%. So, we are close to where it should be based on the existing set of assets.

items.statement: Targets Specialty Chemicals margin 22%+ (closer to 25% with scale), Nutrition 16-18%, Chemical Intermediates 10-12% long-term average
items.quote: I think for the Specialty Chemicals with everything we are doing and we have said that in the past also 22%-plus margin is visible, hopefully more close to 25% as we build out scale and continue to work on our cost initiatives. items.quote: But at a company level, what we are working towards as we announced in our Pinnacle 345 strategy also is more than 17%, 18% plus margin across the three segments put together.

items.statement: Agrochemical volumes rebounding with stabilized pricing after inventory destocking easing
items.quote: In the Agrochemicals sector, the global inventory destocking issues have eased, leading to a gradual rebound in agrochemical volumes and stabilized pricing.

items.quote: If I look at the Specialty Chemicals segment, obviously, prices have come down across segments as we have been sharing in the last few quarters, but we think they have bottomed out now and for the last six months or eight months also the prices by and large speaking have been stable.

items.quote: On the Chemical Intermediates, as I explained to the very first question, we are at the bottom of the cycle or very close to that. We are hopeful that pricing will start to go up gradually in next quarter or so based on at least whatever we are hearing from our customers.

items.statement: Niacinamide feed grade stable long-term; cosmetic/food grade higher value with potential marginal price increases
items.quote: On the Nutrition and Health Solutions segment, the feed segment of B3 will remain stable. items.quote: the narrow-aisle aircraft, they're already producing now 3 2 -- at a rate of 32 plus, and they are moving towards 38 aircraft. So we can already see the pull and those reflect in the numbers of the last quarter.

items.statement: Auto ancillary domestic market robust but export markets subdued due to European slowdown and Red Sea crisis

However, export markets remained subdued for auto ancillary and engineering consumables segments, primarily due to ongoing slowdown in the European automotive market and the disruptions caused by the Red Sea shipping crisis.

items.statement: JDA peak funding requirement ranges INR250-400 crores per project at 8-9.25% interest rates
items.quote: On an average, the peak funding requirement ranges between INR250 crores to INR350 crores maximum going up to INR400 crores. Depending on project to project, it can be different. But that's the range, between INR250 crores and INR400 crores.

items.statement: Raymond Limited net cash surplus INR263 crores with gross debt INR677 crores and cash INR940 crores
items.quote: We continue to remain a net debt-free business with a net cash surplus of INR263 crores in the March 2025. The total gross debt stands at INR677 crores and have cash and cash equivalents of INR940 crores as on 31st of March 2025.

items.statement: Real Estate business net cash surplus close to INR400 crores in March 2025
items.quote: We continue to remain a net debt -free business in the Real Estate as well, with a net cash surplus of close to INR400 crores in March 2025.

items.statement: Real Estate demerger effective May 1 2025, listing expected in Q2 FY26 with 1:1 share allotment
items.quote: The scheme has become effective from the 1st of May 2025, and the record date is 14th of May 2025 for the purpose of determining the eligible shareholders of demerged company, Raymond's Limited, to whom the equity shares of the resulting company, Raymond Realty Limited, would be allotted in terms of the scheme.

items.statement: Engineering restructuring scheme filed with NCLT to create separate aerospace/defense and auto components subsidiaries
items.quote: Currently, we have filed the restructuring scheme with the NCLT for the Engineering business and awaiting the final approval.

items.statement: JDA launch timeline 12-24 months from appointment to market launch depending on project type
items.quote: So that's the range typically, from 12 months to 24 months, for each JDA from the time you get appointed and to the market launch.

items.statement: Real Estate launches scheduled for Q3-Q4 FY26 with possible Thane launch in Q2, none in Q1
items.quote: So in the current year, you will see a few launc hes from us, but they will all be in Q3 and Q4. You may see in Q2 some launch in Thane. But Q1, we haven't scheduled any launch

items.statement: Real Estate prices firming up healthily but not running away, supply not keeping pace with demand
items.quote: the supply has only been going down in the market as the absorption has been increasing. So the number of launches have not really been able to keep pace with the demand, which has been in the market. So -- and that's why last 2 years, you've also seen the prices also firming up a little bit.

items.statement: Supreme Court environment approval case near Sanjay Gandhi National Park delaying some MMR project approvals
items.quote: For instance, there is a Supreme Court case going on for the environment approval just now. So some of the projects who get impacted by that, if they are within a certain vicinity of an eco -sensitive zone, and Bombay also gets impacted with that because Sanjay Gandhi National Park is right in the heart of the city.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-like situation caused temporary dip in Real Estate footfalls for one week
items.quote: In April and May so far, it's business as usual. Like barring the last 1 week, we saw some dip in the falls. I guess there was -- that was more to do with the fear and the uncertainty, because of the war-like situation, which got created.

items.statement: Real Estate revenue grew 13% YoY to INR766 crores in Q4 FY25
items.quote: that has resulted in a revenue of INR766 crores in the fourth quarter of fiscal '25 vis-a-vis INR677 crores in the fourth quarter of fiscal '24, recording a growth of 13%.

items.statement: Engineering sales INR528 crores and EBITDA INR81 crores in Q4 FY25 including Maini Precision
items.quote: the Engineering business, which includes the MPPL, Maini Precision business, reported a sales of INR528 crores and EBITDA of INR81 crores, with a margin of 15.3% in the fourth quarter of fiscal '25

items.statement: Raymond Limited continuing operations total income INR601 crores, EBITDA INR99 crores at 16.4% margin in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Raymond Limited delivered a strong quarterly performance, reporting a total income of INR601 crores with a delivery of an EBITDA of INR99 crores, with margin of 16.4% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.

items.statement: Raymond Limited full year FY25 total income INR2,105 crores, EBITDA INR335 crores at 15.9% margin
items.quote: The total income for the year was INR2,105 crores and delivering an EBITDA of INR335 crores, and EBITDA margin of 15.9% in the fiscal 2025.

items.statement: Engineering export markets subdued due to European automotive slowdown and Red Sea shipping disruptions
items.quote: export markets remained subdued for auto ancillary and engineering consumables segments, primarily due to ongoing slowdown in the European automotive market and the disruptions caused by the Red Sea shipping crisis.

items.statement: MMR supply scenario well balanced, launches not keeping pace with demand, no dramatic supply change expected in 3-6 months
items.quote: As of now, the supply scenario seems to be well balanced and not very different from what it was last year or -- in fact, the supply has only been going down in the market as the absorption has been increasing.

items.statement: Real Estate contracting via competitive bidding, no fixed contractors, evaluating financial strength and quality capability
items.quote: So the way the contracting entire process moves in, it's a competitive bid for each project that we float, and various contractors or different caliber quote for that. Then a negotiation takes place, 2, 3 rounds of negotiation, and finally a contractor is decided basis that.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 expected to be similar to or slightly better than Q4 FY25 performance
items.quote: If I share with you the Q1 for next F inancial Year working as on today things are operating either equivalent to Q4 or slightly better than that

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 6.2% in Q4 FY25 from 4.6% in Q4 FY24 and 4.6% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 6.2% from 4.6% in Q4 FY24, reflecting a YoY increment of 163 bps.

items.statement: Gross margin declined in Q4 FY25 vs Q3 FY25 due to liquidation of lower-margin synthetic yarn stock
items.quote: If you look at particularly this quarter, we have liquidated good stock for synthetic yarn. So, EBITDA out of the different 5 products that we work, it's comparatively lower.

items.statement: FY26 capex limited to maintenance and balancing equipment; no major expansion planned
items.quote: So, during this year, capital expenditure will be limited only through normal maintenance capital expenditure or some balancing equipment for enhancing the utilization.

items.statement: No major modernization planned for Ginni Filaments Chhata spinning unit in FY26
items.quote: Even next year also, we are not proposing any major restoration package for Chhata.

items.statement: Yarn utilization remains high 90%+; denim utilization improved 5-7% to post-90%; knitting utilization improved 5-7% to mid-80%
items.quote: In knitting and denim, our utilizations have improved by 5% - 7% in both the businesses. And we are in now post-90% in denim and mid-80% in knitting.

items.statement: Exports grew significantly in Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia; market share growing with US and EU brands
items.quote: There has been significant increase in the revenue from Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and other markets in FY'24 -'25.

items.statement: India-UK FTA could unlock $1 billion additional exports, raising India's share from 6% to 15-20% of UK's $24 billion apparel market
items.quote: We are expecting with these changes in the policy, FTA, we have an opportunity to unlock almost $1 billion additional exports from India to UK and taking our share from 6% to maybe 15% - 20%.

items.statement: US import tariffs unclear; company monitors trade policy changes closely
items.quote: While US import tariffs still being not clear for India at this moment, we are closely monitoring this and we understand that our partners have to prepare for any potential change in trade policy or the cost structure thereafter.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spreads under pressure across sector; fabric realizations improved to partially offset margin pressure
items.quote: On the industry front, cotton yarn spread remained under pressure, impacting the spinning margin across the sector. Despite these external challenges, we have stayed focused on improving our fabric realizations.

items.statement: Green power share at mid-20%; converting all boilers to biofuel within FY26
items.quote: We are currently in mid-20 percentage of our green power which is from solar and wind and we continue to work on this area and become more and more green power in terms of consumption.

items.statement: Consuming 60 lakh PET bottles daily for recycled polyester staple fiber production
items.quote: We are currently consuming 60 lakh bottles a day. And thereafter, ensuring that we become recycled or contribute our bits in terms of sustainability.

items.statement: Total debt at ₹1,700 crore (₹700 crore term loans, balance working capital); targeting lower debt-to-equity and improved interest coverage
items.quote: So, with respect to the debt management, including our working capital, we are at ₹ 1,700 crores, which includes ₹ 700 crores of term loan and balance being a part of a working capital.

items.statement: Finance cost at ~2.8% of sales; restructuring debt, exploring vendor/debtor bill discounting to reduce cost
items.quote: So currently we are at roughly 2.80% in terms of the overall sales number. But definitely we are working on restructuring of the debt.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory built up in H1 FY25 was liquidated during the year, reducing balance sheet inventory
items.quote: We had a build-up of finished goods inventory, which was subsequently liquidated during the year, which has resulted in a decrease of our inventory standing in the balance sheet at the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Focus on improving cash flows through working capital optimization and releasing blocked current assets
items.quote: We are also working on the blocked current assets so that we are able to improve the flow of the working capital.

items.statement: Shifting focus to value-added segments for better margins; investing in product centers for co-creation with customers on blends and functional features
items.quote: Now we focus more on the value-added segment, which probably will give better margins.

items.statement: Graphene-based textile development with Birla Cellulose and TACC in early stages; master batch development underway
items.quote: Graphene is still under development and it is in very early stages. So, we are still working on developmen t of a master batch

items.statement: Targeting value-added customers globally; direct engagement with brands seeking sustainability and eco-friendly products
items.quote: We have been trying to go direct to the customers, customers which are looking for sustainability and environment-friendly products.

items.statement: India's favorable tariff positioning vs Vietnam and China helping deepen engagement with global brands from US and Europe
items.quote: India's favorable tariff position ing remains a strategic strength, especially compared to the competitors like Vietnam and China

items.statement: India-UK FTA signed; expected to be transformative for Indian textile exporters
items.quote: Looking ahead, major strategic development that has happened recently is very progressive in nature, that is India-UK Free Trade Agreement.

items.statement: US-India tariff situation uncertain; 90-day pause period creates unpredictability for indirect exports
items.quote: Similarly, I also expect that the India -U.S. tariff will also settle for tim es to come. But overall, the expectation is that India stands to gain with these challenges

items.statement: RSWM 2.0 transformation driving cultural shift toward agility, cost effectiveness, smart manufacturing, and sharper execution
items.quote: RSWM 2.0 is not just a transformation plan, it represents the cultural shift across the organization.

items.statement: FY25 revenue grew 18.9% YoY to ₹4,825 crore; EBITDA rose 76.8% to ₹233 crore; PAT loss of ₹41 crore due to finance and depreciation costs
items.quote: Despite external challenges, RSWM reported a FY'25 revenu e increase of 18.9% year-on-year reaching to a new height of ₹4,825

items.statement: Ginni Filaments acquisition cost ~₹160 crore for 80,000 spindles; knitting division performing well, spinning division challenged by old machinery
items.quote: The acquisition to best of my knowledge or memory at this point of time it was around ₹160 crore.

items.statement: Management acknowledges shareholder pain from past dividend and rights issue; committed to better performance to compensate
items.quote: The pain that you have expressed yourself in terms of not receiving as a stakeholder your dividend for last couple of years, we fully appreciate and new management definitely take note of that and we will try to work on that.

items.statement: Expect cement demand growth of 6.5% to 7.5% in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting the cement demand to grow by 6.5% to 7.5% during FY '26, fuelled by infrastructure projects, rural recovery, real state momentum and softening interest rates.

items.statement: Target volume of about 39 million tons for FY26
items.quote: I would be slightly more aggressive. I would like to say that we may do about 39 million tons for this year.

items.statement: Capex earmarked at about INR3,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: About INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Depreciation expected at INR3,000-3,200 crores for FY26
items.quote: It is about INR3,000 crores to INR3,200 crores for 25-26.

items.statement: Q4 demand rebounded driven by government capex and rural recovery
items.quote: The Q4 last quarter has witnessed a rebound in demand driven by increase in government capex and overall pickup in all the economic activities.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 47% to INR1,383 crores; EBITDA per ton up 29% to INR1,406
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,383 crores, representing a growth of 47%. EBITDA per ton increased by 29% to INR1,406 from INR1,088 on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA per ton at INR1,437 after VRS impact of INR30.66 crores
items.quote: In fact, I might just like to add that our adjusted EBITDA per ton is standing at INR1,437 when the impact of one-off item of INR30.66 crores regarding impact of voluntary separation scheme of employees and contract workers undertaken by the company during the quarter is taken into account.

items.statement: Average realisation improved 5% sequentially to INR4,768 per ton
items.quote: Our focus on premium products helped us improve our average realisation per ton by about 5% to INR4,768 from INR4,554 on a sequential basis again.

items.statement: North realisation up 4% QoQ, East up 8% QoQ, South up 2% QoQ
items.quote: For quarter-on-quarter, the Northern realization is up by 4%, 8% for East and 2% for South.

items.statement: Fuel cost per kCal fell to INR1.48 from INR1.82 YoY
items.quote: Fuel costs per kCal for this quarter is INR1.48 against INR1.82 of March '24.

items.statement: Installed cement capacity reached 62.8 million tons after commissioning Etah (3 mt) and Baloda Bazar (3.4 mt) grinding units
items.quote: This has taken our total installed cement capacity to 62.8 million tons in India.

items.quote: The current clinker capacity is 36.7 million tons and by the end of financial year '25-'26, it will become 44 million tons.

items.statement: Premium product share rose to 15.6% in Q4 FY25 from 11.9% a year ago
items.quote: Recognizing the market demand for premium products, the company has launched several premium products, which have resulted into increase of share of premium product sales from 11.9% in Q4 2024 to 15.6% in Q4 of '24-'25.

items.statement: Launched Bangur Marble extra white Portland slag cement in Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand
items.quote: During March quarter. The company launched Bangur Marble cement, extra white Portland slag Cement in Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand markets.

During March

items.statement: Lead distance 446 km in Q4 vs 435 km YoY
items.quote: Lead distance is 446 Km for this quarter against 435 Km for March '24.

items.quote: Indeed, the Jaisalmer limestone was awarded to us in 2008 and then it got caught in the quagmire of various legal appeals and counter appeals. Final order has come to us about 10 days back. And it is a part of our expansion strategy.

items.statement: RMC business operating ~15 plants, targeting 50+ units; several plants already EBITDA positive
items.quote: We are currently operating about 15 plants, but the plan is to grow RMC rapidly. At this moment, we are looking at various markets where more and more units will be set up. I'm happy to say that there are several plants in our RMC division, which are already EBITDA positive, they have achieved in a faster ramp-up of those units, especially in the markets of Mumbai o

items.quote: Purulia has already been done. Patas also commisioned. Both are fully operational. And the rest sidings, I think we have said by mid-'27 or early '28 will be done.

items.statement: Demand subdued in April-early May due to war; expect pickup in 2-3 years to 75-85% utilisation
items.quote: And that is because of the fact that the demand has not been as robust as it should have been in April -- until first week of May, which was because of the war. So we are slightly cautious. Give us some time the demand should pick up. We are positive about it. No growth is possible without cement and steel. So we expect that in 2-3 years' time, we should go back to about 75%-85% capacity utilizati

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 2,500 crores and FY27 growth of 20-25% CAGR
items.quote: So as the guidance given for FY '26, INR 2,500 crores of revenue, we are confident to achieve for FY '26. And for FY '27, we expect a growth of 20% to 25% of CAGR.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance of 22-25% for next two years
items.quote: On margins, we expect to remain like in the range of 23%. I mean, like we gave the guidance of 25% plus/minus 3%. This up and down depending on the seasonality will happen, but we are confident to achieve between 22% to 25% without any issue.

items.statement: Second PPF line on track for Q2 FY26 start; TPU extrusion line (INR 118 cr) expected by October 2026
items.quote: We are also pleased to report that the work on the second PPF line is progressing well and remains on track for completion by Q2 FY '26. This facility with a capacity of 360 lakh square feet per annum is expected to commence production by October 2026.

items.statement: Second PPF line adds ~INR 400-450 cr revenue potential; full capacity with both lines could reach INR 3,000 cr
items.quote: So after the second, as we said, that will add around INR 400 crores of revenue, but that will be step-wise. So we can say, like the 33% additional which we made this year from a fungible line of Sun Control that will now be produced after September, will be produced on the PPF line. So overall, the revenue will go to INR 450 crores, estimated, but that will be stepwise.

items.statement: TPU line expected to improve company-level margins by 150-200 bps
items.quote: So we expect 1.5% to 2% betterment in the margins. I mean this is a rough estimate, but 1.5% to 2% percentage margin on company level.

items.quote: Yes. So we have, in fact, we had like 5 new distributors who were selling the products from big companies. They were mainly doing business with China and Korea, right? So that discussion is still going on and 1 or 2 of them has already been converted and rest are being worked out.

items.quote: One, the current challenges of tariff, which is 10% additional has been implemented. So with this, we don't see much of the -- I mean, challenges on that because this is somehow we have managed and it has been, I mean, taken care of.

items.statement: Collection days maintained at just 7 days in FY25
items.quote: Additionally, we have also managed our working capital efficiently and have kept our collection days at just 7 days. This reflects our ongoing commitment to operational excellence and efficient cash flow management.

items.statement: Zero net debt with cash reserves of INR 650 crores as of FY25
items.value: INR 650 crores cash; zero net debt
items.quote: Our balance sheet was zero net debt and a healthy cash reserve of INR 650 crores. The robust financial standing allows us to confidently invest in future growth opportunities.

items.statement: Evaluating US manufacturing/JV options if tariffs rise to 30%; current cost advantage from full backward integration; US labor costs estimated 30-40% higher
items.quote: But let me tell you one thing. that there is hardly any manpower available in the U.S. People can say anything. They will make garment, they will make this. But on the ground, right, to find people run the facility, our estimate says the current cost, which we have will go like 30%, 40% up in manufacturing, right, against the tariff of total 26%, which is 10% or worst scenario, it may another 16%.

items.statement: Added new teams in Europe, Middle East, East Africa; 1,000 trained PPF/window film applicators in India
items.quote: We have added new resources in Europe market. which is growing very fast for us. And then Middle East is one of the area which is growing very fast, where architectural segment and automotive segment are important, and we expect to grow very high on these markets like growth -- more than 50% growth in these markets because we have adde d new teams there

items.statement: Revaluation reserve of INR 764 crores
items.quote: Yes. So revaluation reserve is about INR 764 crores.

items.statement: Garware Home Solutions (B2C residential) in early stages; US D2C e-commerce portal launched 2-3 months ago showing good response
items.quote: Furthermore, we are planning to introduce Garware Home Solutions, a one-stop solution for all film requirements for residential spaces. While this initiative is currently in its early stages, we plan to scale it up to full capacity in the near future.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance 10-12% and EBITDA margin ~14%
items.quote: We are estimating a top line growth of about 10% to 12%, which is everything put together, and with an EBITDA guidance of approximately 14%.

items.statement: FY26 retail capex ~INR50 cr for 35 new stores; maintenance capex INR40-50 cr
items.value: INR50 cr retail, INR40-50 cr maintenance
items.quote: the capex planned for these 35 stores will be approximately INR50-odd crores. Other than that, the traditional business will have a capex of about INR40 crores to INR50 crores, which is regular maintenance capex.

items.statement: Plan to open 35 new ZECODE and DEVO stores in FY26 after 19 opened in H2 FY25
items.quote: During FY '26, we intend to open about 35 new stores across both brands.

items.statement: New retail formats may dilute EBITDA margin by 100-150 bps in FY26
items.quote: the new business is going to make losses to the tune of maybe 100 to 150 basis points.

items.statement: Consumer demand mixed in Q4 FY25; festive tailwinds extended to January then moderated
items.quote: In Q4 FY '25, the overall consumer demand environment remained mixed. The tailwinds from the festive and wedding season in Q3 extended into January but gradually moderated into the following month.

items.statement: Expect gradual recovery in discretionary spending supported by tax relief and easing inflation
items.quote: We believe consumer confidence will improve, paving the way for a gradual recovery in discretionary spending in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Launched ZECODE (fast fashion, <INR999) and DEVO (ethnic wear, kurta INR2,000-12,000) in H2 FY25
items.quote: we have expanded beyond our core fabric business by launching 2 new brands: ZECODE, which is focused on fast fashion; and DEVO, which is focused on ethnic wear.

items.quote: the Board of Directors has approved a total dividend INR12 per share o with a face value of INR2 each for FY '24-'25, amounting to a total dividend payout of INR54.4 crores.

items.statement: Trade receivables higher in Q4 due to strong sales; routine seasonal increase

items.statement: Cumulative non-convertible redeemable preference shares issuance pending regulatory approvals; timeline 9-12 months from announcement
items.quote: we had announced that there is a regulatory process that we have to follow, and we are waiting for approvals as yet. Approximately from that time, we had estimated this timeline to be about 9 to 12 months, which is sometime this year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue mix: Fabric 81%, Garments 13%, Others 6%

items.statement: FY25 capex INR143 cr mainly for looms, balancing equipment, solar, land and building

items.statement: ZECODE cluster in Karnataka/South India; DEVO cluster in Delhi/UP/North India; premium and high-footfall locations

items.statement: COCO model chosen initially to control operations and test consumer preferences; franchise may follow later

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at higher double digits; EBITDA margin to remain similar to FY25 (~20.5%)
items.quote: On the revenue this year, what we are planning is a higher double digit growth and on the EBITDA, we expected to remain on similar lines as this year.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin expected to decline ~100 bps; EBITDA margin maintained at FY25 level

items.quote: We've done better than that. This year, we have done better than that. That will be the desire to keep the EBITDA better than 27%, 28%. So generally, we aim to make it about 30% plus.

items.statement: FY25 average realization up 40% YoY driven by product mix; like-to-like price growth ~10%

items.quote: So while in the past, we've seen it go to INR11,000 or high INR11,000, we see whatever is in our next 4 quarters, we're looking at around INR10,000 average. That's mainly from the product mix.

items.statement: Gross debt INR4,444 crores, cash INR3,483 crores, net debt INR962 crores (Brigade share INR199 crores), net D/E 0.14

items.statement: Zero residential debt maintained; 82% of debt is commercial portion backed by rental income
items.quote: We continue to have zero residential debt, driven by higher sales, real estate and collections. Almost 82% of the debt pertains to the commercial portion, which is backed by rental income.

items.statement: Average cost of debt reduced to 8.67% from 8.82% YoY; CRISIL outlook upgraded to AA-positive from AA-stable
items.quote: Our average cost of debt has been reduced to 8.67% as of March '25 from 8.82% as of March '24. CRISIL has updated our rating outlook to AA - positive from AA - stable.

items.statement: Net cash from operating activities FY25 INR2,135 crores (+36% YoY), Q4 FY25 INR586 crores (+30% QoQ)
items.quote: Net cash flow from operating activities stood at INR2,135 crores, an increase of 36% over FY '24.

items.quote: So, as of 31st of March, about INR1,100 crores is the free cash. Then about INR480 crores is the cash which is out of QIP that we have to use, and balance is in RERA.

items.quote: if I take all 3, must be around 60%, 65%. We have been getting this question about IT services and so on. But I would say, over t he last 10 years, the profile of what is considered as IT as a job has really gone up the value

items.quote: Compared to 2 years back, you can say we are adding about 2 months' delay compared to 2 years back. But still, we generally -- say, for large projects, we still keep in mind about 12 months as the launch cycle.

items.statement: Leasing revenue FY25 INR1,165 crores (+24% YoY), EBITDA INR771 crores; Q4 FY25 revenue INR331 crores (+34% YoY), EBITDA INR194 crores
items.quote: The leasing segment clocked a turnover of INR1,165 crores, an increase of 24% over FY '24, with an EBITDA of INR771 crores.

items.statement: Hospitality subsidiary Brigade Hotel Ventures filed DRHP with SEBI in Oct 2024, received approval; IPO process underway
items.quote: Our Brigade Hotel Ventures Limited has filed the DRHP, the Draft Red Herring Prospectus, with SEBI in October, and we received the DRHP approval.

items.statement: Disbursement target of INR2 lakh to INR2.1 lakh crores for FY26
items.quote: And this year, again, we are expecting, provided the market conditions are there, then we are expecting that our disbursement should touch around INR2 lakhs to INR2,10,000 crores during the year itself.

items.statement: Loan book growth target of around 12% for FY26
items.quote: Yes, we expect so. It should be around 12%, plus/minus 1% or 2%, you can take it up.

items.statement: Target loan book of INR10 lakh crores by 2030
items.quote: We have targeted a INR10 lakh crore loan book by the year 2030.

items.statement: NIM guidance of 3.5% to 3.75% and spread of 2.75% to 3% for coming year
items.quote: And we are very confident that we will maintain the spread in the range of 2.75% to 3% and the NIM in the range of 3.5% to 3.75% for the coming year.

items.statement: Net zero NPA target by end of FY26
items.quote: We hope to continue this trend, and we are very hopeful that we'll become a net zero NPA company by the end of '25-'26.

items.statement: RE disbursement target of INR3 lakh crores by 2030 from current INR58,000 crores
items.quote: We have set a very ambitious target of touching INR3 lakh crores investment -- I mean, disbursement in the RE sector from our current loan book of roughly INR58,000 crores by 2030.

items.statement: RBPF disbursement target of INR80,000 crores to INR90,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: We are targeting RBPF disbursement close to INR80,000 crores to INR90,000 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: RE sanctions target of close to INR1,50,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: In the current year, we are targeting close to INR1,50,000 crores of sanctions.

items.statement: Borrowing plan of INR1,70,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: This year, we have plan of raising INR1,70,000 crores.

items.statement: Expected recovery of INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores from NPA resolutions in FY26
items.quote: So I am expecting that around INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores will be recovered in the FY '25-'26.

items.statement: Sanctions of over INR3.37 lakh crores in FY25
items.quote: Just for information, during '24-'25 financial year, our sanctioned projects stand at over INR3.37 lakh crores, which is a huge and which sustains basically the momentum of the last year.

items.statement: Documentation increased to INR2.07 lakh crores in FY25
items.quote: documentation has, of this year, has increased to INR2.07 lakh crores.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 18% YoY to almost INR1.9 lakh crores in FY25
items.quote: Disbursements, if we look at it, have also increased on an 18% year-on-year basis to almost INR1.9 lakh crores

items.quote: The yields on our assets has improved to 10.05%. The cost of our funds stand at around 7.11%, and our resultant spread is at 2.94%.

items.statement: Gross NPA reduced to 1.35% and net NPA to 0.38% in FY25

items.statement: Total borrowings INR4.88 lakh crores with 33% foreign currency, 99.8% hedged
items.quote: the total outstanding borrowing of REC has reached to almost INR4,88,000 crores, of which foreign currency borrowings constitute 33%. Just to remind you all, almost 99.8% of these foreign currency borrowings are hedged.

items.statement: Raised USD500 million via 144A bonds at 127.5 bps over US Treasury in Sep 2024

items.statement: Raised INR5,000 crores via domestic zero coupon bonds at 6.25%
items.quote: We also tapped the domestic zero coupon bond market and raised close to INR5,000 crores at an interest rate of 6.25%.

items.quote: it gives me a lot of pleasure to announce that this year also, we have declared a final dividend of INR2.60 per share, indicating a total dividend of almost INR18 per share for the financial year '24-'25, which is a growth of almost 13% compared to the previous year total dividend of INR16 per share.

items.statement: Total dividend payout INR4,740 crores in FY25 vs INR4,000 crores in FY24
items.quote: If you look in overall terms, the dividend payout for the company stands at INR4,740 crores, which is in comparison to roughly INR4,000 crores of dividend that we disbursed last year.

items.statement: 51 lakh applications received for PM Surya Ghar, 12.5 lakh installations completed, 70% subsidy released

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 25-30%, EBITDA margin 16-17%, DI Pipe production >4 lakh tons

items.quote: With this encouraging outlook, we are targeting revenue growth of around 25% to 30%, EBITDA margins in the range of 16% to 17% and DI Pipe production surpassing 4 lakh tons.

items.quote: Yes, of course, we are also exporting DI Pipes, and we will be expanding further on the export market as we are doing for Ferroalloys?

items.quote: Our current depreciation -- for the last financial, it was INR63 crores -- INR94 crores as compared [inaudible 0:34:04] in FY '23-'24. Once all the plants are commissioned, it can go up to INR105 crores, INR110 crores, an increase of INR10 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: Carry-forward tax losses INR250 crores at start FY26; normal taxation after INR250 crores profitability
items.quote: As far as cash flow, the tax is concerned, we started the last financial year with INR1,000 crores carry-forward tax losses. Out of that, INR750 crores, INR800 crores has been consumed. And still we have started this current financial year with a carry forward tax loss of INR250 crores. After the profitability of INR250 crores, we will be in normal taxation.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR1,500 crores with strong upward potential; order inflow guidance INR1,600-1,700 crores
items.quote: We give our initial guidance at INR1,500 crores with a strong upward potential given the sustained order inflow as well as the third plant commission coming on stream in H2 of this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR1,900-2,000 crores driven by new products, export railway, and larger generators
items.quote: We are also focused on FY '27 and new products in large generators, large motors and, of course, execution of the traction motors for Europe, U.S. and the CIS countries, which will drive the company towards the INR 19 billion to INR 20 billion mark in FY '27.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 18-18.25% with upward potential
items.quote: EBITDA margins will be in the range of 18% to 18.25% with an upward movement potential.

items.statement: Manufacturing order book INR13.68bn (INR10.12bn regular, INR3.16bn railway, INR0.11bn space/aftermarket, INR0.29bn Turkey); exports 62% excluding railway
items.quote: Order book of Manufacturing segment is INR13.68 billion, INR10.12 billion regular manufacturing business, INR3.16 billion railway business, space and aftermarket, INR0.11 billion and INR0.29 billion Turkey business.

items.statement: Q4 order inflow INR4.13bn highest ever, up 43% QoQ and 41% YoY; 68% exports, 32% domestic
items.quote: Order inflow for the quarter is INR4.13 billion, highest ever since inception of our company. Order inflow has increased 43% Q-to-Q basis and 41% over a Y-o-Y comparison basis.

items.statement: Export demand very strong from gas turbines, engines, motors for fracking, data centers, AI server farms, grid stabilization, Ukraine; domestic market growth moderated to 4%
items.quote: The demand is simply huge, and the market growth presents the company with the most exciting growth opportunities ever since its inception.

items.statement: Third plant commissioning starting May, first shed already started; impact on numbers from H2 FY26; full ramp-up in FY27
items.quote: We have already started by the end of this month May, we will start commissioning the first shed , the second shed and third shed, all the equipment and everything, all the trials and everything will start.

items.statement: No new capacity until INR2,200 crores revenue; will optimize existing capacity to INR2,200-2,300 crores first
items.quote: We will not put any new capacity until about INR2,200 crores. We will optimize and we will make this existing capacity extremely efficient to produce more.

items.statement: Launching larger generators up to 40-45MW this year, targeting up to 100MW; new products for gas turbine market up to 25MW and trial machines for 40-45MW
items.quote: And this year, we'll put larger generators into the market up to 40 megawatts, even 45 megawatt size. And this segment of the market is equal to the size compared to the market where we're currently operating in.

items.statement: Working with all 3 major gas turbine OEMs globally; one dominant OEM is largest customer; new OEM signed up for gas turbine generators
items.quote: There are only 3 big OEMs in the world who make these gas turbines. So we are working with all 3 of them. But one of them is having a very large market share and the other 2, smaller amounts.

items.statement: Export order inflow grew 67% YoY to INR9.85bn; EUR/INR forward bookings at favorable rates (INR96-97) will yield solid FX gains all year
items.quote: Order inflow from direct and deemed exports has increased by 3.95 billion from 5.9 billion to 9.85 billion, which is a 67% growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: US revenue share ~20-25% currently, could grow with larger machines in FY27; Europe government-driven, US private sector-driven
items.quote: Approximately, it will end up being around that number, 20% to 25%.. But if we penetrate with the larger machines in FY '27 into that market, then this share could grow.

items.statement: Turkey market outlook bleak due to changed local content rules making local production unviable; may shut plant after current order
items.quote: They've changed the calculations for local content once again. Of course, it will not be applicable for this order, but it will be applicable for future orders. I think it will be almost impossible for anyone to meet those new guidelines.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to improve dramatically from Q1 as inventory consumed and March receivables collected; strong improvement by end H1
items.quote: We will see a big improvement in the operating cash flow starting from Q1 onwards. We will see because we'll not be buying steel and copper, we'll be consuming from inventory.

items.statement: Strong cash position INR1.99bn consolidated; minimal balance sheet impact from Turkey exit (INR3-4cr investment recoverable)
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong cash position of INR1.99 billion.

items.statement: Setting up UK design center with 2-3 highly qualified individuals for large generator/motor designs up to 100MW; white collar hiring starting now
items.quote: TDPS is going to set up a design center in the U.K. initially with two or three highly qualified individuals who will be responsible for developing new generators and more products for the future.

items.statement: Gas turbine generator global market share <3%; significant room for growth with new products and OEMs
items.quote: Very small, less than 3%.

items.statement: Only one dominant competitor in larger generator segment (40-100MW); market seeking second player; TDPS well positioned with new products
items.quote: Actually there is just one big competitor in this range, which dominates the market. And the market is also looking for a second player. So I think that we are in the right place, right time.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty but demand unaffected as OEMs pass duties to end users; India-US trade deal could provide advantage if lower tariffs than Europe
items.quote: These are all highly uncertain things. They change from week to week. And as far as our customers are concerned, they need to import generators. They know that they have to pay the import duties. It's not coming on to us.

items.statement: Railway traction motor prototypes for Europe, US, CIS under development; volume production from Q4 FY26, revenue impact FY27; 3-3.5 year contracts
items.quote: We are building prototypes this year. Testing will take place this year and volume production will start by about Q4, but the impact will be felt in FY '27. And these are something like 3- to 3.5-year contracts that's starting from FY '27.

items.statement: NPCIL motor order ~INR50cr, 13 motors 3MW each; execution next 12 months; BHEL main competitor; steady replacement market opportunity
items.quote: We gave that. We announced it already on the exchange when we got the order, I remember it to be somewhere around INR50 crores, It could be around plus/minus, but around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Geothermal Phase 2 (~1000MW) still preferred party, finalization expected in 3 months; configuration changes ongoing
items.quote: We are still the preferred party. It's not yet finalized, but it will get finalized soon, I think, in the next 3 months, we should be able to deliver a good news to the market about this.

items.statement: Gross contribution margins sustainable in current range; staff costs to increase as white collar hiring begins for new plant
items.quote: Coming to the gross contribution margin in general, they have been delivering fairly consistent numbers for the past few quarters. So it's sustainable in this range for sure.

items.statement: Bulk purchased copper and electrical steel during price dip and tariff uncertainty; inventory build to support H1 production
items.quote: For example, when the copper prices dropped recently, we purchased a lot of copper, and we also bought a lot of electrical steel because we saw prices were coming down.

items.statement: Dividend payout ~11% FY25; increasing steadily 10-12% per year but growth investments prioritized over higher payouts
items.quote: We have been steadily increasing the dividend as a percentage by something like 10%, 12% per year, and we will continue to do that. But that's not the first priority.

items.statement: No inorganic opportunities currently; focusing internal accruals for future capacity beyond third plant
items.quote: We are definitely looking one step beyond the third plant also right now looking at funding that through internal accruals.

items.statement: Debt reduction guidance of Rs 100 crore over two years; Rs 37 crore reduced in FY25, targeting ~Rs 60 crore in FY26
items.quote: We are on track, and we wish to achieve the guidance that we have given. However, considering the market changes with respect to the big four entry, we are constantly evaluating the requirement of any further investment, and we will keep you updated on the same.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 first positive EBITDA in six quarters at Rs 2.4 crore; adjusted EBITDA Rs 17 crore excluding new initiative expenses
items.quote: The Company has posted its first positive EBITDA in six quarters, primarily driven by materialization of deferred B2B deals. This was despite the impact of accelerated inventory charge-offs.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA loss Rs 80 crore; adjusted EBITDA loss Rs 29 crore excluding Rs 51 crore new initiative expenses
items.quote: For the Financial Year ended 2025, the revenue from operations stood at around Rs. 685 crores which declined by 3% year -on-year. EBITDA loss stood at Rs. 80 crores and net loss was reported at around Rs. 85 crores.

items.statement: Advertising outlook subdued near term due to macro pressures, IPL, and GEC return to Free Dish; non-sports categories particularly affected
items.quote: Given the ongoing macroeconomic pressures, geopolitical tensions and major sporting events like IPL, the overall advertising outlook is expected to remain subdued in the near term, particularly for non-sports category.

items.statement: Digital media revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 252 crore in FY25; traditional media declined 9.69% to Rs 433 crore
items.quote: Digital media revenues for the 4th Quarter stood at around Rs. 57 crores, up by 1.25% year-on-year. For the full financial year, it was around Rs. 252 crores, which was a growth of approximately 11%.

items.statement: TV syndication B2B business decline dragged overall FY25 revenue down 3% YoY; excluding it, revenue grew 8.3% YoY
items.quote: If you were to exclude the TV syndication B2B business, the Company's revenue recorded a growth of around 8.3% year-on-year for the full year, despite a challenging advertising environment.

items.statement: B2B licensing deals lumpy and non-recurring; FY26 outlook positive with strong content and acquisition pipeline
items.quote: I believe the outlook for the next year is positive. The business should be on a higher number than where we have done this year. We have enough content pipeline on offer as well as on the acquisition pipeline.

items.statement: No plans for new channel launch; monitoring impact of big four GEC entry on Free Dish
items.quote: No, currently we have no plan s. As I shared in my opening comments, the big four GECs have entered on the Free Dish platform . And as a result of that , the viewership shares and lot of things there has been a significant change in

items.statement: Two of four channels at or near breakeven; Shemaroo Umang requires major investment in original content
items.quote: Actually, two of our channels, so one has in fact broken even more than a year, actually probably I would imagine almost last nearly 1.5 year ago. One more channel is in, you can say, near breakeven, very low investment or burn kind of situation.

items.statement: Chumbak TV ratings at fresh high, unaffected by big four Free Dish entry; breakeven outlook positive
items.quote: Chumbak in fact has been on a good growth path. This last recent rating also we have for Chumbak has been kind of on a fresh new high. And in fact, it is one of the few channels which has not been impacted by the entry of the big four large broadcasters on the Free Dish platform.

items.statement: Shemaroo FilmiGaane YouTube channel crossed 71 million subscribers; 10.5 billion views across portfolio in Q4 FY25
items.quote: On YouTube, Shemaroo FilmiGaane crossed 71 million subscribers this quarter. The Company garnered more than 10.5 billion views during the quarter across its portfolio channels.

items.statement: GEC channels hold 8.2% viewership share in overall Hindi GEC genre; two original shows launched in Q4
items.quote: In broadcasting, the GEC channels have a viewership share of around 8.2% in overall Hindi GEC genres. Two original shows were released during the quarter, Bade Haveli Ki Choti Thakurain and Jamuniya.

items.statement: Acquired Aikyam to gain end-to-end control of broadcast licenses for ShemarooTV, Shemaroo Umang, Shemaroo Marathi Bana; nominal rent cost savings
items.quote: They essentially hold the underlying broadcast licenses on which we are operating the ShemarooTV, Shemaroo Umang and Shemaroo Marathi Bana. So, essentially what it does is it brings in the end-to-end control of the broadcast right from the licensing part.

items.statement: US tariff impact uncertain; industry examining interpretations; management believes not intended for foreign films, no major impact expected
items.quote: As of now, there is no order that has come in. So, we do not know what is the nature or the basis on which this is going to be applicable. There are multiple interpretations, and the industry bodies are also examining.
