items.statement: Will generate significant free cash flow over next few years; allocation via deleveraging, dividend step-up, buybacks (Indus or Africa), potential acquisitions
items.quote: I think you will have to leave it to our judgment to use the cash, right. We will manage this throug h a combination of deleveraging, dividend step up, some buyback. This could be in Indus or it could be in Africa or it could be some other expansion o n acquisition but at this point, we really do need to say that, for us, we are going to be very fiscally prudent.

items.statement: No plan to call partly paid shares currently; will call only when needed
items.quote: No, we will call that only when we need it. At this point in time, there is no requirement for us to call the partly paid shares.

items.statement: DTH faces regulatory asymmetry vs cable and broadband; free DD Free Dish adds pressure; subsidies being removed, waiting for competition to follow
items.quote: We have taken a brave call and we have done it. We are waiting for the competition to follow and we hope sense will prevail to strip those subsidies out because there is no point putting in subsidies in a market where the only subsidy is going in to rotate your own customer.

items.statement: Hexacom capex trajectory to move downward from FY25; transport job limited in its two circles
items.quote: On capex, I think, the capex will come down, like it is happening in Airtel, there is a transport job to be done, but I think the transport job in these two circles is not so much. So, the capex trajectory should see a downward move from FY2025.

items.statement: Hexacom Q4 EBITDAaL margin 46.6% (+30bps QoQ); not representative due to low opex, inflationary cost pressures ahead; targets margin improvement as rural rollout largely done
items.quote: I would say, this is not a quarter which is representative. I think, if you look at post tariff like, maybe Q3-Q4, that would be more representative, but I must at the same time tell you that these are very small nuances and I think increasingly, we will target to improve our EBITDAaL margins.

items.statement: Hexacom prepaid 858 Cr of high-cost DoT debt (8.65% coupon) from 2024 auction; remaining spectrum dues from FY21 and FY22 auctions at ~7.2%
items.quote: During Q4, we prepaid 858 Crores of high cost DoT debt pertaining to the 2024 auction. This was at a coupon of about 8.65%. With this, the company is left with only FY2021 and FY2022 spectrum dues.

items.statement: Hexacom home broadband growth driven by FWA (lion's share of Q4 adds) due to lack of wired broadband in Rajasthan and Northeast
items.quote: FWA is a very, very strong offering for us and as a matter of fact, lion's share of homes acquisition in Q4 has been with FWA. It is just the fact that there is no wired broadband in large geographies of these two circles.

items.statement: Hexacom tower sale to Indus put in abeyance at TCIL's request; fresh process to be undertaken per PSU governance requirements
items.quote: We remain convinced about the business logic and merit of the proposal ; however, in keeping with the highe r standards of corporate governance and transparency, it has been agreed to put the current proposal in abeyance and undertake a fresh exercise in consultation with TCI L.

items.statement: Not commenting on Vi 5G launch impact; focused on own customer growth opportunity which remains intact
items.quote: I do not want to comment on what our competitors are doing. I think that the way I would see it is that as far as postpaid is concerned, we have added about 600,000 net a dds this quarter . I see no reason why t hat should not actually step up because the number of high value users on our platform is still a large number and prepaid to postpaid could be a very, very important driver of growth.

items.statement: Hexacom not accelerating 5G SA transition; adequate NSA capacity for current FWA rollout; SA implementation when capacity chokes, no deadline
items.quote: I do not think we are looking at a target of acceleration. It is a simple function of the capacity of our 5G infrastructure being utilized. Today, there is adequate capacity for us to roll out more F WAs. Of course, as FWAs capacity gets choked up they can be liberated by laying fibers because then you can do a concentrated fiber laying and wire up those homes, alternately, you can go to SA

items.statement: Hexacom dividend payout ~33-34% vs Airtel 35%; difference marginal; will prudently deploy cash balancing deleveraging, dividends, growth needs
items.quote: I think we should not see too much between 33 and 35 and all of that. I think this company also, yes its debt is less, but it does not have some of the other engines of growth, which possibly Airtel has. Like what was mentioned in the Airtel call , we will balance between the three, four objectives and we will prudently use the cash that is generated and deploy it as and when required.

items.statement: Consumer spending remains weak due to high inflation and lower capex; secondary sales picked up in H2 FY25 but dealers hesitant to restock
items.quote: Lower CAPEX and persistent higher inflation did impact discretionary spending as households prioritized essential goods and services over non-essential items.

items.statement: Expect FY26 to be a year of recovery with growth trajectory returning; early bookings show 12-13% growth vs last year
items.quote: We will be back to the growth trajectory in FY '26 and continue to build on our initiatives to deliver sustainable growth and value to our stakeholders.

items.statement: Branded Textile steady-state margin range 20-22%; overall lifestyle business decent margin 14-15%
items.quote: In a Branded Textile we have always mentioned that it is a margin in the range of 20%, 21%, 22%, that's the kind of margin we have always been maintaining. Overall, if I look at the business, I think if I take lifestyle as a business, anything between 14% to 15% you can consider as a decent margin.

items.statement: Autumn winter 2025 bookings for Branded Textile are decent; overall bookings up 12-13% vs last year
items.quote: We are observing some decent bookings for the Branded Textile business for the autumn winter collection of 2025.

items.statement: Garmenting capacity expansion underway; once complete will be one of largest suit makers worldwide
items.quote: We continue to expand our capacity, a move that will significantly bolster our global standing. Once this expansion is complete, we would become one of the largest suit maker s worldwide, paving the way for further growth in customer

items.statement: Garmenting customers renegotiated pricing due to global uncertainties; training costs for new product lines affected profitability
items.quote: However, due to global uncertainties, customers have adopted a wait and watch approach. This has primarily impacted our margins as customers have renegotiated pricing. Additionally, the cost of training personnel for new prod uct lines have further affected profitability

items.statement: Launched sleepwear (Sleepz) and innerwear (Park Avenue Innerwear) categories; Ethnix crossed Rs 100 cr revenue
items.quote: Our journey to enter new categories with sleepwear by Raymond were launched during the previous quarter. And in order to expand the product suite for the Complete Man, we had entered the innerwear category with the successful launch of Park Avenue Innerwear.

items.statement: Added 20+ new garmenting clients across US, UK, Europe in FY25
items.quote: In Fiscal '25, we have successfully added over 20-plus new clients across key markets including the US, UK and Europe.

items.statement: Ethnix category growing but competition increased from national players and city-specific boutiques; both will coexist
items.quote: So, in my opinion, this is the sort of business which would take three to five years to mature itself. So, you will find a place for national brands like us to play the role . And then you will have a city -specific or town -specific boutique player who will have their own play. B ut both will coexist, and each one will have a market

items.statement: US tariff differential ~30% vs China benefits garmenting; UK-India FTA presents growth opportunity but supply chain realignment takes 12-15 months
items.quote: On the US tariff front , for all our Garmenting products, we would be benefiting from a substantial tariff differential of approximately 30-odd-percent vis-à-vis China. This competitive edge allows us to offer more attractive pricing and enhance our market position and improve the market share with our customers in US

items.statement: Net working capital 87 days (Rs 1,473 cr) in Mar'25 vs 89 days (Rs 1,553 cr) in Dec'24; reduction due to lower receivables and inventory
items.quote: In terms of net working capital which stood at 87 days amounting to Rs. 1,473 crores in March '25 compared to 89 days which is Rs. 1,553 crores in December 2024. This decrease is mainly due to a reduction in trade receivables and inventory.

items.statement: Net debt-free with net cash of Rs 90 cr as of 31 Mar 2025
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we continued to have a net debt free position with net cash of Rs. 90 crores as of 31st of March 2025.

items.statement: Ransomware attack caused ~25-26 days disruption; ~50% sales loss recovered in quarter, balance over 6-8 months; estimated Rs 150-175 cr sales impact, Rs 70-80 cr EBITDA impact
items.quote: Approximately 25, 26 days of impact had happened. And whatever the sales, because it is an entire production, we are connected on all IT systems and the systems were not available, so it impacted all the production, sales and everything. However, almost 50% of the sales loss has been recovered during the quarter, and the balance most likely will be recovered over the next six to eight months.

items.statement: Branded Textile Q4 revenue Rs 727 cr (-21% YoY), EBITDA margin 7% vs 21.8%; Branded Apparel revenue Rs 391 cr, EBITDA margin 0.4% vs 13.5%; Garmenting revenue Rs 248 cr, EBITDA loss 2.9% vs 12% margin; High Value Cotton Shirting revenue Rs
items.quote: In terms of our Branded Textile segment, revenue declined to Rs. 727 crores by 21% in the 4th Quarter of Fiscal ‘2 5 as compared to Rs. 920 crores in the 4th Quarter of Fiscal ’24, predominantly on account of weaker consumer demand and also impacted by the ransomware attack leading to scaled deleverage, resulting in lower EBITDA margins at 7% in the 4th Quarter of Fiscal ‘25, as compared to 21.8%

items.statement: Store breakeven extended from 24 to 36-40 months due to weak demand; 350 stores opened in last 3 years carrying rental and manpower costs
items.quote: normally 24 months is a decent time frame by which store becomes decent breakeven. But if the demand scenario goes weaker, obviously, 24 extends to 36, 40 months. And that is that additional one year period. And as we said, 350 stores we have opened in the last three years, so you can well imagine the impact of these rentals, the manpower cost which is sitting has not been able to perform or deliv

items.statement: Ethnix store closures ~10 stores; target 300 stores over 3-4 years via franchisee-led model
items.quote: So, basically, I think only 10 stores we have closed, not more than 10 stores we have closed. And as far as the number of stores is concerned, it is not right for me to give only the next 12 months. As I said, over the next 36 months we will get to a level of 300 stores.

items.statement: Plan to double hotel room inventory to 4,000 keys over next five years via greenfield, brownfield and acquisitions
items.quote: Looking ahead, our growth ambition remains unchanged. We plan to double our hotel room inventory to 4,000 keys over the next five years, through a combination of greenfield and brownfield projects and acquisitions.

items.statement: Estimated INR 5,000 crore capex needed over next five years at INR 2.5 crore per key for 2,000 new rooms
items.quote: Assuming a mix of luxury and upscale hotels with a capex of around INR 2.5 crores per key, we estimate around INR 5,000 crores will be needed over the next five years, right?

items.statement: Expect over INR 6,500 crore EBITDA generation over next five years driven by mid-teen RevPAR and high-teen EBITDA growth
items.quote: Our existing assets in India and Maldives, we expect to generate substantial EBITDA. And we conservatively estimate that over INR 6,500 crore s will be generated in the next five years, driven by, let's say, mid-teen RevPAR growth and high-teen EBITDA growth

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA ratio at 1.7x; can raise additional INR 1,300 crore LRD debt against annuity EBITDA at 6x multiple
items.quote: Our net debt to EBITDA ratio is at 1.7, one of the lowest in the industry. At a current level of debt in India, on a 6x multiple, the company can raise additional LRD debt of INR 1,300 crores based on a FY25 annuity EBITDA of INR437 crores.

items.statement: India hospitality EBITDA margin target 40-42% in next 2-3 years from current 37%; Maldives target 35-36% from 32%
items.quote: Our internal target is to take it to around 42% in next two to three years. And Maldives from 32% to 35-36%.

items.statement: Pune luxury market has limited supply; portfolio controls 65% of luxury inventory; office space growing from 70 to 110 million sq ft over five years
items.quote: Pune has very limited or no supply in the luxury market. And this is one of the single-biggest reasons why I feel our hotel portfolio in Pune will continue to grow. The other is the fact that we actually dominate the luxury space with over 65% of the inventory, that we control.

items.statement: No significant impact from US tariffs on India bookings; Maldives demand diversified with US only 3% of inbound tourism; soft season supported by Asia markets
items.quote: We are not seeing any huge downward trend through the U.S. tariff situation that you're mentioning. We just came out of a very strong quarter and our bookings are looking pretty strong in this quarter in India as well. As far as Maldives is concerned, the beauty of Maldives is that it's provided from a very well diversified customer profile from all over the world. And it doesn't really depend on

items.statement: India Q4 ADR grew 16% YoY to INR 12,571; full year ADR grew 10% to INR 11,076; RevPAR grew 24% in Q4 to ~INR 9,000
items.quote: In India, our dynamic revenue management strategies helped us to grow Q4 ADR by 16% year on year t o 12,571, while full year ADR grew 10% over the previous year to 11,076, showing our power pricing and

items.statement: Maldives Q4 TRevPAR grew 5% on same-store basis; Raaya operates at TRevPAR ~INR 35,000 with volume-based strategy initially
items.quote: Raaya is operating at TRevPAR at around INR35,000. Now, typically, especially for Maldives, it takes a long period for ramp up of any resorts, considering it's sitting in isolation and you have to have a lot of to showcase the resort to a lot of people in all over the world.

items.statement: Announced pipeline of 367 keys across Varanasi, Sri Lanka, and Aloft to AC by Marriott rebranding in Bangalore Whitefield
items.quote: We have announced a pipeline of 367 keys, in the three different cities, Varanasi, Sri Lanka and the rebranding of the Aloft to AC by Marriott, in Bangalore, Whitefield. That's 367.

items.statement: ROFO assets include 900 keys: Navi Mumbai JW+Moxy big box, two Moxys in Pune integrated business parks (150 and 250 keys)
items.quote: We have 900 keys from our ROFO assets. The big box being built in Navi Mumbai. That's a combination between JW and a Moxy, and two more Moxys in integrated business parks in Pune- one with 150 and the other with 250 keys.

items.statement: Targeting ~300 keys from branded villa projects with two large land parcel MOUs close to signing; remaining ~500 keys via acquisitions
items.quote: So, the balance, we will be looking at branded villa projects, around 300 keys, for which we are very close to signing MOUs for two big land parcels. And the balance, which is the remainder 500 keys will be covered through acquisitions. So, that's our plan.

items.statement: India RevPAR grew 24% YoY in Q4 to ~INR 9,000 vs industry 18%; TRevPAR grew 25% to INR 16,531; full year RevPAR 18% to INR 7,256
items.quote: This translated to our RevPar growing at a standout 24% in Q4 to almost INR 9,000, while the industry grew at 18%. Our RevPar also grew at 25% to INR 16,531 in Q4.

items.statement: India occupancy expanded 4pp to 71% in Q4; full year occupancy up 4pp to 65.5%; weekend occupancy driven to 65% by MICE and weddings
items.quote: Our focus on MICE and weddings helped us to drive up weekend occupancy to 65% in Q4, resulting in occupancy expanding 4% points to 71%. Full year occupancy also improved 4% points to 65.5%.

items.statement: Maldives Q4 TRevPAR grew 5% same-store; peak occupancies during Christmas, New Year, Easter, Chinese New Year, Valentine's, August holidays
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that in Q4, our TRevPAR Maldives grew 5% on a same-store basis. The TRevPAR, including Raaya, is lower in absolute terms because it operates at a lower price point compared to our other two Uber luxury resorts.

items.statement: India non-commissionable direct/web channels up to 40% from 31% last year; Maldives 60% wholesale but shifting to direct digital platforms
items.quote: In India, 40% of our business comes through non-commissionable distribution and web channels, up from 31% last year, reducing our dependency on non-direct channels, improving profitability. In Maldives, while 60% of our business still flows through wholesale channels, we have a clear strategy shift towards direct digital platforms to improve margins.

items.statement: Annuity assets provide stable cash flows: Q4 revenue INR 125 crore (+5% YoY), EBITDA INR 111 crore (+5%); full year revenue INR 483 crore, EBITDA INR 437 crore
items.quote: Our annuity revenue in Q4 was at INR 125 crores, up 5% year-on-year, while EBITDA was at INR 111 crores, a growth of 5% year-on-year. For the full year, our annuity revenue was at INR 483 crores and EBITDA was at INR 437 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt INR 2,306 crore (INR 1,340 crore rupee + USD 113M/INR 965 crore USD); cash INR 560 crore; net debt INR 1,745 crore
items.quote: We maintain a strong balance sheet with a consolidated gross debt of INR 2,306 crores. This includes INR 1,340 crores in rupee-denominated debt and USD113 million equivalent to INR 965 crores in USD-denominated debt for our Maldives hotels. Our consolidated cash balance stands at INR 560 crores, resulting in a net debt of INR 1,745 crores.

items.statement: Cost of finance competitive: 8.24% rupee loans, 7.7% USD loans; further 15bps reduction post-March
items.quote: Our cost of finance is very competitive in the market. As on 31st March, rates were at 8.24% for rupee-denominated loans and 7.7% for USD-denominated loans. We have seen further reductions post-March of around 15 basis points in the overall cost of funds.

items.statement: CRISIL AA (Stable) rating assigned; material subsidiary Panchshil Corporate Park received AA+ (Stable)
items.quote: We have received strong credit ratings with CRISIL assigning us AA rating (Stable) and one of our material subsidiaries, Panchshil Corporate Park Private Limited, receiving AA plus rating (Stable).

items.statement: No equity dilution planned for promoter stake reduction to 75% per SEBI; 2.5 years timeline; will explore options including OFS
items.quote: So, we still have around 2.5 years for that dilution, but the cash flow, what I explained, is coming out of internal accruals. I mean, most of our capex will be funded through internal accruals. We are not looking at any dilution. We will look at ways and means, how to reduce that to 75% as and when it is required as per SEBI guidelines.

items.statement: Maldives tax 15% on profit but not taxable due to debt; India effective tax rate 25% after exhausting 35AD carried forward losses; current tax outflow ~INR 200 crore/year
items.quote: Maldives tax is at 15% on profit. So we have some debt there. So taxable, the income is not taxable there. In India, we have different entities. So tax rate is different. One of our material subsidiaries, we are at 25%. We have carried forward tax losses on account of 35AD incentive given to hospitality companies. So we'll use that once we exhaust with that, we will move to a new tax rate and effe

items.statement: Organic EBITDA expected to grow from INR 1,000 to ~1,700 crore over five years via operating leverage from mid-teen revenue and high-teen EBITDA growth
items.quote: And that will take our EBITDA from organically, from INR 1,000 crores to around 1,700 crores. As for same-store revenue, we expect to go from INR 2,000 crores to INR 3,000 crores.

items.statement: Short-term cancellations seen from airline disruptions and travel advisories due to geopolitical tensions; no cancellations in last 4-5 days; portfolio resilient with diversified revenue streams
items.quote: Yes, there is been a blip. We've seen some cancellations due to some airline disruptions and travel advisories. Yes, there's also some geopolitical tensions. But I feel this is only, it was rather, let me stress on the word 'was', for a short period of time. And I mean, we don't expect to see cancellations. As of this morning. I checked, there were no cancellations that were happening in the last

items.statement: ROFO assets to be transferred at warm shell stage at fair market value in 2.5-3 years; announcements expected soon
items.quote: Just to add to Milind, I think we will bring the assets into Ventive at a warm shell stage at fair market value. And I think that will ensure creation of wealth for minority shareholders as well. So the timeline for warm shell transfer will be around 2.5 to 3 years, just to answer that question as well. You'll be hearing some announcements very soon on this.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% CAGR over 3-4 years on consolidated basis
items.quote: So roughly, our idea is that over a period of 3-4 years, we should grow at a CAGR of 20%-25% usually. That's what we are planning.

items.statement: Honeywell business to grow 70-80% annually
items.quote: Honeywell w ill keep growing the trajectory as we are growing at almost, we try to grow it by around 70 %-80% every year

items.statement: Honeywell EBITDA margin normally 15-17%
items.quote: Normally, we generate around 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Operational leverage to improve EBITDA by 2-3% after reaching 17-18 countries
items.quote: After one year and a half, when we have reached to 17-18 countries, then all this operational leverage will come into play and we will improve our EBITDA numbers for sure.

items.statement: Honeywell FY25 revenue INR255.17 crores; India INR133 crores, International INR121 crores
items.quote: INR255.17 crores happened in fiscal '24-'25. Out of that, India was INR133 crores. And outside India was INR121 crores.

items.statement: Honeywell revenue split: IT accessories INR84 crores, air purifiers INR79 crores, audio INR50 crores, structured cabling INR41 crores
items.quote: So air purifier was close to INR79, audio was close to INR50 crores. IT accessories was INR84 crores, the highest category. And Honeywell SES was close to INR41 crores.

items.statement: License covers 37 countries; currently in 12-13, targeting 5-7 more; plan to expand Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Thailand, Indonesia
items.quote: We have a license to go to 37 countries. So when we expand the country, we need to invest in people first. So for us, it is who first and then the sales numbers.

items.statement: Asset-light model; no factories; contract manufacturing via 16-17 factories in China, 2 in Taiwan, 2-3 in India; certification and tooling expensed not capitalized
items.quote: We have been -- our Board has given us a guidance to be asset light. You know, there are many methods, but we are asset light. And we have around 16, 17 factories in China, 2 in Taiwan and 2, 3 in India.

items.statement: Working capital days increased from 32 to 39; target to bring down to 35 days; March sales INR212 crores drove higher receivables
items.quote: Number of days has increased from average 32 in the last financial year to 39. Okay. We will b e now constantly working on it and you know, on an average we feel that we should be around 35 days

items.statement: Operating cash flow turned positive: standalone INR14 crores, consolidated INR21.85 crores vs negative INR26.29 crores last year
items.quote: After a very long time if you are noted, oper ational cash flow has been positive. Last year, it was INR26.29 crores negative. This year, for standalone, it is almost INR14 crores positive. Consol, it is even better. It is INR21.85 crores

items.statement: Marketing spend increased from INR7 crores to INR23-24 crores; currently 14-15% of sales; will continue at 15-20% for 1-1.5 years then decline
items.quote: So I think I may and pardon, I may be slightly off my figure, but I think previous to that we had spent close to INR7 crores on the marketing and this year we had spent close to INR23 or INR24 crores on marketing.

items.statement: Employment cost increased by INR11 crores
items.quote: Another cost was the employment cost, around INR11 crores, okay.

items.statement: Air purifier adoption growing in Southeast Asia and Middle East; expected to become household necessity like water filters in 3-4 years
items.quote: And I think in the next three to four years, they should become like a water filter or a RO. They will become every household necessity. And this trend across Southeast Asia and across the Middle East, we are seeing.

items.statement: Air purifier market growing at 24-25% CAGR in India; current market INR2,200 crores
items.quote: For example, air purifier is going at a 24%-25% CAGR. So every four years, it should double, right? So from the current market just in India of INR2,200 crores, it should go to INR4,000 crores, INR4,500 crores, right?

items.statement: Honeywell license renewed every 5 years; auto-renews if minimum guarantee and royalty paid; next renewal Dec 2025; scored 4.8/5 on quarterly scorecard
items.quote: And we had just our meeting for the last quarter and our score was highest ever till date. We have got a 4.8. So that's their feedback mechanism and that's how Honeywell runs this, overall the licensing business.

items.statement: BIS certification for air purifiers expected Oct 2025; may require JV or contract manufacturing in India; influencing inventory decisions
items.quote: For example, there was no BIS on air purifiers. And this October, they are thinking of putting BIS on air purifiers. We have now 14 models of air purifiers. So obviously, our season also starts from end of September, October.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks: Trump tariffs, China supply chain dependence, India-Pakistan tensions affecting northern India logistics
items.quote: One is the geopolitical situation, right? Because of the Trump's tariff, that is the first part. Because most of our material is manufactured in China. And our cables and our audio, part of it is manufactured in India. But the supply chain is still with China.

items.statement: Audio products receiving poor Amazon reviews; sabotage suspected; investing in 2-3 marketing teams to improve
items.quote: And that's why we started our journey from being a low-to-mid-end brand to becoming from a mid-to-premium-end brand. On Amazon today, the case is that if you sell 100 units, then probably 10 people will give review.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25: Total income INR1,801.47 crores, EBITDA INR72.86 crores (4.04% margin), PAT INR53.11 crores
items.quote: Looking at consolidated full year results, the company's total income for FY '25 stood at INR1801.47 crores. The EBITDA for FY '25 stood at INR72.86 crores and the EBITDA margin for this period stood at 4.04%. The PA T for FY '25 came in at INR53.11 crores

items.statement: Q4 FY25: Total income INR408.72 crores, EBITDA INR19.08 crores (4.67% margin), PAT INR13.73 crores
items.quote: Looking at consolidated Q4 FY '25 results, the company reported a total income of INR408.72 crores. The quarterly EBITDA stood at INR19.08 crores and the EBITDA margin for this quarter stood at 4.67%. The PAT for the quarter is INR13.73 crores.

items.statement: Planning acquisitions with synergy (1+1=3); targeting innovative Indian brands for distribution; CyberPower in development stage
items.quote: And third is look at some potential where there's a synergy, where one plus one at least becomes three and not two, and try to acquire a certain kind of brand.

items.statement: Investing in people first for country expansion; employment cost up INR11 crores
items.quote: We need to expand from 13 countries to at least 5-7 more countries. We have a license to go to 37 countries. So when we expand the country, we need to invest in people first.

items.statement: International Honeywell sales INR121 crores (47%); higher margins abroad due to spending power; avoiding Egypt currency exposure
items.quote: Second advantage is you make a higher percentage of margin there because people spending power there is much more.

items.statement: Distribution business flat due to 15-20% annual price erosion; no new experiential brands added; selective brand partnerships
items.quote: The electronic industry as a whole, there is a price erosion of a product. So for example, a product is introduced in the month of January. By the end of December, the product would -- price erosion would be there for between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Enterprise business margin fell from 2.61% to 2.09%; Q1 FY25 lost INR200+ crores sales; shifting to Make in India brands on back-to-back basis
items.quote: enterprise busin ess is a very low margin business. And enterprise business, our philosophy is that not to block our any capital there. And it's a more of a back to back business

items.statement: FY26 NPK sales target of 280,000 metric tons, up from FY25, with capacity utilization expected to reach 80% from 70%
items.quote: We hope to sell about 280,000 metric ton of NPK, which will be up from last year. Because as we have already worked on de-bottlenecking some problems and the capacity utilization which was hovering in the range of 70%, we hope to touch 80% this year.

items.statement: Planning capacity expansion in fertilizer and backward production facilities via brownfield expansion, backward integration, and acquisitions for market, product, or logistics synergies
items.quote: We are in advanced stages of planning for capacity expansion in fertilizer as well as backward production facilities with options being explored both organically through brownfield expansion and backward integration and inorganically through acquisitions that could offer market product or logistics synergies.

items.statement: SSP operated at 95% utilization in FY25; NPK/DAP utilization improved from 45% to 70%; installed NPK/DAP capacity is 330,000 tons
items.quote: For the full year, SSP operated at 95% utilization, while while NPK/DAP utilization improved significantly, rising from 45% to 70%, reflecting our successful ramp-up and strong market demand.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected to remain stable around ₹5,500–₹6,000; EBITDA margin of 12% considered a comfortable base; 22-23% margin in FY23 was an aberration
items.quote: It will be stable, because the raw material prices have gone up and that is why the subsidies have been increased. So, EBITDA levels will be almost similar.

items.statement: Phosphatic fertilizer industry volumes grew 7.5% YoY in FY25 driven by NPK; company volumes grew 50% YoY, outpacing industry; NPK seen as long-term growth driver due to soil health and subsidy policy
items.quote: In FY25, Phosphatic Fertiliser industry volumes, excluding MOP, grew by 7.5% on YoY basis. Overall, the growth was driven by NPK grades. At the same time Krishana first time recorded much higher volume growth of 50% for FY25 and consistently outgrown the industry demand.

Sulphur prices have doubled over previous year, mainly attributable to volatile global demand. The governments increase in Kharif 2025 subsidy has largely offset the raw material price inflation, which helps maintaining price competitiveness and margin stability.

items.quote: Our debt-to-equity ratio improved, with net debt decreasing by 19%, reflecting our commitment to prudent financial management.

items.statement: QIP may be considered if opportunity arises and investors encourage; holding company OPIL increased stake to ~65% to minimize future dilution
items.quote: I can't comment at the moment. But if the opportunity arises and we get encouragement from investors, we will definitely consider it. There is huge potential in phosphatic fertilizers in India, so we can think about expansion, adding capacity, and doing many things.

items.quote: We have also ensured robust backward integration and secured a reliable supply of rock phosphate through long-term agreements with suppliers in Egypt, Jordan and domestically, which is a crucial strength in our subsidy driven business model.

items.quote: See, the government is already working on the nutrient based policy , which aims to ensure that hat only the exact nutrients required are provided to the soil. DAP, for instance, comes with a fixed composition of 18-46-0 — that's 18% nitrogen and 46% phosphorus. On the other hand, there are various types of NPK grades available in the country. The idea is to provide only what the soil specifically

items.statement: DEI FY25 challenged by weather, Middle East geopolitics, double Ramadan, FTI bankruptcy impacting East Africa, US operations closure
items.quote: Almost everything that had to go wrong went wrong from the weather not playing up in the first quarter to the challenges of the geopolitical situation in the Middle East that lasted nearly up to 2 quarters in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Corporate travel Q4 saw delayed decision-making due to tariff ambiguity, some new wins pushed to Q1 FY26
items.quote: There is also some impact of the tariffs that came in because there was a lot of ambiguity about what the impact of it on corporates. So, we saw a bit of a delayed decision-making. Also, some of the new wins that we had, which were likely to go live in the last quarter of FY '25 is actually moving on to the first quarter of FY 2026.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY25 income from operations grew 18%, PBT up 51% to INR 92 cr; FY25 revenue up 12% to INR 8,140 cr, PBT up 12% to INR 385 cr
items.value: Revenue INR 8,140 cr; PBT INR 385 cr
items.quote: Income from operations for the quarter ended Q4 of FY '25 grew 18%. And consequently, our profit before tax improved by a sharp 51%, moving from INR 61 crores to INR 92 crores. If I look at the full year numbers, our income from operations grew from INR 7,299 crores to INR 8,140 crores, registering a growth of 12%. Consequently, our profits before tax improved from INR 345 crores to INR 385 crores

items.statement: Sterling F&B revenue crossed INR 1,000M for first time, up 16% YoY
items.quote: Food and beverage crossed INR 1,000 million for the first time, growing at 16% Y-o-Y, driven by higher in-house guest dining participation, innovative restaurant concepts and increased revenues from weddings and from MICE.

items.statement: Thomas Cook India added ~21 distribution locations in FY25 (~12-13% of network), focusing on Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: Between SOTC and Thomas Cook, we've added close to about 11 locations during the quarter and for the full year, roughly about 21 new locations. That represents about roughly 12%, 13% of our overall distribution network.

items.statement: Decorative revenue flat in Q4 FY25; premium and urban grew, mass economy putty saw price erosion and discounting
items.quote: The good news as far as decorative paints is concerned is that we move towards a revenue which was flattish, led by premium and urban towns.

items.statement: Coatings business delivered double-digit growth in Q4 FY25 across marine, protective, industrial and powder coatings
items.quote: On our coatings business, we've seen double -digit growth. We continue to see very strong growth and that's because we are seeing rounded performance, whether it's marine and protective or our industrial coatings.

items.statement: EBITDA margin protected at 13.6% for FY25 despite growth project costs and competitive intensity
items.quote: I think for a number 2 player with 13.6% EBIT margin, in the year with a 7%, 8% market share, I think, is quite unheard of.

items.statement: Margin impact from B2B/B2C mix shift and carry-forward of last year's price drops; raw material sourcing efficiencies held
items.quote: I think this is largely driven by the B2B and B2C product mix. And we held our efficiencies in terms of the raw material sourcing and which is also largely protected.

items.statement: Price erosion of 15-20% by new entrants in mass economy, texture and putty segments; company chose not to participate actively
items.quote: I think -- and I think that there will be obviously a point of time when this will all start seeming to come back. So in the short run, there has been an impact. Obviously, when a lead player adds upwards of INR2,000 crores and a couple of these players have done well.

items.statement: Raw material situation: crude oil correction offset by rutile anti-dumping duty increase; strategy to retain profitability and reinvest for sustainable growth
items.quote: So we are again consistent with our strategy in terms of that last year, if I refresh on these things, we will retain the profitability of the business, and we will invest back into the business in terms of ensuring that a sustainable growth trajectory is back.

items.statement: Capex in normal trajectory with capacity augmentation for coating businesses and tinting machine placements; major announcement expected in a month
items.quote: We have a couple of growth projects which are running in terms of capacity augmentation for some of the coating businesses. And then it is also the mixing machine placements to enhance the numeric reach and the distribution breadth.

items.statement: Coatings order book remains reasonably strong; some project completions in May-June may cause timing bumps
items.quote: The order book is still reasonably st rong in our Coatings business. So yes, we will have a couple of bumps because there was a lot of projects that started last year, which ends in May, June.

items.statement: Added 3,200+ tinting machines (gross) in FY25, taking total to 22,000+; focus on productive outlets and tinting machine productivity up 2%
items.quote: We continue to add 3,000-plus machines. Look, Lakshmi, our definitions are a little more stringent because I look at productivity, I look at what we call the tinting machine productivity. And what I've seen is an uptick of 2%.

items.statement: 11 experiential stores opened in Q4 FY25 across North, East, West, South; dealer-owned shared investment model; plan to scale to hundreds
items.quote: Now 11 is a small number. So really honestly, for me to say the revenue will come out of it is not apt. Our idea is that over a period of time, we want to open hundreds of these stores.

items.statement: Construction chemicals ready to launch but delayed for margin accretive and superior product testing; not yet in numbers
items.quote: Even today, our numbers are without construction chemicals. We've not yet started our construction. We are ready to launch, but we've not entered it.

items.statement: B2B growth driven by disciplined pipeline execution, innovative products and complete solution approach rather than just selling paint cans
items.quote: Regarding the growth trajectory, what is driving the growth in the B2B business is absolutely the focus and the disciplined execution of the pipeline. And the teams are completely focused in terms of ensuring that the customer needs are met and through the innovative products and the services.

items.statement: Strategic review by parent Akzo Nobel N.V. expected to conclude by June end; company not directly involved due to regulations
items.quote: Look, as far as the strategic review is concerned, Rajiv has said, look, all I can say is there may be a time line given by the Global CEO that the transaction will be affected by the end of this quarter, by June end, right?

items.statement: Dividend distribution policy mandates 85% of retained profits; FY25 included one-time special dividend of INR 70 for 70th anniversary
items.quote: We have the dividend distribution policy, which clearly outlines and which is in the part of the website and which mandates 85% of the retained profits can be distributed as a part of the dividend. Of course, '24- '25 is the 70th year of Akzo Nobel being present in India. There, we took the -- we have distributed as a onetime special dividend in the month of November of INR70.

items.statement: Sales and marketing attrition not increased in last 6 months; challenge is recruitment dropouts, now being addressed
items.quote: No, the attritions haven't really gone up. I think the industry numbers are now more or less firming. Our challenge has not been in the attrition, but I'll also be honest in saying our challenge has been that in the recruitments we've had, we've had a bit of dropouts.

items.statement: Rural demand still muted; expect uptick post-monsoon around August-September as inflation cools and tax changes boost smaller town incomes
items.quote: I think it will start improving because inflationary -- inflation has come down to 3%, 3.6% as headline. We believe that, look, I do think that there's going to be a lot of other positive factors driving the economy and consumption. And with the tax change, which has got implemented in -- from April, I think the smaller town incomes will start going up.

items.statement: Industry growing at early single-digit; demand outlook positive for second half FY26; long-term industry growth to revert to 1-1.2x GDP
items.quote: I personally believe that, look, the second half should be better, unless there is an external event, which again, I cannot comment on. Yes. So really, I think the future outlook, I would say that if you take a year from now, and I would not be very pessimistic, I would say within -- after a year from now, I do see demand uptick.

items.statement: Decorative revenue expected to return to single-digit growth in FY26 with volume slightly above value growth due to price corrections Jan-Apr
items.quote: I think decorative is going to look at least getting back to a -- for the fiscal getting back to a single-digit growth in terms of revenue and the volume should be a shade above.

items.statement: Coatings business structurally poised to continue double-digit growth despite near-term project timing bumps
items.quote: I think structurally, we are poised to continue to grow double digit.

items.statement: Committed to delivering superlative operating working capital performance by churning cash efficiently
items.quote: And we are committed to deliver the superlative performance in terms of th e operating working capital by churning the cash efficiently, which is also reflected in the results which we shared.

items.statement: Strategic review timeline uncertainty; competitive intensity in mass economy segments; rural demand recovery timing uncertain
items.quote: I think the uncertainty -- I think the dark clouds have moved out. I think the sun is shining bright again. So let's hope -- I'll keep my fingers crossed.

items.statement: Powder Coating business classified as held for sale (INR 329 cr); separation delayed by two months; segment numbers not separable until completion
items.quote: Until the point of time that Akzo Nobel N.V. completes the elements of what the powder coating separation is, which is why we've taken two months extension, we would not be in a position to give you operations-wise numbers.

items.statement: P&L growth of 5% in FY25 is on like-to-like basis; IndAS 105 assets held for sale accounting only affects balance sheet classification
items.quote: I think the IndAS 105, the assets held for sale accounting has not triggered anything in the P&L portion. And it's only reflected in the balance sheet where we classify the fixed assets into th e current assets. So the P&L disclosure of 5% growth is on a like-to-like

items.statement: FY26 pen sales target of 30-35 million units, ~70% growth over FY25
items.quote: I believe this year -- I can tell you this year, we're looking at selling close to somewhere between -- somewhere around 30 million to 35 million pens this year.

items.statement: Medical device business to reach ~30% of revenue over next few years
items.quote: We anticipate that our medical device business will comprise about 30% of our revenues over the next few years, enhancing value and profitability.

items.statement: INR150 crore capex for pen capacity expansion in FY26, total capex INR180-185 crore
items.quote: The overall capex, which we will end up doing will be about INR180 crores, INR185 crores. Predominantly INR150 crores is going into Pharma for capacity expansion in terms of our pen capacity.

items.statement: Adding 40-50 million pens/year capacity over 18-24 months, total capacity reaching 80-90 million
items.quote: We're expanding our pen manufacturing capacity to add another 40 million to 50 million pens per year across primarily 2 platforms, both for servicing the growing demand of GLP-1.

items.statement: 8 contracts signed for pen/auto-injectors primarily for GLP-1s, commercial semaglutide supplies starting FY26
items.quote: During the last year, we signed 8 contracts with different customers for pen injectors or auto injectors, primarily for GLP-1s, but also for some other therapies.

items.statement: 75-80% of 55-60 GLP-1s in development are injectable, oral share limited to ~20%
items.quote: Even out of these 55 to 60, we see that 75% to 80% are injectable form and 20% to 25% in oral form.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin 25.1%, FY25 22.7% (+350bps), year-on-year margin improvement expected
items.quote: Do we feel that if we execute the plan that we will have better margins? I mean the short answer is, yes. That's the ambition, and that's also what we think should happen.

items.statement: Healthcare segment grew 53% to INR165 crore (21% of revenue), IP-led pens driving growth
items.quote: In FY '25, our revenues from Healthcare segment have grown by 53% on a year-on-year basis to INR165 crores, 21% of our top line.

items.statement: 2 new IP-led pen platform customers (Neo, Toby), 2 teriparatide commercial launches expected FY26
items.quote: We have received commercial orders for teriparatide. So we are going to produce and ship. Now when it actually gets launched, I'm fingers crossed, any time over the next 3 to 4 months, hopefully, maybe 5 months.

items.statement: Consumer segment: 2 new global retail chains, 2 new FMCG products, 2 plastics + 3 carbon steel products with home furnishings customer
items.quote: Over FY '25, we received new business from 2 global retail chains for which supplies have started in this quarter.

items.statement: Pen capacity utilization ~40-44%, asset turnover target 1.5-2x on pharma gross block
items.quote: Machine utilization rate was around 44% in Q4 FY '25 and 40% in FY '25. We expect this to increase in the coming years, and we expect to increase utilization levels over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Inventory days increased due to 3-month raw material stocking for supplier shutdown and pharma scale-up prep
items.quote: There was a plant maintenance shutdown by one of our principal supplier. And that's a large quantity of material, which we use, so we've basically requested that if we can take on the next 3 months requirement.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.4x, long-term debt-to-equity 0.07x as of March 2025
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity stands at 0.4x while our long-term debt-to-equity stands at 0.07x as on 31 March 2025.

items.statement: No outstanding regulatory queries in Canada/Brazil, present with 2+ players in both markets
items.quote: We don't have any outstanding queries that we have to address, and we are present in both markets with at least 2 players.

items.statement: Customer concentration risk: 3-4 customers for FY26 pen growth, none have approval yet
items.quote: So, I think customer concentration, that entire volume would be totally divided by 3 to 4 customers at the equal risk. None of the 3 to 4 have approval right now.

items.statement: Next-gen GLP-1 device: non-priming, fixed-dose, pull-push mechanism with dose counter, targeting innovator pharma
items.quote: We have now developed a device that will be non-priming, fixed dose, activated by a simple pull and push mechanism instead of dialing, along with the dose counter to show the remaining pens in the device.

items.statement: Potential medium-large capex for consumer electronics in next 2 years if business plans finalize
items.quote: Short answer is, yes. We -- if we can come to some sort of a conclusion on a business plan with the customers that we are speaking with, we will be looking at capex. And we will be looking at potentially at least medium to large capex in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Pharma gross block to reach INR350-375 crore after FY26 capex, 70-30 pen vs auto-injector capacity split
items.quote: Pharma gross block will be probably somewhere in the region of about INR 370 crores to INR 375 crores.

items.statement: No crude benefit for margin improvement; driven by healthcare scale-up and better utilization
items.quote: Crude, no, I don't think there's has been any, no crude benefit. Harsh Shah: Then does this -- yes. Amit Sanghvi: Mostly On account of scale up of health care and higher revenue and better utilization

items.statement: Ypsomed makes 100-150M devices/year; Shaily yet to prove scale-up but has development advantage on pen injectors
items.quote: Ypsomed already manufactures maybe 100 million, 150 million devices a year. So it would be wise for me to say that we're as -- I guess they were as good as them, we've yet to prove it, right?

items.statement: Insulin pen growth expected 20-30% annually, focused on large players in regulated markets
items.quote: I think considering an ave rage of maybe 20%, 25%, 30% growth on the insulin side

items.statement: Applicator project validation H1 FY26, 4-6 months sales contribution in FY26
items.quote: See, applicator is going to probably get validated, I think in the first half of Q2, potentially end of Q2 and then we should see at least somewhere around 4 to 6 months of sales for the applicator in the current year.

items.statement: Exports 78% of FY25 revenue, 80% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Exports during Q4 FY '25 and FY '25 stood at 80% and 78%, respectively, of total revenue.

items.statement: FY25 polymer processing 24,932 tons vs 22,098 tons FY24 (+13%)
items.quote: For FY '25, we processed 24,932 tons of polymers as against 22,098 tons in FY '24.

items.statement: No vertical integration into fill/finish or API planned long-term; may add final assembly for clinical support
items.quote: I don't think we should -- short term, there is benefit. I don't deny that. There is certainly short-term benefit. You can make a limited business case out of it, saying that, okay, we'll support clinical development.

items.statement: Tariff situation evolving, no disruption seen in Q1 FY26, orders at same pace
items.quote: No. We have not seen any disruption. It's been -- orders have been going on at same pace. There have not been any changes on anything.

items.statement: Business development team traveling, limited visibility on exact pen volume split
items.quote: Unfortunately, like I said, since 2 weeks, my business development team has been traveling, we haven't had a chance to catch up.

items.statement: Capex guidance for next year is Rs 1,200-1,300 crore, largely for EV manufacturing facility, product development and new things
items.quote: So I take the CAPEX to be between Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores next year, which is largely towards investment in EV manufacturing facility, product development, and new things.

items.statement: Urban market growth was muted last year but expected to recover with income tax cuts; rural market continues to grow; premiumization trend continues
items.quote: Last year also, the rural market has been very good, and the urban market growth has not been so good. It was slightly muted. This year, with the tax cut, especially on the income tax cut, we expect the urban growth will start coming up back.

items.statement: Royal Enfield gross margin down ~19 bps QoQ due to 30 bps model/variant mix, 20 bps commodity prices, 20 bps inventory provisions for old bikes
items.quote: So effectively that is what is causing the impact of, I think approximately 19 bps versus Q3 of this year.

items.statement: VECV EBITDA margin improved to 10.5% in Q4 from 7.8% a year ago; full year margin 8.8% vs 7.8% prior year
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 10.5% and at 8.8% for the Financial Year '25. And as you can see, the EBITDA margin has significantly improved from 7.8% last year Quarter 4 to 10.5% in this current Quarter 4.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 280,801 motorcycles in Q4 (+23.2% YoY) and 1,002,893 in FY25 (+10% YoY); domestic 902,757 units (+8%), exports 100,136 units (+29.7%)
items.quote: In the past financial year, we sold about 1 million plus motorcycles. It is almost 1,002,893 motorcycles to be precise marking a 10% increase over the previous year.

items.statement: VECV sold 28,675 units in Q4 and 90,161 units in FY25 (best ever); revenue Rs 7,139 crore in Q4 (+13.8% YoY) and Rs 23,548 crore in FY25 (+7.7% YoY)
items.quote: We had a robust sales performance of 28,675 units in Quarter 4 of FY25 and 90,161 units in Financial Year '25, our best ever performance.

items.statement: Royal Enfield capacity ~1.2 million units; Cheyyar plant supports backend operations (chrome plating, powder coating) for Vallam and Oragadam; modular expansion planned as needed
items.quote: Our capacity as you mentioned is about 1.2 million with the plants and we also have Cheyyar where we protect the land and we also have the sheds ready. And all our manufacturing facilities are done in a modular way.

items.statement: Brazil CKD capacity being expanded via third parties; evaluating own CKD investment given strong demand (22,000+ units last year, #3 market position)
items.quote: Now, we have added one more party also so that the year's requirement is done and parallelly we are also evaluating what does it Eicher Motors Limited May 14, 2025 mean for us to be of our own and what is the kind of an investment and what is the capacity which we have to

items.statement: Royal Enfield took 1.15% price increase on select models in April 2025 for OBD2B transition and new year; passed on cost increases but added more value than margin
items.quote: We have taken about 1.15% increase in some select models in April.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility (steel, aluminum) impacted gross margin by ~20 bps QoQ; waiting and watching for further impact
items.quote: We have about a 20 bps impact of higher commodity prices in Steel and Aluminum.

items.statement: Royal Enfield launched 6 new motorcycles in FY25 including Bear 650, Guerrilla 450, Classic 650, Goan Classic 350; Hunter refresh adds assist clutch, LED headlight, USB charger, new colors targeting younger buyers
items.quote: We introduced 6 new motorcycles in the past year, which strengthened our product portfolio to meet the diverse needs of our customers' right here in India and across the globe.

items.statement: Royal Enfield customer profile shifting younger: ~30%+ below 25 years, ~60-65% below 35 years; first-time buyers up to ~19%; finance penetration ~61%
items.quote: Around 30 plus percentage of the consumers are below 25 years as of now overall aggregated level, but there is product level we have to see and another about 60%-65% will be about below 35 years of age.

items.statement: Top 20 cities contribute 18-22% of Royal Enfield volumes
items.quote: Around the top 20 cities will be about 18%-20%, 22%. That is the range.

items.statement: VECV became #1 in Light & Medium Duty trucks with 36% market share (5-18 tons); Heavy Duty truck market share 9.1% (Eicher) / 9.7% (incl. Volvo); Bus sales highest ever
items.quote: We became #1 in Light & Medium Duty trucks market share. We have now 36% market share in Light & Medium Duty trucks, which is 5-18 tons, and we are #1 in the market now.

items.statement: Royal Enfield exports crossed 100,000 units for first time; #1 in UK mid-weight, #2 in Argentina, #3 in Brazil; Bangladesh new market showing good signs; US inventory built pre-tariff to cover riding season
items.quote: International, this is the first year we also crossed about 100,000 motorcycles. It is backed by solid retail in all the markets.

items.statement: Leadership changes: Siddhartha Lal became Executive Chairman; Vinod Aggarwal became Vice Chairman of Eicher Motors while remaining MD & CEO of VECV; B. Govindarajan became Managing Director of Eicher Motors; new directors added to board
items.quote: Siddhartha was the MD & CEO of Eicher Motors, has taken over as an Executive Chairman of Eicher Motors and Vinod - MD and CEO of VECV Commercial Vehicle business is now, apart from the MD & CEO of Commercial Vehicle, he is the Vice Chairman of Eicher Motors Board, and I took a larger role as a Managing Director of Eicher Motors.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio improved to ~40% from historical 33-35%; Board will evaluate right payout ratio based on performance and cash situation going forward
items.quote: We had been consistently paying out around 33%-35% sort of the dividend payout and this year, we have improved it depending on our better performance and going forward also I think we will be open at looking at, but the right payout ratio based on the performance and the cash situation.

items.statement: Royal Enfield domestic market share ~88% in mid-weight segment; international retail strong across markets
items.quote: We grew the market and the growth primarily came from the focus of delivering the pure motorcycling experience to the customers with the motorcycles, which are very differentiated and look wise and fit and feel wise, it has to be very differentiated and that is what we have been consistently working on, which has really helped us to grow the market where we are almost about 88% market share in the

items.statement: VECV EBITDA margin 8.8% for FY25 vs 7.8% prior year; Q4 margin 10.5% vs 7.8% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 10.5% and at 8.8% for the Financial Year '25.

items.statement: International markets cautiously optimistic; tariff uncertainty in US being monitored; sentiment shocks (e.g., war) can temporarily dampen CV demand
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic about the international market, but our retail has been good, our interest in products has been good.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sustainability: motorcycles >97% recyclable; plants 86% renewable electricity; net water positive 2.6x; zero waste to landfill target
items.quote: Our motorcycles are designed for more than 97% recyclability and reusability. Our plants now consume about 86% of electricity from renewable sources, and our net water is positive to the tune of 2.6x.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 same-store sales growth was 0.7%, adjusted for leap year impact 1.7%
items.quote: Our same- store sales growth stood at 0.7%, and adjusted SSSG, excluding the leap year impac t, was 1.7% in Q4

items.statement: Eating out frequency in March quarter unchanged from previous year; soft demand and stagnant consumption trends across markets
items.quote: Eating out frequency during the March quarter remained largely unchanged from the previous year.

items.statement: Vision 2027 targets 580 to 630 restaurants
items.quote: We continue to move towards achieving our Vision 2027, targeting 580 to 630 restaurants.

items.statement: FY25 expansion funded largely through internal accruals; net debt stable at INR90 crores
items.quote: Furthermore, I would like to highlight that despite a challenging year, we were able to fund our expansion largely through our internal accruals as seen in our net de bt position, which remains stable versus last year at INR90 crores

items.statement: Added 47 new restaurants in FY25, in line with guidance of 45-50; total 438 restaurants across 69 cities as of March 31
items.quote: For the full-year, we added 47 stores, in line with our guidance of 45 to 50 for FY '25.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin around 70%; restaurant operating margin and operating EBITDA margin dipped 30 bps and 50 bps YoY due to operating deleverage
items.quote: Our Q4 margin remained broadly in line with our guidance, that is around 70% gross margin.

items.statement: Commodity inflation increased substantially in H2 FY25 for coffee, oil, cocoa; managed through product mix, pricing, cost efficiency
items.quote: Certain commodities inflation, actually increased substantially in the last half of the year, likes of coffee, likes of oil, likes of cocoa, etc., have gone through the roof.

items.statement: Growth driven by volume from value offerings (McSaver Meals, McSavers+ Combos); Korean range and Mango Burst range launched as LTOs
items.quote: So largely, almost all our growth is coming on the volume -- on the back of volume, not necessarily value, primarily because of the value offering, which we have given

items.statement: Digital sales 75% of total sales in Q4; 41 million cumulative app downloads, 3 million MAUs
items.quote: In Q4, digital sales sustained a strong growth, accounting to almost 75% of our total sales, driven by self-ordering kiosks and our mobile apps.

items.statement: Inventory increase per restaurant due to seasonality and strategic buying; will average out over the year
items.quote: No, it's more of a seasonality effect, and there could be some strategic buying, etc., that would have happened.

items.statement: Net debt to equity 0.15x as of March 31; net debt stable at INR90 crores vs last year
items.quote: Our net debt to equity stands at a comfortable 0.15x as of March 31.

items.statement: Store staff wage inflation typically 5% to 10% YoY; labor managed through productivity optimization
items.quote: It's typically wage rate anywhere between 5% t o 10% is what the increase happens year -on-year, and that continues to be our plan even this year

items.statement: Competitive intensity grows the market; Westlife stands out on offerings and performance; no unusual consolidation seen
items.quote: In terms of consolidation, I mean, you will see what you normally see in the news. I don't see anything different in terms of how it's been operating.

items.statement: Informal eat-out segment under pressure for 1-2 years; structural headwind for food retail sector
items.quote: I think the informal eat-out has been under a lot of pressure, which once upon a time used to have a significant amount of growth.

items.statement: Committed to mid- to high single-digit SSSG over next couple of years per Vision 2027; seeing green shoots and sequential improvement
items.quote: We are quite confident that with our plans, we remain committed towards Vision 2027, which implies that we plan to get back to that mid- to high single-digit SSSG over the next couple of years.

items.statement: South India (Hyderabad, Chennai, Bangalore) and infrastructure-led white spaces (highways, metros, airports) key focus for store additions
items.quote: We see a lot of potential in South, where we are under-indexed and hence, cities like Hyderabad, Chennai, Bangalore, as well as smaller towns will see a healthy addition.

items.statement: On-premise business grew 8% YoY in Q4, outpacing off-premise at 5% YoY; off-premise 43% of total sales
items.quote: In Q4, our on-premise business grew by 8% Y-o-Y, outpacing the off-premise business, which increased 5% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: FY25 sales, EBITDA, cash PAT at INR24.9B, INR3.3B, INR1.9B respectively; 3-year CAGR 16%, 17%, 14%
items.quote: For the full-year FY '25, our sales, EBITDA and cash PAT stood at INR24.9 billion, INR3.3 billion and INR1.9 billion, respectively, growing by 16%, 17% and 14% on a 3-year CAGR basis.

items.statement: Achieved top ranking in India and 5th globally in restaurant sector in S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment
items.quote: Westlife Foodworld has achieved the top ranking in India and 5th place globally in the restaurant sector in S&P Global's Corporate Sustainability Assessment.

items.statement: Korean range launched as limited-time offering at entry price INR69; no plan to make it permanent
items.quote: Korean is an LTO. At this point in time, it continues to be an LTO, which is limited time offering in our menu. There is no plan per se to make it as a permanent offering in our menu.

items.statement: Off-premise growth muted vs peers; over-indexed on Swiggy/Zomato; expanding own channel to compensate
items.quote: Our business was relatively over-indexed towards both the operators of Swiggy and Zomato. And we've seen some amount of -- the growth trajectory has reduced for sure in both the channels.

items.statement: New stores take 2-3 years typically to reach system-level sales; proportion of new stores in mix similar to past 2-3 years
items.quote: Normally, we don't give any breakups. Obviously, we've stated in the past also that sometimes it takes 2 years to 3 years typically for a store to become at a system

items.statement: Cash profit after tax INR469M (7.8% of sales) in Q4; actively pursuing operational efficiencies to enhance return ratios
items.quote: Cash profit after tax reached INR469 million or 7.8% of sales. We're actively pursuing operational efficiencies to enhance our return ratios.

items.statement: Store addition run rate may need to accelerate from ~41 net additions/year to 50+ over next 11 quarters to meet Vision 2027 lower end
items.quote: We've continued to hold on to our guidance in terms of Vision 2027, which is 580 to 630 restaurants by 2027.

items.statement: Input costs stable in Q4; gross margin maintained at ~70%
items.quote: Input costs were stable.

items.statement: Demand environment picking up slowly and gradually; sequential improvement seen in last couple of months of Q4
items.quote: We do feel that the demand environment is picking up, not in a very accelerated way, but in a slow and gradual manner.

items.statement: Other income increase in Q4 due to annual reconciliations at book close; business as usual

items.statement: Antioxidant portfolio expanded with novel lubricant additive developed by R&D team
items.quote: Our R&D te am has been instrumental in developing a novel antioxidant for lubricant additives broadening our portfolio and enhancing our value proposition

items.statement: VOPL go-to-market leverages existing B2B relationships across US, Europe, China, India with some new customers
items.quote: So VOPL is a mix of different products across different applications. MEHQ is used in polymers, Guaiacol is used in pharmaceutical, TAA used in agriculture, PTAP is used in resins industries, TAA is again used in pharmaceuticals. So some of these customers are our existing customers, which we are supplying other products, some may be new. So it is, again, a B2B sales spread across countries. We ar

items.quote: Other major products that we sell in domestic, it may be partly of the butyl phenols, which are also the demand has increased and Isobutylene which is used in cypermethrin. So all these three products are actually our share of domestic sales is increasing slightly year-on-year and export has decreased I believe from 70% to 60%. Kaviraj Devaraj: Now it's only 55%. Vinati Mutreja: 55%, 3 years, 4 ye

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin of 26-27% for specialty chemical B2B manufacturing business
items.quote: No, I think over a long term pe riod of 3 to 5 years, 26% - 27% EBITDA margin is what is sustainable in a B2B manufacturing business specialty chemical

items.statement: Antioxidant pricing competitive with Chinese and Singapore imports but major customers prefer domestic suppliers for annual/biannual contracts
items.quote: Yes. So there is antioxidant, there is imports coming from China, from Singapore. And…but we are also able to…now our products have been accepted by this thing qualified by all the major customers and the major customers are very keen to work with our domestic suppliers. Hence, we think that going forward, the contracts, the annual contract, biannual contract should come. We're in a better positio

items.statement: ATBS global market share steady at 60-65% reinforcing industry leadership
items.quote: Our global market share in ATBS remained steady at 60 -65%, reinforcing our leadership position in the industry.

items.statement: VOPL expected to achieve above 1:1 asset turnover at full utilization of INR500 crores capex
items.quote: Yes. On full utilization, it will be above 1:1. That's right.

items.statement: VOPL incurred INR12 crores depreciation and INR4 crores loss in FY25 during teething phase
items.value: INR12 crores depreciation and INR4 crores
items.quote: In VOPL FY25 there is a loss. In that INR12 crores is the depreciation and INR4 crores. So, that production and expenses in VOPL you can see the consolidated and standalone difference.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided flat; FY27 onwards 10-15% growth expected
items.quote: we expect FY'26, there will be a stable growth and from FY'27 onwards, we expect around 10% to 15% growth.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 13-14%
items.quote: Guidance wise, we maintain like that only because there will be a of mix of the projects executed and also 13% to 14% is we expect to do.

items.statement: Order book Rs 15,217 cr plus Rs 2,500 cr L1/LOA; FY25 inflow Rs 550 cr; FY26 target Rs 10,000 cr
items.quote: As of March 31st, 2025, our order book stands at Rs. 15,217 crores excluding L1 with 66% of that coming from hydropower, 23% from irrigation, 8% from tunneling and the remaining from other sectors. This excludes projects of around Rs. 1200 crores which are L1 and projects of Rs. 1300 crore which have been received recently in Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target Rs 10,000 cr; bid pipeline Rs 40,000-50,000 cr with 15-20% success ratio
items.quote: Our target is to bid for around Rs. 40,000- Rs. 50,000 crores and our success ratio is generally between 15%-20%.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 EBITDA margin 14.4% vs 15.19% FY24; Q4 FY25 margin 13.55%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA is Rs. 733 crores as compared to Rs. 690 crores. EBITDA margin is 14.4% as compared to 15.19% in FY'24.

items.statement: Quarterly margin variation due to work mix; long-term average 13-14%
items.quote: See it depends upon what type of work has been executed during the quarter so we always say that our average margins are between 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt Rs 1,600 cr vs Rs 1,886 cr FY24; debt/equity 0.42 vs 0.6; term debt Rs 601 cr, WC debt Rs 1,000 cr
items.quote: The consolidated gross debt is Rs. 1600 crores compared to Rs. 1886 crores at end of FY'24. In this quarter, we have replaced some client advances of Rs. 70 crores with bank debt.

items.statement: Term debt to reduce ~Rs 200 cr in FY26; WC debt may rise; overall debt stable; interest cost flat
items.quote: The term debt we see going down by around Rs. 200 crores, but then working capital debt may go up. Overall we don't see the debt going up to a very large extent.

items.statement: Net working capital ~110 days after adjusting land stock and arbitration awards
items.quote: In working capital days, the net working capital after adjusting for stock of land, arbitration awards is around 110 days.

items.statement: Capacity building gradual; employee base 4,500 vs 1,500 five years ago; gross block Rs 1,100 cr
items.quote: See we have almost 4500 employees today which were at 1500 5 years back and we have a gross block of around Rs. 1,100 crores.

items.statement: Cost escalation pass-through in contracts protects margins
items.quote: Because pass through, there is an escalation of cost, that is a pass through for us. So that is why we don't see that the impact will come on us.

items.statement: Indus Water Treaty suspension to expedite hydropower project clearances and launch
items.quote: With the suspension of the treaty, the government will also look at accelerating works on existing projects and exploring ways to maximize its hydropower potential and improve the storage of water by constructing larger dams.

items.statement: Hydropower civil construction ~Rs 5 cr/MW; pumped storage ~Rs 3-4 cr/MW
items.quote: So in terms of value, hydropower civil construction works is almost Rs. 5 crores per megawatt and for pumped storage, it is between Rs. 3 to Rs. 4 crores per megawatt.

items.statement: 30 GW pumped storage and 30 GW hydro projects for bidding in next 2-3 years
items.quote: So around 30 gigawatt projects were coming for bidding in near future, both from private and public sector.

items.statement: New project funding via client advances (5-10% of value) and working capital debt
items.quote: Generally we have to do mobilization expenses. So we fund it through working capital debt or client advances which is between 5% to 10% of the project value.

items.statement: Arbitration awards: Rs 750 cr awarded, Rs 2,250 cr under arbitration; target Rs 200 cr/year realization
items.quote: So we have around Rs. 750 crores of awarded claims and another Rs. 2,250 crores of which are under arbitration getting into arbitration to over Rs. 3000.

items.statement: Land bank valued Rs 800-1,000 cr; partial monetization over 2-3 years; proceeds to term loan repayment
items.quote: It's between Rs. 800 to Rs. 1000 crores.

items.statement: Border tensions may impact labor availability if prolonged
items.quote: So see there if it elongates for a longer period, then you will get some impact.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow subdued due to elections; FY26 started with Rs 1,318 cr CIDCO dam LOA and 240 MW NEEPCO L1
items.quote: We managed to get projects worth of Rs. 550 crores during the year. However, FY'26 has started a positive note and we have received two projects. Number one, Rs. 1,318 crore for which LOA has also been received, which is for the construction of Kondhane Dam located in Karjat, Maharashtra from CIDCO and the other 240 megawatt Heo hydropower project located in Arunachal Pradesh from NEEPCO for which

items.statement: Vivad Se Vishwas scheme over; no further exceptional provisions in FY26
items.quote: The scheme was only up to this year. So that scheme is over now. We don't see any further thing coming for this.

items.statement: Employee cost up 8-9% for FY25; Q4 spike due to new hiring
items.quote: If you see the overall year, it is only increase of around 8%-9%. So, year-on-year basis, the number is similar. It is only some cost would have come in this quarter because of some new hiring.

items.statement: Kondhane Dam mobilization ~6 months before revenue recognition
items.quote: Generally, a project takes around 6 months for mobilization, post which the revenues will start.

items.statement: Pumped storage competitors similar to hydro; private players Adani, JSW also bidding
items.quote: Competitors are also similar to hydro.

items.statement: Not bidding in Bhutan yet; may evaluate
items.quote: We have not bidded yet. We may look into it.

items.statement: Promoter pledge 89%; talks with lenders to start after results
items.quote: So now once the results are out, maybe this quarter or after one quarter we will start talking to the lender.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue growth expected at 20-30% YoY; full-year operational EBITDA margin guided at 11-13%
items.quote: We expect anywhere between 20% to 30% growth in Q1. We have already had good growth in April that continues into May and hopefully we will end up with a very strong quarter in Q1.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin guided at 11-13% for FY26, consistent with last 3-4 years
items.quote: The operational EBITDA will continue to be in the range of 11% to 13%, which we have adhered to in the last 3-4 years. The guidance is in the same range this year as well.

items.statement: Normal monsoon forecasted, expecting healthy Kharif demand for small farm machines and tractors; tractor growth may lag industry due to limited high-HP presence
items.quote: We expect a healthy demand during the Kharif season. We foresee growth for small farm machines in key states. We also expect growth in the tractor industry. However, given our limited presence in the higher horsepower space, we will have growth but may not be at the same rate as the industry growth.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operational EBITDA margin at 13.39%; full-year margin declined to 11.17% from 12.83% due to R&D and product development investments
items.quote: The operational EBITDA, which is dropped by about Rs. 13 crores primarily, due to the increased expense on resourcing for the future, which is where we have incurred these additional expenses in terms of our R&D capacity and product development capacity which we have invested in last year.

items.statement: Power Weeder volumes grew 63% to 7,458 units in FY25; Power Reaper grew 22% to 2,403 units; Precision Components external business grew 71%
items.quote: We have been able to grow the Power Weeder business the way we had evinced that it will grow, growth of 63%. Similarly, the Power Reaper business which we started has also grown 22%. The Precision Component division started focusing on external business from last year and it has grown by about 71%.

items.statement: Invested in R&D capacity and product development capabilities on both OpEx and CAPEX in FY25; PAT impact ~Rs 5 crore
items.quote: Despite the increased investments into R&D and our product development capabilities, both on OpEx and CAPEX side, the PAT effect is only about Rs. 5 crores, current year at about Rs. 70 crores and previous year was Rs. 75 crores.

items.statement: Tractor capacity 36,000-40,000 units (1 shift); Power Tiller 60,000-70,000 (1 shift), up to 1 lakh with shifts; Power Weeder ~10,000 units India-made capacity
items.quote: Tractors with the one shift operation, we can go up to 36,000 to 40,000 tractors. On power tiller, we can go up to 60,000 to 70,000 tillers without increasing shift. And with shift, we can go up to 1 lakh. On power weeders, currently we have set up a capacity to do about making India weeders up to about 10,000.

items.statement: Product mix shift toward Northeast/Eastern states (lower pricing due to subsidy-linked pricing) offset raw material benefit, pressuring gross margin in Q4
items.quote: It is primarily because of the product mix. We have got the benefit of commodity movement. That definitely has come in, but the product mix has changed and also the geographical distribution. To be specific, the sales in the Northeast and Assam and Orissa was higher in Q4 compared to sales in the South, which kind of impacted the pricing and hence the overall contribution.
