items.statement: Northern market (One VST) grew from ~200 to ~900 Power Tillers and ~1,000 Power Weeders in FY25; financing 70-80% in North vs ~10% retail finance in South, targeting 15-20% this year
items.quote: from about 200 power tillers in FY '24, in the last year we have sold close to 900 power tillers. So, it's just the first year of the northern market. So, we are getting tremendous response. So, we will continue to build on it. And this gives us a lot of encouragement, to answer your question. And this we have seen both in Power Tiller, we have seen in Power Weeder, which is again close to 1,000 n

items.statement: Tractor exports fell to 1,411 units in FY25 from 1,680 due to European demand weakness; entered Cyprus, Czech Republic, Russia, Angola, Turkey, Mali; logistics challenges persist
items.quote: In tractor exports, while we were at par till Q3, we had a drop in terms of our dispatches into the export market due to lower demand compared to the previous year. So, we did 260 tractors in Q4, FY '25 vis-a-vis 525 the previous year. Hence, the shortfall in Q4 resulted in 1,411 tractors in FY '25 vis-a-vis 1,680 previous year.

items.statement: SPARSH subsidy payment mechanism implemented in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Odisha; Northeast/Assam pending, causing cash flow disruption in Jan-Feb
items.quote: In three states, it is completed. In Tamil Nadu, it is completed. In Karnataka, it is completed. And in Orissa, more or less, it is completed. In the Northeast, it is still not done. So, there is a bit of uncertainty in the Northeast.

items.statement: Receivables days improved from 88 (Q2) to 75 (Q4) after SPARSH-related dealer support; targeting 50-60 days
items.quote: Arjun, we had 59 days outstanding the previous year. We are at currently 75 days. But if you look at Quarter 3, we were at 81 days and in Quarter 2, I think we were at around 88 days. So, from 88, we have brought it down to 75.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities; Kobashi JV for blades likely dropped due to insufficient scale; expect at least one deal in next two years
items.quote: Kobashi, we were contemplating a JV. We didn't announce it in terms of a JV. We may drop that JV plan because we didn't see the scale-up happening to the extent that VST's growth ambitions are in this particular segment. So, we did a lot of work, and finally we may decide to drop that project.

items.statement: Power Tiler domestic volumes grew 2.24% to 37,297 units in FY25; Tractor domestic grew 4.53%; Power Weeder 7,458 units (+63%)
items.quote: in the full year, while we were lagging till Q3 end, we were able to reverse the situation and get down to the growth path in Q4, and we ended with a 2.24% growth at 37,297 nos vis-à-vis last year of 36,480

items.statement: Launching SCORE (between tiller and tractor), electric Power Tiller and Power Weeder in FY26; global tractor platform (3 platforms, 8 models, 16 variants) for India/Europe/US in FY27
items.quote: We had announced a product between tiller and tractors which we will be launching soon in the Indian market which is going to be called SCORE. And we will also be entering the Power Tiller and Power Weeder both on electric platforms which will also be launched in FY '26.

items.statement: Zetor brand well-recognized in North India vs VST in South/West; targeting ~1,500 units of 40-50 HP Zetor tractors; upgrades in H2 FY26 based on dealer feedback
items.quote: We will be close to that number. We don't give numbers on VST Zetor for obvious reasons. But we are around that number only. We are not changing that.

items.statement: US tariffs on Monarch tractor chassis imports from India; business unlikely in Q1 FY26; China/Mexico tariffs may have bigger impact on Monarch
items.quote: However, definitely there is a tariff effect because that will play out as we can see that it is not Monarch not only imports from India, but it also imports from China as well as Mexico. So, they may have more impact due to China and Mexico rather than India. So, I think it didn't get sorted out as we see that the Chinese tariff is under negotiation and is kind of getting into a deal situation. S

items.statement: Stage-V emission norms to increase higher HP tractor costs by 25-30%, anticipating shift to lower HP 4WD tractors
items.quote: Higher horsepower will continue to sell, but Stage-V creates a higher cost. Almost 25% to 30% cost is what is being estimated, which will go up. So, the higher horsepower tractors will become very expensive. We anticipate a shift towards lower HP four-wheel drive tractors to meet the same applications.

items.statement: Distribution business added 56% more distributors; digital distribution model scaling with electric pumps (Rs 10-15 crore revenue)
items.quote: Distribution business, we have appointed new distributors, and it's up by almost 56% in terms of our distribution capability.

items.statement: Targets asset growth north of 12% for FY26, hopes to beat by 3-4 percentage points
items.quote: We think that our growth, we will be growing faster than last year. The environment is an important imponderable that we are not entirely sure as to how it is going to behave. But I think that, 20 %-30%, maybe 40% increase in our growth rate is feasible, and we now have the tools to get there. So I would say that we would be north of 12 % growth assets for the year.

items.statement: Targets deposit growth north of 10% for FY26
items.quote: We will be north of 10% ma'am deposit growth, total deposits, CASA as well as time deposits. We think we will be north of 10% next year.

items.statement: Expects ROA in 1% ballpark for near term, sees potential to reach 1.15-1.2% later
items.quote: We think that we have enough levers to ensure that our return on assets is in the neighborhood of 1%. We have reasonable expectation of it being in this 1% range in the near term. And then as the environment changes, and the interest rate cycle moves in the opposite direction and as our retail book grows, retail and MSME book grows, we expect gaps to widen. So we expect that to become one, go clos

items.statement: Hesitant to guide NIM due to 40% balance sheet linked to external benchmarks; actively managed NIM in Q4 prioritizing margin over growth
items.quote: am a little hesitant to give guidance on NIMs because the full impact of all the changes to the reference rates and how they will impact us is a little difficult for us to compute at this stage because it's not known when those changes will occur. Roughly 40% of our balance sheet South Indian Bank May 16, 2025 is exposed to external factors. I mean, in the sense that they are linked to either repo

items.statement: Home loans grew 55% YoY, auto loans 24% YoY; will maintain momentum in disbursements and collections
items.quote: On a YOY basis, we are able to achieve 55% growth in home loan and 24% growth in auto loan. We will continue to maintain the momentum in disbursemen t and collections in the coming quarters to achieve our desired targets.

items.statement: Gold loan book at Rs 16,982 cr, up 9% YoY; average LTV 61.88%, average ticket Rs 1.88 lakh
items.quote: Our gold loan business now stands at 16,982 crores with an average LTV of 61.88 % including buyout. And this number includes buyout and an average ticket of about 1.88 lakhs. Gold loan book grew by 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Fixed rate loans ~44% of book, floating ~42%, rest MCLR/base rate/foreign currency; corporate loans repriced at each disbursal
items.quote: Our fixed rate book is about 44% of the total. And the variable rate book is about 42% of the total. So that's it and then we have MCLR and other such things, other asset categories, dollar linked, etc. which make up the rest.

items.statement: RBI draft circular on gold loans may require substantial changes; bank has sought clarifications; business as usual for now
items.quote: The RBI's most recent draft circular has a few points that we need clarity on and we have written to RBI and we have sought some changes to the new draft circular. If the draft circular were to be implemented in total as is, it would require pretty substantial change at our end. We are hopeful that that would not be the case and we are awaiting feedback from RBI.

items.statement: Personal loan book 90% cross-sell to existing savings base; housing loans cross-sold via campaigns; cross-sell embedded in DNA
items.quote: Our personal loan book is about 90 % of the book is cross -sell. So it's to our own existing savings account base that the product has been sold. On the housing loan side as well, we do periodic campaigns to try and sell people housing loans.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution AUM ~Rs 1,000 cr on self-service platform; plans to set up active wealth management arm this year
items.quote: So right now, we offer this on a completely self-service platform, and we have an AUM of about a Rs. 1,000 crores or so. We are in the process of thinking through whether we should set up an arm of the institution that actively makes available wealth products to our customers. So this is something which is in the works.

items.statement: CASA grew 3% YoY to Rs 33,730 cr; one large account outflow masked underlying growth; expects significantly better CASA growth in FY26 as rate cycle turns
items.quote: We had one particular account which had at the end of the prior year, a very large balance which went out and then we had to claw our way back and cover all of that and then grow by three percent. So South Indian Bank May 16, 2025 none of those challenges exist this year for us and we expect next year to be significantly better from a CASA growth perspective

items.statement: NIM pressure expected in H1 FY26 as cost of funds not falling as fast as asset repricing; temporary phenomenon; has levers to manage ROA at 1%
items.quote: The interest rate movement in the environment is adverse at this point in time. So our cost of money is not reducing as fast as some of our assets are repri cing. So I think the entire industry is facing some amount of NIM pressure. So we think that that's a temporary phenomenon, which will be felt during the first half of this year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25: Net profit Rs 342 cr, NII Rs 868 cr, Op profit Rs 683 cr (+57% YoY), NIM 3.21%, ROA 1.11%, ROE 13.74%
items.quote: Bank's net profit for the quarter was Rs. 342 crores compared to Rs. 288 crores during Q4 FY'24. Net interest income for the quarter was Rs. 868 crores. Operating profit for the quarter was Rs. 683 crores as against Rs. 434 crores, an increase of 57 % on a year-on-year basis. Net interest margin for the quarter was at 3.21%. The return on assets was 1.11 % and return on equity was 13.74% for the q

items.statement: Branch value-added (SVA) metric tracks NPV of future cash flows from new products sold; Q4 SVA up 50% YoY but not yet reflected in P&L due to time dimension of assets
items.quote: This represents the net present value of future cash flows. So, if I give a housing loan today, we are going to get a set of interest receivables, which are over a period of time, the net present value of that is x today. This will drip through our P&L. So it won't come through our P&L all at once.

items.statement: Management guides for north of 30% revenue growth in FY26 including Fenixys contribution
items.quote: I feel good about being able to grow north of 30 %. I think you are right about the order book. It is it is fairly strong at the moment.

items.statement: Planning revenue of Rs 1,550-1,600 Cr for FY26 with Fenixys contributing ~5%
items.quote: Yes, we will be talking a number of about 1 ,550-1,600, Fenixys l et's say is 5% thereabouts, slightly less.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 1,400 Cr, up 40% YoY with 4-6 quarter execution timeline
items.quote: we have a very strong Rs. 1,400 Cr worth of orders in hand, which is a 40 % growth on a YoY basis. I do understand that t he execution timeline is Aurionpro Solutions Limited May 14th, 2025 about 4 to 6 quarters

items.statement: Strong demand across banking and TIG segments with significant pipeline growth
items.quote: Both our segment s continue to demonstrate strong business momentum underpinned by significant growing pipeline across both the banking and FinTech as well as Technology Innovation Group.

items.statement: Added 42 new clients in FY25 with major wins in Delhi Metro, Chennai Metro and banking products
items.quote: During the year , we added 42 new clients , a great proof point of the increasing market relevance of our solutions.

items.statement: Planning significant increase in R&D spend for AI-native architecture, Transit, Transaction Banking, lending and Europe market readiness
items.quote: We will significantly step up our R&D spend this year , focusing on significant adjacencies in Transit, Transaction Banking and lending, market readiness for new markets, especially in Europe

items.statement: Evaluating major increase in investments for building sales and distribution channels across Europe
items.quote: We are evaluating a major increase in investments aimed at building sales and distribution channels across several key jobs within Europe.

items.statement: Expect 55-60% EBITDA to cash conversion in normal year, FY25 converted close to 80% net of tax
items.quote: I feel we will be able to convert 55% to 60% of EBITDA to cash normally in normal year. Last year, net of tax I think we converted close to 80%.

items.statement: DSO improved from 120 to 95 days in FY25, expects sustainable level in 90s
items.quote: DSO climbing down from 120 to 95 I think is a sign of that. I feel a 95 DSO , I am not convinced is totally sustainable . I think probably some thumb number in 95s will stay.

items.statement: Banking revenue split 35% one-off license vs 65% recurring/near-recurring; license revenue ~30% of banking
items.quote: I would say that's roughly 35, 65. So 35 on the one -off side, and 65 on the recurring or near -recurring side.

items.statement: Banking license revenue 30% split half from new logos, half from existing accounts
items.quote: So look on the banking products I would say license revenue was something in the range of 30%. Right, so some of it I would say roughly half of it coming from new logos , the other half coming from existing accounts

items.statement: Headcount grew ~50% in FY25 to support delivery capacity; capacity constraints remain key growth limiter
items.quote: I think in terms of number of people, grew about 50% last year. So, we've been hiring, we have been building capacity.

items.statement: Banking projects executing in parallel up 70-80% vs 12 months ago
items.quote: The number of projects we are executing in parallel today and if you compare that to 12 months' back, that's probably 70 % or 80 % more than what it was.

items.statement: Europe expansion investments to pressure H1 FY26 costs but partially absorbed by improving software economics
items.quote: I think you are right, it will probably be especially in the first half of the year put a little bit more pressure in terms of investments. I think for us it's a very significant investment but I think that is needed to capitalize on the long -term opportunity and a large part of that increase I think can get absorbed by the improving economics for the software side of the business at least.

items.statement: Europe revenue currently 7-8%, targeting growth via Fenixys acquisition and organic sales channel
items.quote: Europe, we feel we are ready for, we feel it would be a significant growth driver for us over the next 3 years and Europe is many countries, so it obviously varies, depending on where it is. But we see a very strong alignment with our AI focus, especially with the maturity, regulatory maturity there of AI.

items.statement: Transaction banking win rate leading in Asia; expanding to Southeast Asia and Europe
items.quote: I think transaction banking is really the standout line. We have an astonishingly high win rate in that space. Probably gone more deep than anyone else in that space in Asia Aurionpro Solutions Limited May 14th, 2025 and the next vector of growth for us to expand it more aggressively to Southeast Asia and Europe

items.statement: Transit segment secured Delhi Metro and Chennai Metro wins; end-to-end stack with hardware and software IP
items.quote: We of course, announced the big wins in India, the Delhi Metro and Chennai Metro. I mean, more than big, that's like very prestigious even the homegrown IP. We probably today have the most integrated end -to-end stack in the transit space, transit payment space.

items.statement: Data center business growing 30%+ with strong design team; building own IP for non-linear economics
items.quote: The data center side, I mean really that is a space where there is more demand than anyone can meet. It's more a question of I think we continue to grow at 30 % plus in that space and that's what we will continue to be very selective on the business that we take on.

items.statement: Talent acquisition remains top priority; attracted senior talent from global fintech vendors for Europe and Asia
items.quote: We are probably one of the very few firms who really gets CVs from the top global fintech vendors and that too very senior level CVs. We built out the whole Europe set up right now if you look at it. It's extremely senior talent.

items.statement: Need to continue building talent bench for Rs 3,000-5,000 Cr scale; current team sufficient for Rs 1,200 Cr
items.quote: We still a Rs 1,200 Cr firm. Do we have the talent, when we will be a Rs. 5, 000 Cr firm, do we have the talent to run Rs. 3,000 Cr firm? Probably not. Right? So we will need to continue to work on this.

items.statement: Fenixys acquisition completed; providing delivery capability in France, Norway, UK for Europe expansion
items.quote: We of course have a really mature delivery capability built out through Fenixys as well with good presence in France, good presence in Norway, in the UK.

items.statement: Delivery capacity and execution quality are constraining factors for growth above 30-35% organically
items.quote: I think the constraining factor for us continues to be one - capacity, second - how much do you really want to do without taking unnecessary risks in delivery, right?

items.statement: AI explainability lab expansion to Paris driven by EU AI Act regulatory demand from banking sector
items.quote: But the second also is with the Europe AI Act, there is a lot more regulatory maturity and demand from the banking world around it.

items.statement: No plans to provide Arya.ai capabilities to third-party products outside Aurionpro
items.quote: Will we do that for other products? Probably not. Are we doing that for our products? Yes.

items.statement: India vs global revenue mix roughly 60-40; both growing at similar 30%+ rates
items.quote: I think it's roughly been 60 -40 for some time. I think it will go up or down 1 or 2 points depending on execution, but that's not a meaningful shift in either direction.

items.statement: India's steel demand projected to grow 9% in 2026 driven by infrastructure, housing, engineering and packaging sectors
items.quote: India's steel demand is projected to grow by 9% in 2026, outpacing other major economies. This growth is driven by increased infrastructure development, housing projects, and rising demand for engineering and packaging sector.

items.statement: Indian paint industry projected to grow at 9.4% CAGR through 2030 supported by urbanization, disposable income, infrastructure development
items.quote: The industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of around 9.4% through 2030, offering significant opportunities for expansion.

items.statement: Steel franchisee volumes grew 6% to 34.4 lakh MT in FY25; own manufacturing volumes grew 5% to 119,841 MT
items.quote: Our steel volume from franchisee route have stood at 34.4 lakh metric ton in FY '25, as compared to 32.6 lakh metric ton in FY '24, year-on-year growth of 6%. Our steel volume from own manufacturing stood at 119,841 metric ton as compared to 114,336 metric ton, year-on-year growth of 5%.

items.statement: Royalty income from franchisees grew 8% to record INR139 crores in FY25
items.quote: Royalty income through franchisee stood at INR139 crores in FY '25 as compared to INR129 crores in FY '24, a growth of 8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% bottom line growth for steel business in FY26-27
items.quote: And with regard to revenue, we are also expecting the increase of the bottom line by 20% to 25% in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: Targeting 14% volume growth for steel business in FY26
items.quote: We are targeting around 14% over the last year, 14%. We have made projections for 14% increase in this financial year.

items.statement: Planning 20% increase in brand expenditure for FY26
items.quote: And for FY '26, we are planning to increase it by 20% expenditure.

items.statement: Paint business capex estimated at INR10-15 crores for FY26, mainly tinting machines and balancing equipment
items.quote: It would be ranging between INR10 crores to INR15 crores only.

items.statement: Planning 20% capacity increase at existing franchisee units by end of FY26, with 10-12% operational within FY26
items.quote: And we are planning to increase by 20% of the capacity by end of this financial year, and also considering that out of that, around 10% to 12% will be operational within this financial year.

items.statement: TMT bar prices 1-2% softer in FY25 vs FY24, now steady with upward trend expected
items.quote: Almost. If you take the average of FY24 or take the average of FY25 for the whole year, you can say around 2% prices were softer in 2025 as compared to '24. But now the price is almost steady and I think we can see some upward trend.

items.statement: Paint ASP rose from INR58/kg/liter in FY15 to INR87 in FY25, a 51% increase
items.quote: We have consistently focused on offering a high-quality premium finish, which is evident in the steady rise of our average selling price from INR58 per kg/per liter in financial year 2015 to INR87 in financial year '25, an increase of about 51%.

items.statement: Paint price hikes follow major players like Opus, Birla, Asian Paints; company follows their lead
items.quote: In fact, price hike in the paint business is driven by the major players like the new entrant Opus Birla and Asian Paints. If they increase their price, then the rest of companies also follow that line.

items.statement: Three new entrants in paint industry created competitive turmoil in FY25; impact limited on Kamdhenu due to small network and brand equity
items.quote: As you all know, there are three new entrants in the paint industry. And the entire trade has been very competitive for the past one year. You all understand that there is no extraordinary demand in this year, especially in 2024-25, no new demand has been generated and no new retail network has been created.

items.statement: Paint competition expected to subside in next 6 months (2 quarters of FY26) as players position themselves
items.quote: So I think that in the next 6 months, in the 2 quarters of FY26, the competition will almost begin subsiding as the players choose to position themselves by the end of FY26.

items.statement: 25,000 painters enrolled in branding and marketing schemes
items.quote: As of now we have 25,000 painters are enrolled, and I understand that the demand for different products is increasing.

items.statement: Exploring strategic stake acquisition in select franchisee units to reshape franchisee model and expand in-house manufacturing capacity
items.quote: We are also exploring strategic stake acquisition in select franchisee units. This move is aimed to reshaping our franchisee model, while also contributing to the expansion of our in-house manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Received INR45 crores of INR97 crores preferential issue; invested in franchisee units, office acquisition, brand strengthening
items.value: INR45 crores received of INR97 crores
items.quote: So far, we have received INR45 crores from the total preferential issue of INR97 crores. And it has been invested in the franchisee unit and there are certain other expenditures for acquiring the office and brand strengthening, which as per the objective of that issue, we are using that fund.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: We continue to remain debt free as on March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Steel business ROCE 25.5% and ROE 19.2% in FY25
items.quote: ROCE and ROE stood at 25.5% and 19.2%, respectively.

items.statement: Steel business maintains 20% market share in organized retail branded TMT segment
items.quote: While average selling price for TMT bars was slightly softer, with a marginal year-on-year decline, we continue to hold a strong 20% market share in the organized retail branded TMT segment.

items.statement: Government safeguard duty on HR coils, cold rolled coils, sheets benefits TMT pricing; no Chinese TMT imports
items.quote: government has imposed safeguard duty in steel products which are HR Coils, cold rolled coils, sheets it has been imposed on them for the bigger plant, but that effect ultimately comes in the TMT. So TMT last year it has reached from INR1,000 to INR2,000 tons and from that INR1,000 per ton is recovery is done and there no channel that TMT can come from China or from any other country.

items.statement: Acknowledged foul play and social media manipulation caused extraordinary share price movement in Kamdhenu Paints; filed FIR and identified individuals
items.quote: It might be in your knowledge that some people have foul play and social media messages is also there because of that some people have misused it and extraordinary price movement you and I have also seen. The normal price which was running it has been escalated a lot and some people and we also have made efforts and we have identified some people also and after that when we have taken action that

items.statement: Paint strategy focused on premiumization - climbing value chain by increasing share of high-value premium finishes
items.quote: Our strategy going forward will be focused on climbing up the value chain by increasing the share of high-value, premium finish in our portfolio. This will help us drive higher average selling price and improve overall profitability.

items.statement: No sales depots closed in any region; strengthening retail network where weak; freight disadvantage limits supply to South India
items.quote: No, we have not closed any sales depot in any region. Our entire effort is to improve our retail network, and we are strengthening where we were falling weak. There is no such area where we are falling weak, and there is one drawback -- our unit is in North India, and we are not able to supply to the entire country just because of freight disadvantage.

items.statement: Targets FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 10,000 crores with 7% volume growth and 13% EBITDA margin
items.quote: This year we are expecting a full year with the integration of the balance 49, we are expecting the revenue to be Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects 9-10% volume growth in India business organically with flat value growth in FY26
items.quote: There will be volume growth of almost 9% to 10% of volume. That will happen.

items.statement: Targets 13% EBITDA margin for FY26
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting in the range of 13% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin expanded 370 bps to 36.6% due to favorable input prices
items.quote: Gross profit grew by 20% and the gross profit margin is 370 bps higher, that is 32.9% to 36.6% which is attributable to the favorable input prices.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin expanded 200 bps to 34.5%
items.quote: Gross profit stood at Rs. 3,030 crores and the gross profit margins expanded by 200 bps from 32.5% to 34.5%.

items.statement: Golden Star margins expected to improve as freight costs normalized and 10% tariff passed to customers
items.quote: Freight cost this year is back to normal because last year only in between the disruption came and we were not able to pass on. But this year it has been normal and it's all in control.

items.statement: FY26 capex of Rs 340 crores for warehousing and RTH facility in US, excluding stake buyout
items.quote: So, regarding the CAPEX this year, what we have is almost a Rs. 340 crores of CAPEX that will be there and that will be majorly in the warehousing facilities and the RTH facility in the US.

items.statement: Proposed acquisition of Global Green Group (canned food, ~€40M revenue) for ~€6M equity plus debt
items.quote: First of all, it's value is around 25-24 million. It's not Rs. 600 crores. It's only in terms of rupees its around Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: No demand impact from US recession historically; home consumption increases during downturns
items.quote: So, what we have seen in history, we have seen 2-3 times, we acquired this business in 2008 and there was a recession in 2009 -10. But what we have seen in all the times, even in Covid time and all the time when the recession come, home consumption goes up in America, especially in the food side.

items.statement: Golden Star 10% tariff passed on to customers with no demand impact seen
items.quote: Regarding the impact of the duty as I just said that 10% there is a duty, and we have passed on to the customer. So, we have yet to see any impact on the demand side, but we expect that there will be no impact here.

items.statement: Sourced 100% paddy from India in FY25 vs 4-5% from Pakistan previously
items.quote: Not, in the last year we sourced from Pakistan but this year we don't have any position from Pakistan. It's all sourced from India. But last 2-3 years we were sourcing from Pakistan.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 196 in FY25 from 188 in FY24
items.quote: Our net working capital day stands at 196 days in Financial Year '25 versus 188 days in Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Higher inventory built in FY25 due to favorable paddy prices; bought more paddy than rice
items.quote: Resham as you said rightly one is the inventory gone up because of the volume growth. And the second, the prices w ere very in favor of us. Normally we keep as a policy partly we buy in procurement and partly we buy in off season. But this year we thought it's a very attractive price. So, we bought more inventory than regularly we buy or of course, we are a little optimistic also as this year the

items.statement: India and US entities to be debt-free from July FY26; net debt positive in India
items.quote: In India our net debt position will be positive, we won't be having any kind of debt. In fact, in the month from July and onwards. So, our cash position and the net debt basis we will be positive.

items.statement: Net debt to equity 0.2x and net debt to EBITDA 0.6x in FY25
items.quote: The net debt to equity ratio is at 0.2 in Financial Year '2 5 versus 0.1 in Financial Year '24 and the net debt to EBITDA ratio is 0.6 in Financial Year '25 compared to 0.5 in Financial Year '24.

items.statement: Royal brand holds >55% US basmati market share; positioned at $20 price point with Daawat at premium
items.quote: So Royal hold more than 55% market share. We are number one selling brand, both in the mainstream as well as in the ethnic channel. Regarding price point, there are two price point available, and the royal is on the price point you have seen.

items.statement: No impact from Indus Water Treaty or UK FTA; zero duty on brown rice unchanged
items.quote: Although in this year as I said earlier that we are not buying so India was more competitive. So, this year we bought only from India and that's what we are expecting next year also we will most probably buy from India only. So, on the UK treaty there is a no negative impact on us. So, it is same, as on the brown rice there was a zero duty, this year also no change in that.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia revenue Rs 55 crores in FY25; will take years to impact top/bottom line
items.quote: In the coming '25-26, our revenue will be more than Rs. 10,000 crores and at the moment Saudi is contributing only Rs. 55 crores. So, it will take some years to make the impact from the bottom line and top line.

items.statement: Increased advertising spend in FY26 for brand building with Shah Rukh Khan campaign
items.quote: Advertising will be this year more because we have this year heavy spent on the consumer side. So, advertising will increase more.

items.statement: India basmati volume grew 15% YoY in Q4 FY25 with 7% value growth (6.5% realization decline)
items.quote: With the fourth quarter, if you talk about the fourth quarter itself on the Y -on-Y basis volume has increased by 15% and the value growth is 7%. So, there is the realization has decreased by 6.5%.

items.statement: Pakistan basmati output impact from Indus Treaty too early to assess; sowing in July
items.quote: That is too early to assess. But in the coming months we will be able to know what the impact would be. Sowing happens in the first week of July or midweek of July only able to, we will be able to know but I don't think there will be any impact here.

items.statement: Golden Star (Jasmine rice JV) not consolidated; only JV profit in P&L
items.quote: The Jasmine, the Golden Star revenue is not getting consolidated. It is a JV. It is just the profit from the JV that is getting consolidated.

items.statement: Management targets 14-15% top-line growth and consistent EBITDA margin expansion for FY26 despite weak summer in South India
items.quote: So we could have a situation where Q1 growth could be slightly impacted, but for the full year we should still try and hit that 14%, 15% growth. And margins, we are quite confident of maintaining the margins, we are not so far that worried.

items.statement: Cooling product demand impacted by weak summer in South and East India; North and West still warm with 45 days of season remaining
items.quote: this year in Ap ril we had intermittent showers in the South and eastern part of the country, and summer here has been less warm when we compare with last year. So definitely the sales of cooling products will get impacted like air conditioners, stabilizers, air coolers, fans, pumps, and to some degree inverters as well

items.statement: Gross margin improved 100 bps YoY to 35.5% in Q4 FY25; recovery largely complete driven by in-house manufacturing, cost efficiency, and premium mix
items.quote: We have reported a gross margin of 35.5% this quarter compared to 34.5% in Q4 of last year, an increase of 100 basis points. We have driven a meaningful improvement in gross margin through the year and believe that the margin recovery is largely complete.

items.statement: Solar rooftop business growing very strong within Electronics segment; expected to hit significant scale in 4-5 years with headroom across 35 states
items.quote: The solar rooftop business is growing very strong. It's housed within Electronics. We have had very, very strong growth, although we do not give out product wise numbers. I think in about four to five years' time, we should hit really good numbers.

items.statement: Annual capex around ₹100 crores; no major increase expected; major part going to moulds; Vapi kitchen plant not at full capacity
items.quote: We were around ₹100 crores per annum. I think we do not expect any major increase from this. In fact, a lot of our plants are up and running and there are a couple of more factories that are to come.

items.statement: Hyderabad battery plant at full utilization; new capacity expansion of ₹50 crores to add ₹300-400 crores throughput; full stabilization in 2.5 years
items.quote: About three years back we had initiated a project for setting up a battery capacity in Hyderabad. And about 18 months back, this capacity was commercialized. And as we sit today, the factory is operating on full capacity utilization there.

items.statement: Launched mid-market BLDC fan range and premium water heater range to address pricing gaps; initial response to fans very positive
items.quote: We have launched a mid-market range of BLDC fans, which comes in various configurations. And I think this segment, so V-Guard does slightly less than indexation in BLDC was slightly less than what we would have liked to be, and this should address that.

items.statement: Non-South market grew 18.6% YoY in Q4, reaching 47.5% of full-year revenue excluding Sunflame; well diversified across large states
items.quote: In Q4 FY '25, revenue from non-South market grew by 18.6% Y-o-Y, while the South market grew at 15.3% Y-o-Y. For the full year, the non-South market contribution reached 47.5%, excluding Sunflame.

items.statement: Stabilizer market share at 55-60% of organized market; competitors like Voltas and Everest have been around for years; tactical bundling during weak season not new
items.quote: Generally, yes we are around 55%, 60% of the market, there's a remaining 40%. This keeps changing. Brands come and brands go, brands become active, and brands become slow, I mean, they taper off.

items.statement: Working capital at steady state; debtor days cannot go much lower; inventory has small room for improvement; repaid Sunflame term loan early, now debt-free
items.quote: Working capital remains efficient, ensuring strong cash flow generation. We have repaid, ahead of time, the entire term loan related to the Sunflame acquisition and are back to being a debt free Company.

items.statement: Fully repaid Sunflame acquisition term loan ahead of schedule; company is now debt-free
items.quote: We have repaid, ahead of time, the entire term loan related to the Sunflame acquisition and are back to being a debt free Company.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of 150% (₹1.5 per equity share) for FY25
items.quote: In recognition of this strong performance, the Board of Directors recommended a final dividend of 150% equating to ₹ 1.5 per equity share.

items.statement: Wires Q4 revenue growth 17% (5% volume, 12% price); full-year volume growth 2-3%, price growth 8%
items.quote: Q4 growth is 17%, 5% volume growth and 12% value growth.

items.statement: Sunflame CSD/CPC channel under structural stress due to brand proliferation and inventory correction; recovery timeline uncertain
items.quote: CSD which used to have four or five brands, today is having 12 to 15 brands in each category. So they have added a lot of brands and that has created a lot of problems for them in the sense of a lot of overstocking has happened.

items.statement: Sunflame integration ongoing; product portfolio refresh cycle 18 months; service/logistics/quality integration with V-Guard systems targeted by Sep-Oct
items.quote: We are working on business integration of Sunflame with V-Guard, right. So this is a journey, and I think it will take some more time before the integration is complete.

items.statement: Solar rooftop growth driven by government incentives for individual houses across 7-8 states; significant headroom in remaining states
items.quote: The Government is giving a lot of incentives for individual houses moving to rooftops and that's driving a lot of demand. I think we still have a lot of headroom because this entire demand is from some seven or eight different states out of these 35 states.

items.statement: Copper price uptick in April expected to improve wires performance sequentially in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In April, we have seen that there has been an improvement and increase in copper prices. So, I think this quarter we should do better than previous quarter.

items.statement: Employee cost growth 15-16% CAGR over 3 years from increments, headcount, Sunflame addition, and new factories; ESOP/variable pay writebacks in prior year
items.quote: The underlying growth rate of for the last three years was about 15% to 16%, which is really the routine increments, and some headcount increases and so on.

items.statement: Gegadyne investment: technology validated at pilot plant; commercial launch 2+ years away; exclusive rights for inverter battery and V-Guard categories
items.quote: They have kind of stabilized to achieve their technology goals and we have validated it; it's working well. So now they are in course of figuring out how to scale up and how to move forward, and how to prepare for a commercial launch, but that will be at least another couple of years away.

items.statement: Strategy 3.0 targets 30 GW generation capacity and 40 GWh energy storage by 2030
items.quote: I am happy to announce and we're launching Strategy 3.0, our new roadmap to achieve 30 GW of generation capacity and 40 GWh of energy storage by 2030.

items.statement: EBITDA expected to grow 2.7x-3.0x over FY25 proforma EBITDA by FY30
items.quote: By FY30, we expect our EBITDA on a run-rate basis to grow 2.7x –3.0x over FY25 proforma EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 1,30,000 crore between FY26 and FY30
items.quote: To support this, we plan to invest ₹1,30,000 crore in capital expenditure between FY26 and FY30.

items.statement: FY25 capex was Rs 8,000 crore vs guided Rs 15,000 crore
items.quote: What we actually ended up incurring as a total CAPEX for fiscal '25 was about Rs. 8,000 crores. And if you remember, we had started, we were guided for Rs. 15,000 CAPEX for the year.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at Rs 15,000-18,000 crore
items.quote: For fiscal 2026, we are expecting to end up spending anything between Rs. 15,000 crores to Rs. 18,000 crores in that range to complete the ongoing projects plus the pipeline of new growth projects that have started.

items.statement: Operating capacity reached 12.2 GW after adding 3.6 GW in FY25
items.quote: As I speak today, JSW Energy is a 12.2 GW company, reflecting the momentum we have built across both organic and inorganic expansion. In FY2025 alone, we have added 3.6 GW of capacity strengthening the diversity and scale of our portfolio.

items.statement: 11.3 GW under construction, all fully tied up under long-term PPAs
items.quote: JSW Energy is currently constructing 11.3 GW of generation projects, all of which are fully tied up under long-term Power Purchase Agreements.

items.statement: Locked-in capacity now stands at 30.2 GW including pipeline
items.quote: With 11.3 MW under construction projects and a robust pipeline, our locked-in capacity now stands at 30.2 GW, placing us firmly on track to deliver target set under Strategy 3.0.

items.statement: Acquired KSK Mahanadi 3,600 MW for Rs 16,084 crore; 1,800 MW operational, 95% tied up
items.quote: KSK Mahanadi is 3,600 MW plant and is the largest thermal asset acquired via NCLT proceedings for a total resolution amount of ₹ 16,084 crore. Currently 1,800 MW is operational which is 95% tied up under PPAs and has fuel supply agreements.

items.statement: Acquired O2 Power 4.7 GW RE platform for Rs 12,468 crore; 1.3 GW installed, targeting 4.7 GW by June 2027 with Rs 13,000-14,000 crore capex
items.quote: In another large transaction we acquired O2 Power a 4.7 GW RE platform. The total consideration paid for O2 Power is ₹ 12,468 crore. The current installed capacity of O2 is 1.3 GW and we expect it to scale to 4.7 GW by June 2027 by undertaking capital ex penditure of ₹ 13,000- ₹ 14,000

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA Rs 6,115 crore (highest ever), PAT Rs 1,951 crore (record high)
items.value: EBITDA Rs 6,115 crore / PAT Rs 1,951 crore
items.quote: This has resulted in company reporting the highest ever annual EBITDA of ₹ 6,115 Crore and Record highest PAT of ₹ 1,951 Crore.

items.statement: Pro forma EBITDA Rs 8,860 crore; net debt to pro forma EBITDA at 5x
items.quote: Against the reported EBITDA of Rs. 6,115 crores, if you look at the pro forma EBITDA, which basically is if all these assets that we have acquired in the middle of the year were available with us for the entire part of the year, the pro forma EBITDA is about Rs. 8,860 crores. And hence, the net debt to pro forma EBITDA stands at just about 5x.

items.statement: KSK Mahanadi FY25 operational EBITDA Rs 2,382 crore at 67.4% PLF; PLF improved to 79% post-acquisition
items.quote: In FY2025 the plant reported full year reported EBITDA of ₹ 2,895 crore on a PLF of 67.4% while the underlying EBITDA stands at ₹ 2,382 Crore. We have improved PLF to 79% from FY25 average of 67% post completion of the transaction that is within 25 days of our operation s in the month of March

items.statement: Salboni ultra-supercritical thermal PPA levelized tariff Rs 5.45/kWh for 25 years with domestic coal
items.quote: So Atul, the levelized 25-year tariff under two-part mechanism will be roughly Rs. 5.45 per kWh.

items.statement: Merchant tariff firming: Q4 FY25 higher than Q3, Q1 FY26 at Rs 4.76/unit
items.quote: We have seen merchant tariff firming up in Q4FY25 as compared to Q3FY25. In Q1FY26 we are seeing merchant tariff further incre ased to ₹ 4.76/unit

items.statement: API 4 coal prices currently around $89/t; domestic coal supply robust
items.quote: For the quarter gone by prices were stable year on year at $95/t. Currently API 4 coal prices are around $89/t while within the domestic coal market, sufficient steps are taken to keep a robust coal supply.

items.statement: Long-term project financing typically at 8-9% range
items.quote: But largely, 8% to 9%, that is the range typically at which you can get a long tenor project financing facility today.

items.statement: India power demand grew 4.2% in FY25; Q4 grew 3.2% YoY; peak demand 250 GW in FY25
items.quote: power demand for the country grew 4.2% in fiscal year 2025. In the fourth quarter we saw a demand growth of 3.2% year on year on a high base of 7.4% growth seen last year in the same quarter. Structurally we continue to expect strong power demand in the medium term. The peak demand witnessed in the quarter is 238 GW in Feb ’25 and 250 GW in FY25

items.statement: Open capacity now ~976 MW, 790 MW domestic coal-based (91%), reducing global coal price exposure
items.quote: With Vijayanagar fully tied up, our open capacity now stands at approximately 976 MW of which large part of 790 MW is based on domestic coal which is 91% of the total coal capacity used for merchant. This transformation signifies a decisive move towards a more resilient, domestic coal-based open capacity, reducing exposure to global coal price volatility.

items.statement: Energy storage locked-in capacity expanded to 28.3 GWh; 12 GWh PSP with MSEDCL under implementation, 12 GWh PSP with UPPCL signed in Q1 FY26
items.quote: we have expanded our locked in energy storage capacity to 28.3 GWh. Notably, the Bhavali in Maharashtra, the 12 GWh hydro pumped storage project which is tied up with MSEDCL is currently under implementation. In addition, recently in Q1FY26 we have signed PPA with UPPCL for another 12GWh of PSP project to be delivered in next 6 years.

items.statement: Salboni thermal project secured Section 63 competitive bid PPA for 25 years
items.quote: You see, this is again the Sal boni is a section (63) PPA, which was under the competitive bidding, which we have been able to secure

items.statement: Thermal portfolio PLF 77% in Q4 FY25, 71% for full year
items.quote: Our thermal portfolio witnessed a healthy PLFs of 77% in the quarter and 71% for the full year.

items.statement: Net generation up 24% YoY in Q4 FY25 to 7.9 BU; renewable generation up 32% YoY
items.quote: Our net generation for the quarter rose by 24% year-on-year, to 7.9 billion units, driven by 32% year-on-year increase in renewable generation on the back of capacity additions.

items.statement: Wind PLF assumptions use conservative P90 vs industry P75; LCOE focus protects benchmark returns
items.quote: we have always been very conservative in terms of the assumptions, like the industry in general we have seen in case of wind has operated at P75 but for us the benchmark is P90 which gives us enough room for such kind of deviations when we have seen the last year also that the wind speeds comparatively were lesser than what was anticipated, so we take care lot of assumptions in such a way that eve

items.statement: Vision 2027 targets INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY27
items.quote: To further capitalize on the brand acceptance, we have outlined a vision 2027 of achieving INR1,000 crores turnover by FY 2027.

items.statement: Targets 5-6% same-store sales growth annually for Vision 2027
items.quote: So out of this, we are having 5% to 6% target to have the same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Targets gross margin of 55-56% and EBITDA margin of 28-30% at INR 1,000 crore revenue
items.quote: we have to mainta in our gross margins approximately 55%, 56%. And then the EBITDA margin in the range of 28% to 30% is going to be maintained

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR 50-52 crore for stores, warehouse, and factory expansion
items.quote: So total capex requirement is INR50 crores to INR52 crores for this financial year, right, which completes all my requirement of INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Plans to increase store count to 725 by FY27 with 10% franchisee mix
items.quote: So right now, we have like pres ence of 20% of the stores are in the Tier 1 towns, 40% Tier 2 and 40% in Tier 3 towns. So same kind of spread we are expecting in the next 2 years

items.statement: Average new store size increasing to 1,700 sq ft from 1,635 sq ft
items.quote: So last year, our average size was 1,635 square feet. So it's going to increase a little bit till 1,700 square feet per store, for the new stores.

items.statement: Store format mix to remain: 40% men's, 30% men's & ladies, 20% family, 10% ladies & kids
items.quote: Right now, like we have 10% of our store are ladies, kids store; 20% are the family stores; 30% are the men's and ladies stores; and 40% are the men's stores. These are our broad classification of the stores. So in the same manner, we will be going forward.

items.statement: ASP increased by over INR 20 YoY; positioned in mid-premium segment at ~INR 1,050 ASP
items.quote: So our ASP increased by more than INR20 when compared to the last year. So we always mentioned that our USP is our average selling price because we are into the mid premium segment brand.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 28.4% from 26.4%; Q4 FY25 at 26.8%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the company for FY '25 stood at 28.4% as compared to 26.4% in FY '24.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~2% in Q4 FY25 driven by price correction and controlled discounting
items.quote: So basically, gross margin has been increased by 2%, 2% or 2.5%, right? So majority, it is by the slight increase in the correction in the prices.

items.statement: No fundraising needed; growth funded from internal accruals; cash surplus company
items.quote: Not at all. No, not at all. Absolutely from the internal accruals going forward as well. We are the cash surplus company.

items.statement: Dividend policy up to 20% payout; interim dividend paid post Q3; final dividend at AGM
items.quote: So we have a very clear dividend policy, and up to 20% we are distri buting. So one interim dividend has been already been declared and paid post the result of Q3 and the final would be declared probably in the AGM

items.statement: Sales mix: 81% menswear, 11% womenswear, 5% accessories, 3% kidswear; womenswear target 13%
items.quote: Yes. So overall contribution is like this, the 81% of the sales is coming from the menswear category, 11% is coming from the womenswear category, 5% from accessories and 3% from the kidswear.

items.statement: Rent per sq ft declining: INR 129 -> 122 -> 120 due to larger store formats
items.quote: But regarding the rental, per square feet rentals are going down. So last year, it was INR129 square feet. Last year, it was INR122, and this year, it has came down to INR120 square feet.

items.statement: Warehouse-corporate facility completion by end of calendar year; INR 13-14 crore remaining outflow
items.quote: So our warehousing come corporate facility is going to be complete by end of this calendar as well. So there is an outflow of INR13 crores to INR14 crores remaining, which is going to be there.

items.statement: Bahadurgarh factory expansion: one floor addition at INR 8-10 crore
items.quote: We are enhancing Bahadurgarh facility as well. One floor is being constructed there. That is required approximately INR8 crores to INR10 crores.

items.statement: SSG volatility driven by seasonality (winter severity) and wedding date calendar
items.quote: There is two factors majorly, the season and the wedding season. Season, I mean the winter season was very poor in the Q4. That's why our SSG has gone down. So season has an impact. And the wedding season, the number of wedding dates has an impact on the sales growth and the same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Closed 18 stores in FY25 (8 performance-based, 10 relocations); net additions 66
items.quote: Out of overall closure in terms of its stores was 18. Performance -based closure. Performance-based closure was 8, right, and 10 were the relocation

items.statement: No plans to enter cosmetics/beauty; will stay in accessories category for women
items.quote: You are telling about the accessories and the cosmetics part in the women category. So right now, we don't have plan to go in the cosmetics or beauty products. So we will be only going with the accessories category we are already doing.

items.statement: Mature stores deliver 10-15% higher per sq ft sales than newer stores
items.quote: But when I'm categorizing my stores for more than 3 years or more than 6 years, so there is a 10% to 15% is the difference, right? So a few very old stores are average is delivering INR150 lakhs and few are delivering INR1 crores, which are new.

items.statement: Volume growth expected at 2-3% annually; price correction to drive balance of 5-6% SSG
items.quote: So 50-50 always we said, like this year, 4% and 2% of volume being driven. So going forward, when I'm talking about 5% -6% SSG, 2% to 3% would be the volume and some correction would take it to 6%.

items.statement: Ad spend reduced to 1.32% of revenue from ~1.6% in FY24
items.quote: 1.32%, sir, is the total expenditure this year as compared to last year, approximately 1.6%. So we are controlling it now and...

items.statement: PSF ~INR 785 in FY25 (down from INR 800); average sales per store improved to INR 119 lakh from INR 116 lakh
items.quote: Last year, our PSF was 800. And obviously, in our earlier commentary, we also mentioned t he moment we are opening the bigger stores, theoretically per square feet dimensions have been slightly changed. So this year, we end up approximately 785 is our PSF, right? But you just mentioned the average sale per store, that has been improved from last year, INR116 lakhs to this year, approximately INR11

items.statement: Completed Rs 3,700 crore rights issue and QIP in Jan 2025, strengthening capital base and top-5 shareholder holding to ~25%
items.quote: We successfully concluded two equity raise transactions, one Rs. 3,700 crores equity rights issue and then QIP earlier in January of 2025.

items.statement: Growth AUM reached Rs 37,000+ crores (60% of total AUM), up from Rs 26,000 crores last year
items.quote: That growth AUM has now reached as much as Rs. 37,000 plus crores, rising from approximately Rs. 26,000 crores last year and now stands at about 60% of the total AUM.

items.statement: Target consolidated AUM of Rs 1 lakh crore by FY27; growth AUM at Rs 37,452 crores currently
items.quote: On a goal of reaching a Fiscal '27 growth AUM of Rs. 1 lakh crore, we are at Rs. 37,452 crores, still a long way to go.

items.statement: Annual disbursals growing 20-30% nominally; targeting incremental ROA of 3.2% (currently 3%) and mid-to-high teens ROE
items.quote: With nominal growth 20%-30% every year, we should be able to achieve our target out there. The incremental ROA is also trending and now with a renewed focus on improving our cost-to-income ratio in the short term, I believe we should be quickly hitting the 3.2% mark.

items.statement: Gross NPA halved to 1.3%, Net NPA at 0.8%; credit costs guided at ~100 bps (95 bps in H2 FY25); total imputed provisions at 33% of legacy book (Rs 8,335 cr)
items.quote: Year-on-year, our Stage-3 assets have dropped from 2.7%-1.3% on a gross basis, on a net basis from 1.5%-0.8%. We continue to use asset recovery reconstruction companies for facilitating the recovery process. That is working along well for us. The credit costs have been guided at about 100 basis points.

items.statement: Legacy book cash collections at record Rs 12,834 cr in FY25 (Q4: Rs 2,978 cr); targeting single-digit % of AUM by FY27
items.quote: What is most comforting is that the collection from the legacy book in FY '25 was at its highest ever point at Rs. 12,834 crores with Rs. 2,978 crores collected in quarter 4 itself, well in line with the projections that we have done.

items.statement: Balance sheet borrowings grew 2.3x YoY; retail bond program has 88,000+ investors; free flow of capital established
items.quote: Through Fiscal '25, we have established free flow of capital. We have borrowed about 2.3x of what we did in the previous Financial Year, and this should then bring in the next level of competitive advantage driver, which is lowering of cost of funds.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing rates ~35 bps lower; back book to reprice over 3-6 months as MCLR resets; current borrowing cost ~9%, blended yield ~13% (interest income 11-12%)
items.quote: So our incremental rates that we are getting are about 35-ish basis points lower than what we were getting. The back book would get repriced as and when it is a cycle, so we typically would be running at MCLR plus 3-month MCLR or 6-month MCLR.

items.statement: Target cost of funds reduction ahead of repo rate cuts in FY26; focus on improving cost-to-income ratio
items.quote: Fiscal '26 should see us being able to reduce our cost of funds slightly ahead of the reduction which should anyways in normal course come to us with a reducing repo rate.

items.statement: Consolidated branch network target of ~350 branches by FY27; Sammaan Finserve independent distribution/leadership by end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we should get to about 350 branches by Fiscal '27, which would then be further split between Sammaan Capital and Sammaan Finserve.

items.statement: Hired new CTO Dharmvir (ex-Home First, Hero FinCorp, Spandana); leadership reorganization underway with global HR firm; succession planning in H1 FY26
items.quote: we just a few months ago hired a new Chief Technology Officer, Dharmv ir, who comes with a long financial services experience and has s erved in mortgage companies like Home First, NBFCs like Hero FinCorp and a small bank like Spandana

items.statement: AIF platform targeting Rs 15,000 cr AUM by FY27 (Rs 1,500 cr group contribution, ~10% of net worth); first transaction done, second expected in May
items.quote: This is a platform which will work with several of our partner funds more in our core investment format and this itself expects to be targeting AUM or getting to an AUM of Rs. 15,000 crores and in due course of time, of that Rs. 15,000 crores we expect about Rs. 1,500 crores to be our contribution.

items.statement: Sammaan Finserve FY27 targets: Balance sheet Rs 10,000 cr (currently Rs 7,121 cr), net worth Rs 3,400 cr (currently Rs 3,071 cr), annual disbursals Rs 9,000 cr, monthly run-rate Rs 500 cr in FY26, ROA 5%+, ROE 14%
items.quote: Fiscal '27 goal for balance sheet is Rs. 10,000 crores. We are at Rs. 7,121 crores. The net worth goal is Rs. 3,400 crores. We are at Rs. 3,071 crores. Disbursals annually should be at about Rs. 9,000 crores. We should be looking to get to a run rate of Rs. 500 crores per month within Fiscal '26 itself.

items.statement: Asset-light mix evolving: targeting 40% direct assignment, 40% co-lending, 20% PTC by FY27; RMBS transactions started (first on May 6) at ~7.5% pricing
items.quote: By Fiscal '27, I expect direct assignments to rise to 40%. Very interesting development, which also happening is I have been speaking for the last 2 years about the Government of India, focusing on setting up a residential mortgage-backed security issuance system in the country, that has finally taken off, the first transaction of our RMBS happened on the 6th of May.

items.statement: RBI dispensation for NBFC owning NBFC not long-term; engaging RBI on distinct business model for Sammaan Finserve; priority sector co-lending restriction may be freed
items.quote: There is RBI dispensation that we currently enjoy as far as an NBFC owning an NB FC and that is not a structure which will be long term enabled. So during the course of this year , we will go back to RBI with a firm plan around how exactly do we want to run this business and build a distinct business model

items.statement: Board to propose small dividend for FY25, larger dividend for FY26
items.quote: So dividend, we will discuss with the Board and propose a small dividend this year and hopefully a larger dividend next year.

items.statement: Legacy book rundown remains key management focus; over-capitalized state to continue 2-3 years for lender comfort; net NPA target ~120 bps range
items.quote: The rundown of the legacy AUM continues to remain an area of emphasis for the management. It takes up significant time of the management. Fortunately, the portfolio has been organically run down by over Rs. 1,70,000 crores since in the last 7 years.

items.statement: Co-lending at 95-96% acceptance rate provides stable ALM; growth AUM at 60% of total AUM; gearing reduced to 1.9x; net worth Rs 21,822 cr
items.quote: There is a high rate of acceptance close to about 95%-96% of the loans that we do are being partnered with banks in a variety of structures and this is providing us with the most stable form of ALM, the most durable form of ALM.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance of INR 3600 crore for FY26 maintained, with potential upside to INR 4000 crore
items.quote: We've always had a guidance of 3600 crores organically and inorganically by FY26 and if there are some green shoots or some new things we see could go up to as high as 4000 crores and a base guidance of 3600 crores and we stick to that guidance.

items.statement: Pricol Precision Products targeting INR 1500 crore revenue in three years (from INR 750 crore run rate) including inorganic growth
items.quote: We took it over at around 750 crores run rate. We are pretty confident of growing it to about 1500 crores top line in three years that I stand committed to that commitment that we have made.

items.statement: Employee cost expected to normalize to 11.5-12% of sales as revenue grows; currently elevated due to R&D hiring and lower Q4 revenue
items.quote: We always used to maintain it at around 11.5 to 12% of sales and we are pretty confident that with the current increasing sales in the quarter one itself, we will be able to normalize it.

items.statement: Export margins at almost twice OEM/domestic margins; US exposure ~5% of revenue but equivalent to ~10% due to higher margins
items.quote: There is about 7% of our revenue comes from exports of which about 70% is US linked. So, 5% of our revenue comes from exports but albeit at almost twice the margins of the OEM and domestic products.

items.statement: Two-wheeler sector (65% of revenue) saw muted Q4 due to OBD2 regulation transition; significant revival seen in Q1 FY26, normalizing by Q2
items.quote: The two-wheeler sector, which accounts for 65% of the revenue of our company, has seen very muted numbers in Q4. This was because of the OBD 2 regulation, which saw a huge transformation from April 1st, 2025. We are already halfway into Q1 of FY26 and we see a significant revival of the market in the two-wheeler segment.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 two-wheeler revenue grew ~14% vs industry growth of ~9%
items.quote: The 2-Wheeler industry has grown by about 9% and we have grown by around 14%.

items.statement: Pricol Precision Products: INR 225-250 crore capex over next 8 quarters for modernization, automation, capacity debottlenecking
items.quote: We have planned over the next four quarters approximately between 225 crores to 250 crores of CapEx in Pricol Precision Products. This is to enhance efficiency by replacing about 50 machines add capacity in the tool room, add new machines, add automation.

items.statement: Pricol Limited standalone: INR 200-225 crore capex in FY26 (Pune and Manesar plants), then maintenance capex mode
items.quote: We are going to be at the end of our high CapEx. We have two plants that are happening this year, Pune and Manesar. So, this year, correct me if I'm wrong Priya n, we are looking at around 200 to 225 crores of CapEx after which we will go into a maintenance CapEx

items.statement: Pricol Precision Products acquired at INR 750 crore run rate; currently engaging non-TVS two-wheeler customers for growth
items.quote: this was owned by the TV S group, we were not able to access other two -wheeler customers who are the primary revenue earners for Pricol. Now we have started engaging with all the other two -wheeler makers and we are confident of growing the company significantly

items.statement: Standing firm on export pricing despite US tariff pressure; not reducing prices as China/Vietnam alternatives also face tariffs and 2-year lead time for replacement
items.quote: We have stood very firm saying that we will not be able to reduce the prices because we know the other two low-cost destinations that they can take these products from are China and Vietnam which are also facing similar tariffs.

items.statement: Forex impact of INR 3.5 crore in Q4 FY25 (deferred earnings due to dollar strengthening); will be recovered over 6-month trailing basis in Q1-Q2 FY26
items.quote: The dollar very sharply strengthened in this quarter, which has resulted in a significant f orex impact. Nevertheless, this is only deferred earnings because we have an indexation for Forex with all of our customers. So, while this has been a forex impact in Q4 of FY25 , t his will be recovered on a six-month maximum trailing basis

items.statement: Pricol Precision Products net working capital cycle not explicitly quantified; capex includes efficiency improvements
items.quote: We have planned over the next four quarters approximately between 225 crores to 250 crores of CapEx in Pricol Precision Products. This is to enhance efficiency by replacing about 50 machines add capacity in the tool room, add new machines, add automation, thereby also increasing our top line.

items.statement: Consolidated long-term borrowing INR 800 million primarily due to Pricol Precision Products acquisition
items.quote: At a consolidated level of this quarter, our long-term borrowing is at INR 800 million. This is primarily due to the account of our acquisition of the plastics business from erstwhile Sundaram Auto Components Limited by Pricol Precision Products Private Limited.

items.statement: Acquired plastics business from Sundaram Auto Components (now Pricol Precision Products) for ~INR 195 crore; investing additional INR 250 crore over 8 quarters
items.quote: We acquired a 750 crore turnover company for about 195 crores and another 250 crores is going to be invested to grow the company and bring it to a normalized EBITDA.

items.statement: Divested wiping business in January 2025; loss on divestment booked in P&L and cash flow
items.quote: Furthermore, it was a strategic decision which we had taken to divest the wiping business which albeit a small portion of our overall turnover was contributing some bottom line which we divested in the month of January.

items.statement: Significant R&D hiring for new product verticals (2-wheeler and 4-wheeler PV); costs to persist for 8-12 quarters before revenue contribution
items.quote: During this quarter, we have significantly increased our manpower in R&D to start development work of products for these new verticals and products and have also hired subject matter expert consultants and these costs are not a one-time cost but will remain for the coming quarters.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty impacting exports; temporary jolt expected for ~2 quarters; risk of margin pressure if tariffs require price sharing
items.quote: There could be a risk in the margins based on what the tariffs are going to be imposed. Our margins could come down a little bit, which I think we will have a lot more clarity on in about 3 months because a lot of the customers also want us to share if there is a tariff impact, share some of that tariff impact by reducing our

items.statement: ROCE at 22.86% in FY25 vs 23.18% in FY24; marginal reduction due to acquisition
items.quote: At a consolidated level, our return on capital employed is at 22.86% in FY25 as against 23.18% in FY24 with a marginal reduction again due to the account of our acquisition.

items.statement: Tax rate at 25.168% (lower tax regime); expected to remain similar
items.quote: The tax rates are similar throughout the year. 25.168% we are at the lower tax regime and it is going to be similar in the coming period as well.

items.statement: Signed 3 acquisitions: Core Diagnostics (closed end-March), Scientific Pathology (Agra), and Dr. Ahujas' Pathology & Imaging Center (Dehradun); Core adds oncology/genomics platform and 1,700 oncologist connect; other two give leadership in
items.quote: Number one is Core Diagnostics, the leader in pan-India oncology testing, which we closed also end of March. The other 2 we have signed and not closed yet, Scientific Pathology, which is the leading chain in Agra, positioning us as the second largest player in Western Uttar Pradesh; and Dr. Ahujas' Pathology and Imaging Center, DAPIC, which is Dehradun's premier diagnostic provider, giving us lead

items.statement: North India revenue contribution expected to grow from 8% to 14-15% in FY26 after the three acquisitions.
items.quote: With this, the region's contribution to overall revenue is expected to grow from 8% to approximately 14% to 15% in FY '26.

items.statement: Target adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of ~100 bps on organic business in FY26 (from 24.4% to ~25.4%).
items.quote: we expect the EBITDA to expand by about 1 percentage in this financial year.

items.statement: Patient volume growth guidance of 7% for FY26 (vs 6% in FY25).
items.quote: this current year, we are confident of getting back to the 7 percentage range on patient volume growth.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth guidance of ~12% for FY26 (7% volume + 5% realization); acquired entities expected to grow 13-14%; combined reported growth ~25-26%.
items.quote: we expect the revenue growth to be in the similar range of 12 percentage as w e did during the previous year. And of course, the acquired entities will also grow about 13, 14 percentage in this year

items.statement: B2C revenue contribution expected to rise 1-2 percentage points in FY26 (from 55% in FY25).
items.quote: we expect the expansion to be in the range of 1 to 2 percentage more in this financial year.

items.statement: Capex for organic business guided at INR 50-55 crore for FY26 (down from INR 60-70 crore in recent years).
items.quote: we believe that the capex numbers will be closer to INR 50 crores for the organic business for this year. So you can say INR 50 crores, INR 55 crores.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics to reach high single-digit EBITDA margin in FY26 (from breakeven); Scientific and DAPIC at Metropolis-level margins with no dilution.
items.quote: Core from a breakeven, they'll get into a single-digit EBITDA during this year. That's the plan that we stated before as well. And the other 2 acquisitions that we have done is in the same range of the company margins. Then there is no dilution or anything from that side.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics FY25 revenue ~INR 105-110 crore (breakeven EBITDA); Scientific Pathology ~INR 25-26 crore; DAPIC ~INR 10-11 crore (both at Metropolis-level margins).
items.value: INR 105-110 cr, INR 25-26 cr, INR 10-11 cr
items.quote: Core is approximately, between INR105 crores and INR 110 crores of revenue with breakeven sort of -- I mean it had a loss in '25. But currently, in Q4, it's at a breakeven level. And then for Scientific, I think it's about INR 25 crores to INR 26 crores for the whole year in FY '25. And Dehradun is approximately INR 10 crores to INR 11 crores of revenue.

items.statement: FY25 adjusted EBITDA INR 325 crore (+14% YoY), margin 24.4%; Q4 adjusted EBITDA INR 84 crore (+5% YoY), margin 24.3%; reported EBITDA impacted by INR 21 crore one-time acquisition/tax/inventory costs.
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for FY '25 stood at INR 325 crores, an increase of 14% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA margin for the quarter were 24.3% and for the full-year, it stood at 24.4%.

items.statement: Gross margin stable at ~80% for 8 quarters; no further pressure expected; Core gross margin at 60% with procurement synergy upside.
items.quote: We are not -- yes, we're not anticipating any further pressure on the gross margin levels.

items.statement: Q4 saw lower revenue in February due to seasonal weather impacting acute testing volumes; March recovered and April normal; Q1 revenue buildup expected in line.
items.quote: In terms of quarter 4 operating performance, we observed lower-than-usual revenue in February, particularly in our focus markets. This quarter also witnessed a decline in acute testing volumes due to seasonal weather changes, which impacted hospital footfa ll and diagnostic demand. Having said that, the positive development is that March saw a healthy recovery and April followed normal trends

items.statement: B2C revenue grew 17% YoY in FY25 (INR 735 crore, 55% of revenue); Maharashtra B2C +19%; Tier 3 towns +18% YoY, now 26% of domestic revenue.
items.quote: B2C revenues grew by 17 percentage in financial year '25, driven by the adoption of a more granular approach, leveraging micro marketing strategies for targeted outreach and engagement.

items.statement: TruHealth segment revenue +24% YoY, 19% of total (Q4 exit rate); Specialty segment +13% YoY, 37% of total; added 60 new tests across oncology, women/child, chronic, nephrology, molecular genomics; launched HPV DNA self-sampling kit and here
items.quote: Our Tru Health segment registered a 24% year-on-year revenues increase, now contributing to 19% of the total revenues, considering the exit run rate of quarter 4.

items.statement: Added 29 labs and 400+ centers in FY25; 85 labs added over 4 years (51 in Tier 2/3); now present in 750 towns (up from 350); lab expansion phase largely complete, focus shifts to collection center acceleration and lab consolidation (includi
items.quote: We have added 29 labs at a gross level in financial year '25 and have added more than 400 centers. Over 85 labs have been added in the last 4 years with 51 of these getting added in the Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.

items.statement: Q4 FY25: selective price increases in 4-5 markets and rationalization in a few; net realization impact ~2%; no price changes planned for next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: in the quarter 4 of '25, we did do a price increase in the select markets, like I said, as a part of the micro marketing strategy, about 4, 5 markets, we took the prices up. And then a few markets, we also kind of rationalized the prices. The net impact of that is about close to 2 percentage.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR 118 crore as of March 31, 2025.
items.quote: We have a net cash surplus of INR 118 crores as at 31, March 2025.

items.statement: Surendran promoted to Managing Director; Sameer Patel appointed CFO; Diya Suri appointed Chief People Officer; Rehan Khan and Purvi Sheth added as Independent Directors.
items.quote: We have promoted Surendran to the Managing Director of the business with a clear focus on enhanced organizational performance and improving shareholder returns. We have recently appointed Sameer Patel as CFO; and Diya Suri as Chief People Officer.

items.statement: Tax litigation ongoing: appeal decided in company's favor (refund received), but further stages possible; uncertainty on whether authorities will pursue.
items.quote: Well, we did get a very positive thing on the appeal. So on the appeal side, everything has been sort of disallowed and we've actually got a tax refund. But as we know, after appeal, there is usually 1 or 2 more stages in the tax situation. So it's very di fficult at this point to say that it's completely done with

items.statement: Health-tech/e-commerce competitors less aggressive now; omnichannel (brick-and-mortar + digital) working well; B2C growth sustainable from center expansion, product mix upsell, and added services (radiology, vital checks).
items.quote: To be honest with you, we don't hear so much around the health-tech players much anymore. We don't see the aggression either on the ground or from a funding perspective either at this point of time. We are finding that the omnichannel approach that we are taking, which is the brick-and-mortar as well as online digital engagement is actually working quite well with customers.

items.statement: Patient volume +6% YoY, test volume +7% YoY in FY25; B2B revenue +12% YoY (INR 477 crore); B2C revenue +17% YoY (INR 735 crore); routine/semi-specialty slowdown in Q4 seen as temporary, expected to return to double-digit growth in Q1/Q2.
items.quote: In financial year '25, patient volumes increased by 6% year-on-year, while the test volume rose by 7 percentage.

items.statement: One-time costs of INR 21 crore in Q4: majority M&A diligence/transaction costs (evaluated 6 targets, closed 3), tax case legal expenses, and INR 1-2 crore inventory provisioning; no further M&A costs expected in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Reported EBITDA was impacted by one-time expenses of about INR 21 crores on account of 3 acquisitions completed in quarter 4. These costs include transaction fees and diligence expenses such as legal, financial, banking and tax, etc., as well as provisioning of one-time incentive and other allied costs aimed at a seamless integration and synergies.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics acquired for INR 218 crore (vs INR 247 crore signed); INR 130 crore cash, rest equity; CEO and team retained; consolidation of overlapping labs with Metropolis underway.
items.quote: One more thing you have to remember on Core that while we had signed the deal at about INR 247 crores of acquisition value, finally, what we booked in our books is INR 218 crores of acquisition value on closing. So that's just information for you. Gaurav: And the equity cash split remains the same, right? Ameera Shah: That's right. INR 130 crores was cash and the rest was equity

items.statement: Acquisitions expected to add INR 20-25 crore EBITDA in FY26; Scientific and DAPIC closures expected by end of April (Q1 FY26 consolidation).
items.quote: Yes. So it should be between INR 20 crores, INR 25 crores.

items.statement: Target to cross 100 boutiques in FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain on track to be able to cross 100 boutiques during the current financial year.

items.statement: Opened 14 new boutiques in FY25, reaching 73 total across 26 cities
items.quote: We successfully inaugurated 14 new boutiques in FY '24-'25 and reached a count of 73 boutiques across 26 cities.
