items.statement: City of Time Gurgaon opened 10 May 2025 spanning 22,000 sq ft with 5 exclusive brand boutiques and 2 multi-brand galleries
items.quote: City of Time, Gurgaon, we also opened India's largest horological project on 10th May. The City of Time Gurgaon spanning over 22,000 square feet features five exclusive brand boutiques and two multi-brand galleries with 50-plus independent brands, watchmaking zones, a cigar lounge and more.

items.statement: Two more exclusive brand boutiques to open by next quarter to complete City of Time rollout
items.quote: Two more exclusive brand boutiques will be opened by the next quarter to complete the City of Time rollout.

items.statement: Launched first Messika boutique on 14 May 2025, entering international luxury jewellery segment
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the launch of our first Messika boutique on 14th May, marking a key milestone in our foray into the International Luxury Jewellery segment.

items.statement: Second Rimowa boutique in Delhi under construction; third location identified
items.quote: We will soon launch our second Rimowa boutique in Delhi, further strengthening our presence in the premium luxury luggage segment and expanding our footprint of Rimowa in key metropolitan markets.

items.statement: Pre-owned segment (Second Movement) grew over 30% year-on-year in FY25
items.quote: Our pre -owned segment also continues to demonstrate strong traction, growing at over 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Implemented hedging strategy covering ~50% of foreign currency exposure via forward contracts
items.quote: We have now implemented a prudent hedging strategy covering approximately 50% of our foreign currency exposure through forward contracts.

items.statement: EFTA agreement with Switzerland expected to be effective by end of 2025; benefits to be shared with brands
items.quote: From my understanding, the EFTA agreement will be effectively in place by the end of this year. This is from the comments that I've read in the media from the ministers and talking to -- with our discussions with the Swiss Embassy as well that I think the benefit will start flowing in by the end of this year.

items.statement: April 2025 was very strong; May slowdown due to geopolitical tensions, not tariffs; demand expected to recover
items.quote: In India, we don't see any impact on demand at the moment. April was a very strong month for us. And May, the only slowdown in May has been because of geopolitical tensions, nothing so much for tariffs, and we don't expect any -- even May will recover.

items.statement: Gross margin reached 31% in FY25; structural improvement from lower discounting and India-specific products; CHF volatility currently suppressing margin
items.quote: I think that long term, there will be sustainability. I think 31% could have been much higher because we're in a volatile place where the rupee is because of whatever is happening in the world and global tariffs and flight -- flight of capital to safe havens such as the Swiss franc.

items.statement: Rimowa and Messika margins higher than watch category
items.quote: I think that we are doing very well over there. And all I can say is that margins are higher than the -- margins are higher than the watch category.

items.statement: FY25 volume grew 15.5% YoY; average selling price grew 7.4%; exclusive brand share over 30% in Q4
items.quote: In terms of overall volume, it grew by almost 15.5% year-on-year. And in terms of average selling price, it grew by 7.4%.

items.statement: Exclusive brand share over 30% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: That is the house brand share is over 30% in quarter four, the exclusive brands is over 30% in quarter four.

items.statement: Inventory rose from INR 440 cr to INR 593 cr due to 14 new boutiques, City of Time, Messika boutique, and pre-arranged inventory for 8 May openings
items.quote: Because of the above reasons, the inventory moved from INR 440 crores on 31st March 2024 to INR593 crores as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Working capital expected to normalize over time as new boutiques ramp up

items.statement: No significant equity investment planned in Favre Leuba (Silvercity) in FY26

items.statement: Rebranding exercise underway for 6 months; logo finalized; full implementation targeted by end of 2025

items.statement: CHF/INR volatility (moved from ~96 to ~103) delaying price hikes; brands advised to wait 2 months before adjusting

items.statement: Long-term vision: 10x revenue growth over 10 years from listing; segment split too early to quantify

items.statement: Exploring franchising for faster rollout; study underway; no rollout expected in FY26

items.statement: Favre Leuba present in ~40-45 locations; similar distribution to Rimowa and Frederique Constant

items.statement: Signed location for large flagship boutique in Chennai; opening in 2-3 years

items.statement: Targeting Vijayawada entry next year; Tier 2 cities like Dehradun profitable in first year

items.statement: Pre-owned business accelerating; needs more service centers; plans to open 1-2 more boutiques (Mumbai, Bangalore) next year
items.quote: Next year, we will be opening two more boutiques or at least one more boutique in Mumbai and then in Bangalore. So I do see acceleration taking place.

items.statement: ROCE improvement levers: higher revenue, margin expansion via mix/discounting, modular fit-outs to reduce capex/sq ft, inventory optimization via software

items.statement: Guided FY26 revenue growth of 30%-35% with EBITDA margin around 8%

items.statement: Target to reduce Consumer business mix to 30% in FY26 from 35% in FY25

items.statement: Expect exports to cross INR1,000 crores in FY26 after missing FY25 target

items.statement: Target net working capital below 65 days in upcoming year from current 69 days

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12.4% driven by mix shift and operational efficiencies

items.statement: Order book at INR5,200-5,400 crores as of March 31, 2025 with execution up to 18 months

items.statement: Flight contribution margin reached 45.2% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Contribution Margin reached INR 39.6 crores with a margin percentage of 45.2%.

items.statement: GTV grew 65% YoY to INR 4,418.4 crores in Q4 FY25; full year FY25 GTV was INR 14,971.6 crores, up 46% YoY
items.quote: Our gross transaction value or GTV rose by 65% in Q4 to INR 4,418.4 crores. For a full year FY '25, we recorded INR 14,971.6 crores in GTV, a 46% increase year-over-year.

items.statement: Monthly transacting users crossed 3.7 million in Q4 with 4% MTU to MAU ratio
items.quote: The bigger achievement, though, is how we have grown our monthly transacting users, which have crossed 3.7 million monthly transacting users as of Q4 with a 4% MTU to MAU ratio.

items.statement: Annual active users crossed 544 million and monthly active users crossed 83 million in FY25
items.quote: We have hit pretty meaningful scale with annual active users crossing 544 million for the full year and our monthly active users crossing 83 million across our brands, apps and websites.

items.statement: Bus segment booked 0.55 crore passenger segments in Q4 FY25, up 78% YoY, GTV INR 552.5 crores
items.quote: In Q4, we recorded INR 0.55 crores Passenger segment bookings, making a 78% year-over-year growth and generating a GTV of INR 552.5 crores.

items.statement: Flight segment booked 0.25 crore passenger segments in Q4 FY25, up 73% YoY, GTV INR 1,709.2 crores, up 92% YoY
items.quote: In Q4, we booked INR 0.25 crores Flight segment, a 73% year-over-year increase with a GTV of INR 1,709.2 crores, which is a 92% growth Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Train segment booked 2.62 crore passenger segments in Q4 FY25, up 30% YoY, GTV INR 2,107.1 crores, up 41% YoY
items.quote: In Q4, we booked INR 2.62 crores segment, marking a 30% growth over Q4 FY '24 and contributing to INR 2,107.1 crores, up 41% year-over-year.

items.statement: Jammu & Kashmir saw 70% YoY booking growth in April before Pahalgam attack disrupted tourism
items.quote: the Pahalgam terror attack happened at a time when Jammu and Kashmir was seeing 70% growth Y-o-Y in bookings for us in the month of April.

items.statement: Gen Z and solo travelers dominated Maha Kumbh bookings; over 50% of visitors across all modes were under 30 years old
items.quote: On train, solo travelers made up over half the train bookings to Prayagraj and a staggering 50% of all visitors to Maha Kumbh across all modes of travel that we saw were under 30 years of age.

items.statement: Half of new flight bookers in Q4 were booking their first flight ever, indicating new-to-market user acquisition
items.quote: half of those new users who came to book on the NBU apps had never booked a flight in their life. So we are basically creating a new market.

items.statement: AI-based optimization algorithm prices Travel Guarantee and decides which waitlisted tickets get offered the product, keeping it profitable
items.quote: Our AI-based optimization algorithm for pricing this product as well as deciding for which waitlisted ticket this product even gets offered for, allows us to run this product in a profitable manner.

items.statement: Voice AI agents now handle 45% of flight customer support voice interactions end-to-end
items.quote: recently, we rolled out voice AI agents for our flight and train customer support, and we are already seeing 45% of our flight customer support on voice being done end-to-end by these AI agents.

items.statement: Annual spend per transacting user grew from INR 6,537 in FY23 to INR 9,705 in FY25, compounding at 22% CAGR
items.quote: We have grown from INR 6,537 per user per annum in FY '23 to INR 9,705 per user per annum in FY '25, compounding at 22% CAGR, signifying our deepening relationship with our customers.

items.statement: 85.8% of transactions in FY25 were from repeat bookers
items.quote: In FY '25, 85.8% of our transactions were done by repeat bookers, who have booked with us, which shows the loyalty and faith our users have put upon us.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 72% YoY to INR 284.1 crores in Q4 FY25; full year FY25 revenue was INR 914.2 crores, up 39% YoY
items.quote: Revenue from operations stood at INR 284.1 crores for the quarter, a 72% increase Y-o-Y. For FY '25, the number was INR 914.2 crores, a 39% increase Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Contribution margin grew 69% YoY to INR 120.9 crores in Q4 FY25; full year contribution margin was INR 401.3 crores, up 37% YoY
items.quote: On contribution margin, we delivered INR 120.9 crores in Q4, up 69%. For full year, our contribution margin totalled INR 401.3 crores, growing 37% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA improved to INR 29.1 crores in Q4 FY25 from INR 17.1 crores in Q4 FY24; full year adjusted EBITDA was INR 94.8 crores vs INR 55.3 crores
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding other income and ESOP costs, improved to INR 29.1 crores for the quarter, up from INR 17.1 crores in Q4 FY '24. On a full year basis, we closed FY '25 at INR 94.8 crores in adjusted EBITDA compared to INR 55.3 crores last year.

items.statement: Profit After Tax more than doubled to INR 16.8 crores in Q4 FY25 from INR 7.3 crores in Q4 FY24; full year PAT was INR 60.3 crores vs INR 73.1 crores in FY24
items.quote: Profit After Tax stood at INR 16.8 crores for the quarter compared to INR 7.3 crores in Q4 last year, an increase of 128%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow nearly quadrupled over 3 years from INR 30.8 crores in FY23 to INR 122 crores in FY25
items.quote: our operating cash flow has nearly quadrupled over 3 years from INR 30.8 crores in FY '23 to INR 122 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Suspended flight and hotel bookings for certain countries on May 10, 2025 due to geopolitical conflict; will reassess as situation evolves
items.quote: On May 10, 2025, driven by feedback from our users, we took a decision to suspend flight and hotel bookings for certain countries whose actions and stance during the conflict sparked significant public outrage in India.

items.statement: Bus business benefits from fixed CAPEX model; better CAPEX utilization for bus operators enables higher commission sharing
items.quote: And remember, for bus, the interesting thing is bus is a fixed CAPEX business. So in case we are able to get better CAPEX utilization, better utilization for a bus operator, he is willing to share much more.

items.statement: Core team strength is 509 people
items.quote: I want to end by thanking our team now, 509 people strong in the ixigo core business.

items.statement: Flight contribution margin percentage has dipped from the 50s as the company invests in market share growth, partially offset by AI-driven ancillary attach rate improvements.
items.quote: We used to be in the 50s at one point. And now if you see, it's come down from there.

items.statement: Combined performance marketing, discount and branding costs are maintained at 3% to 3.5% of GTV as customer inducement cost.
items.quote: I look at performance marketing discount and branding as a combined customer inducement cost. And it will be between 3% to 3.5%, where I will remain comfortable on that.

items.statement: Technology costs are proportional to query volume; cost per million queries has been declining year-over-year since measurement began.
items.quote: And I can share that, that number has been only reducing year-over-year since we started measuring it.

items.statement: Current infrastructure handles roughly 8 billion hits per week at current spend levels.
items.quote: at the current spend, we are roughly seeing about 8 billion hits every week on our infrastructure.

items.statement: AI algorithms optimize pricing of value-added services like Abhi Assured, driving significantly better attach rates, revenue and margins.
items.quote: And as time progresses, these algorithms start optimizing for P&L. And I think what we are seeing also is that this optimization is resulting in significantly better attach rate, better revenue and margins that we are starting to see now.

items.statement: AI voice agents now handle 45% of flight customer support voice queries end-to-end at full scale.
items.quote: We have already seen that almost 45% of our flight customer support voice queries are being completely handled end-to-end by AI, right, allowing us to scale this business significantly.

items.statement: Bus segment growth driven by supply expansion (new operators like FlixBus, NueGo, Fresh Bus), premiumization (non-AC to AC, government to private), and low online penetration (under 20%).
items.quote: The third part, which is penetration, is that only under 20% of bus tickets get booked online today.

items.statement: Flight demand remains strong with passengers paying premium fares year-on-year at 85-90% load factors; Maha Kumbh was a single-digit percentage GTV contributor.
items.quote: People are paying a premium on fares year-on-year and still flying 85%, 90% load factors, so it's nota one-off. There is no major impact of Maha Kumbh. Like I said, it's a single-digit percentage GTV contributor

items.statement: Monthly active users (MAU) at 82 million; MTU/MAU ratio crossed 4% from early 3s, indicating improved conversion of utility users to transacting customers.
items.quote: the top of the funnel if you see on a monthly basis, it's our MAUs, it's 82 million, we have got monthly actives, which is the top of the funnel, and that is the potential which you are talking about.

items.statement: Repeat transaction rate at 85.8% in FY25 (close to 86%), with ancillary attach rate at 29.23%, demonstrating high stickiness built without discounting.
items.quote: close to 86% of our transactions in FY '25 were done by repeat bookers.

items.statement: Moat built on deep customer problem understanding and utility-led ecosystem (train PNR, flight tracker, running status) creating sticky, closed user base; network effects and proprietary data add defensibility.
items.quote: if you go back even one more step before that, how did we get there, by understanding customer problems more deeply than anybody else, right? And I think that's a harder playbook to copy, because it takes a while to build some of those things or scale some of those things or prove them.

items.statement: Hotels business in early build-out phase focusing on customer experience (inventory, trust, digital content); no marketing spend, leveraging 83 million monthly captive audience for cross-sell.
items.quote: we are not spending a single amount of dollar or penny to acquire customers to transact on hotels on our platform. And the reason is very simple because we have an extremely large captive audience in our platform, like 83 million people coming monthly on our platform.

items.statement: Company does not provide forward-looking guidance; remains confident in ability to solve customer problems and sustain growth through innovation and new growth vectors.
items.quote: The first thing I would say is we don't give forward-looking guidance. So I would not comment on any specific number.

items.statement: ESOP costs expected to remain around 20% range (may go slightly above due to new target-based incentive plan approved by shareholders); new plan includes VWAP, market cap and time-based criteria.
items.quote: sometime back, I told you that we would be roughly within the range of around 20 maximum. It might go slightly above 20, because as we have already declared, we have got a target-based incentive plan, which the shareholders have voted on.

items.statement: Flight take rate variance driven by fixed fee structure and underlying flight price/mix changes; core business lies outside top 4 metros affecting average price.
items.quote: a large part of my take rate is fixed, and the underlying flight price decides what my take rate would be.

items.statement: Train OTA market share at 58% (disclosed last quarter) and continuing to grow at speed despite high share.
items.quote: on trains, we disclosed this last quarter, 58% share of the OTA market. We continue to grow at the speed that we do, right?

items.statement: No one-off items in flight contribution margin (no GDS incentive true-ups or VAT one-offs); incentives prorated across applicable periods.
items.quote: There are no one-offs in there, just to clarify that. And typically, this kind of incentive, even if they come, are prorated across the period on which they are applicable, etc.

items.statement: Health retail price hike implemented after 6 years; zone-wise pricing introduced; no immediate further hike planned

items.statement: Property (fire) rates corrected after May-Dec decline and have held well for last 4-5 months

items.statement: Cross-border reinsurers (CBRs) agreed to premium withheld option; renewal went smoothly
items.quote: Most of the CBRs whom we interact with, they have agreed for a premium withheld option and that has been going very smooth. In fact, we did not experience any resistance or any great challenges during this renewal.

items.statement: One-time provision of Rs 802 crore for legacy reinsurance balances; aimed at cleaner books for AM Best A- rating
items.quote: No, this is a one-time provisioning because it is actually we have been working hard to get back our global credit rating and some of the aspects that have come in the way of getting back our A minus (excellent) rating from AM Best. items.statement: Investment portfolio mix: debt 70-72%, equity 15-16%, rest money market

items.statement: Targets INR 800 crore revenue with 20-30% EBITDA from 2GW solar cell plant
items.quote: We are expecting 2-gigawatt utility and 1 gigawatt machinery as a first page and expected revenue will be up to INR 800 crores with EBITDA of 20% to 30%.

items.quote: Currently, our distribution segment is looking after 8 states. For pump division, again, last year, we were only in two states. Currently, we have a tender up to 8 different states.

items.statement: PAT margin improved due to revenue tripling from INR 149 cr to INR 439 cr while fixed costs absorbed
items.quote: One is our turnover itself say, we've gone from 150 crores to 430 plus. So and earlier year, because we were planning to expand, we had, say example, more staff, even we had the bigger infrastructure and everything.

items.statement: Forward sales mix: pump 35-40%, wholesale 400+ cr, retail & C&I remainder
items.quote: In pump segment, we are expecting 35% to 40%. And the remaining, we are expecting from distribution business. So the pump business, we are in terms of turnover, if we see, we are expecting 300 plus in pump, 400 plus in wholesale and remaining retail and C&I.

items.statement: 60-70% of business is cash-and-carry; pump segment has 60-90 day cycle but no near-term liquidity issues
items.quote: our 60% to 70% business is ca sh and carry, and only a few % of the business is holding some money. So currently, in short term, I don't see any liquidity issue currently

items.quote: I don't think so in near future, we require to sell it in overseas, at least 5 to 15 months.

items.quote: Because of our long-term relationship with some suppliers, especially Jupiter, we are working with along with them last ten years, we got a long-term contract to get the 350, 140-megawatt supply from them.

items.statement: Revenue split: Gujarat 40%, Rajasthan 20%, Maharashtra 10-15%, remainder from pump/other states
items.quote: Say, overall, from Gujarat, we got around 40% this year and 20% from Rajasthan, 10% to 15% from Maharashtra and remaining from the retail operation from pump and the other state of distribution.

items.statement: Differentiated by diversified model (manufacturing + distribution + pump + retail/C&I) vs pure-play peers like Alpex, INA

items.statement: Equity raise of INR 18 cr in final approval; not actively seeking institutional investors for next 8-12 weeks
items.quote: We are going to do the I mean, fundraising would be in the form of equity as well as debt funding. Like we are -- if you have seen that we have already raising funds of about INR 18 crores right now in APS.

items.statement: Key constraints: cash flow management and long-term policy visibility for solar cell/battery storage expansion
items.quote: Managing cash flow and having right policy, long term policy in a country, those two things are very, very important.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 175 crore with 15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Revenue, this year, we are expecting, see revenue wise, we are targeting somewhat about Rs. 175 Cr this year with 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target close to Rs 300 crore with EBITDA margin close to 20%

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization at 90%, expansion will enable Rs 300 crore revenue potential over next 2-3 years

items.statement: Targeting 20-22% EBITDA margin for FY27, gradual improvement from FY26 15% guidance
items.quote: 28% won't be there, but just but we are looking at somewhere around 20% at least 20 %-22% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Chairman Mr. Prakash Lade passed away on December 29, 2024; was integral to organization and pivotal in shaping company

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 19.8% in FY25 from 17.6% in FY24; targets 3% expansion to ~23% in FY26

items.statement: Plans health-forward SKUs including protein-rich trail mixes, functional bars, seasonal gifting packs, and youth-centric ProV minis in FY26
items.quote: We are gearing up to launch health-forward SKUs including protein-rich tail mixes, functional bars, seasonal gifting packs tailored for weddings and festivals and youth-centric formats like ProV minis.

items.statement: All raw material cost increases have been passed on to consumers; further price increases remain a risk
items.quote: So, whatever has increased on the raw material side, we have passed on. So, now it is completely passed on. There may be a risk of further increasing the prices.

items.statement: Added 25+ senior hires across sales, marketing, R&D, finance; mostly marketing; Shalin Khanna (WTD) resigned for personal reasons; no leadership vacuum

items.statement: Shalin Khanna resigned as whole-time director for personal reasons; remains significant shareholder; senior hiring continues to strengthen leadership

items.statement: Top risks for FY26: 1) RM prices up 25% may soften demand and hit profitability, 2) demand softness, 3) Surat facility execution delay

items.statement: Has sufficient capital for expansion; not currently raising capital; any future raise would be for strategic purposes only

items.statement: Sky Gate acquisition: 80.72% stake via preferential allotment of DIL shares, shareholder approval received, closing in next couple of weeks
items.quote: The stake of 80.72% will be settled by way of preferential allotment of DIL shares in accordance with the SEBI Regulations. DIL shareholders have voted in favor of the transaction, and we are planning to close the same in the next couple of weeks.

items.statement: Sky Gate portfolio includes buyout of Goila Butter Chicken and Mumbai franchise partner consolidation
items.quote: we have to do a buyout of one or two subsidiaries and that is where some of the cash out of Rs. 90 crore will go away. Because Goila Butter Chicken is not fully owned by Sky Gate. So , we have to complete that ac quisition, that is part of the terms. At the same time, Mumbai franchise partner ownership has to be consolidated

items.statement: KFC India SSSG -6% in Q4 FY25 on base of -7%
items.quote: the SSSG number of -6 is also on a base of -7 which was on a base of +2.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR1,350-1,400 crores (15-18% growth) and EBITDA margin of 6-6.5%
items.quote: For the full year 2026, we believe revenue will be in the range of INR1,350 crores to INR1,400 crores, representing a growth of 15% to 18% over FY '25. EBITDA for the year is forecast at between 6% to 6.5%.

items.statement: FY27 target to return to 7-7.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We've mentioned that by fiscal '27 we want to get back to the 7%, 7.5% EBITDA. We are 100% confident of getting back to these numbers by that time.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance of INR100-125 crores, with INR60-65 crores for Bhiwadi Phase 1
items.quote: capex for the year will likely be in a range of INR100 crores to INR125 crores. The split is INR60 crores approximately towards Phase 1 of the new plant at Bhiwadi and the balance for the existing business and factories.

items.statement: Bhiwadi plant total capex INR90-95 crores, 2/3 spent in FY26
items.quote: Bhiwadi, the total capex is in the range of INR90 crores, INR95 crores. So out of the INR90 crores, INR95 crores this year, we will be spending INR60 crores, INR65 crores, which is approximately 2/3.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 70-75%, can scale to 85-95% with demand
items.quote: But at a very, very high level across -- for the entire company, it's approximately between 70% and 75%.

items.statement: Bhiwadi plant operational by March 2026, FY27 revenue INR140 crores, FY28 INR250 crores, full potential INR550-600 crores
items.quote: We expect the plant to be operational and contributing to revenue by March 2026. We expect a revenue of INR140 crores in FY '27 and INR250 crores in FY '28. The full revenue potential of the plant is between INR550 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: Fans revenue up 2x YoY in Q4, export of fans from Goa commenced
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter is up 2x on a Y-o-Y basis. We are further working on making some operational enhancements, which should further drive revenue and profitability in the fans business. Also, our export of fans out of Goa has commenced.

items.statement: Medium appliances (fans, OFR) currently INR65-70 crores revenue, scaling via Bhiwadi
items.quote: Should be -- if I talk of medium appliances currently being fans and OFRs, it should be in the range of INR65 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: Q4 recurring EBITDA margin 5.9% (reported 6.4%), driven by 70bps gross margin improvement and operating leverage
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR20.3 crores against INR12.4 crores in the same period last year. This has been driven by 70 basis points of higher gross margins and some operating leverage playing out.

items.statement: Operations excellence team saved INR1.5 crores in Q4 (INR6 crores annual run rate), targeting INR8-9 crores savings in FY26
items.quote: We have achieved a savings of INR1.5 crores for Q4 or an annual run rate of INR6 crores per annum. We are further confident of achieving this and increasing this to INR8 crores to INR9 crores for the full year FY '26 across labor and overheads.

items.statement: Employee cost to revenue improved from 14-14.5% to under 13% in Q4, targeting 12.5% for FY26
items.quote: We have managed to bring this down to slightly under 13% for the current quarter. We expect for the full year, us to be able to bring this down to around 12.5-odd percent for the full year for the company as a whole.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to ~27% in Q4 from historical 25%, targeting 100bps improvement from mean levels via purchasing savings and mix
items.quote: you look at our current quarter, we are at approximately close to 27%, right? [Inaudible 0:25:08]. We've already seen that improvement. Now obviously, this is not going to happen every quarter, because there is some element of sales mix also that plays a part

items.statement: Strategy to become one-stop shop for high-value home appliances; medium appliances (air coolers, fryers, chimneys, OTGs) have realizations of INR2,100-5,000 vs current INR300-600
items.quote: These medium appliances that we are planning to make have realizations between INR2,100 to INR5,000 per product. This is substantially more than our realization from our current range of products, which stand at between INR300 to INR600 per product.

items.statement: OTG launch in Q2 FY26, chimneys in prototype phase targeting Q4 FY26 trials, air coolers/fryers/ovens from Bhiwadi FY27
items.quote: Looking to the OTG, we will be starting from quarter 2. Already the orders are processed. Yes, the scale up, which we project in a larger scale as medium domestic appliances will be done in Bhiwadi plant next year.

items.statement: Net working capital at 52 days (unchanged YoY), targeting 40-45 days by H1 FY26 via fortnightly review mechanism
items.quote: We are currently at 52 days. We are saying that we will do 40 to 45 days. So we are talking of, say, between 7 days on the lower side, 12 days on the higher side.

items.statement: Inventory ~45 days (on material consumed), debtor ~70 days, fortnightly review of AR/AP/inventory implemented
items.quote: Inventory is closer to 45. So inventory, we look at on material consumed, not on revenue basis.

items.statement: FY26 capex funded by internal accruals, no long-term debt expected, working capital debt on need basis
items.quote: This is going to be largely funded only by internal accruals. Even after this large round of capex, we do not expect to have any debt on our books. When I say debt, I mean long-term debt, working capital debt on a need basis, obviously, is actually present right now.

items.statement: Exploratory talks with global OEMs to localize in India and export to USA/Western markets, engagement levels encouraging
items.quote: We are in exploratory talks with a few global OEMs to localize in India and export to U.S.A. and the Western world. While still in early stages, the engagement levels have been very encouraging.

items.statement: China cost advantage 4-8% on bill of materials, but India more competitive on conversion/labor (China labor 4x Indian)
items.quote: As things stand today, maybe China is more competitive by anywhere between 4% on the lower side, 7%, 8% on the higher side. It is less than 10% the price differential. It's not larger than that. And if you look at China labor, China labor is almost 4x that of Indian labor cost

items.statement: Medium appliances EBITDA 7-7.5-8% despite lower gross margins (18-22%) due to lower labor/overhead ratio
items.quote: For larger -- for these larger appliances, gross margins itself are slightly lower. They're probably closer to between 18% to 22%, or 19% to 22%, in that kind of range. That said, the EBITDA is slightly higher, because like I pointed out, on -- from a labor cost and other overheads perspective, that ratio to revenue drops significantly.

items.statement: Signify JV impact uncertain, professional lighting (50% of segment) not affected, further leakage possible but unlikely to be complete
items.quote: We have mentioned in full transparency, we don't know, it's still early days. Point one, what we understand is that this is restricted to the consumer lighting part of the business. We are also present in the professional or the office part of the lighting business.

items.statement: New CEO Praveen Tandon (supply chain specialist) driving purchasing savings not yet fully reflected in numbers
items.quote: Also, one point I'd just like to make, there is a lot of work ongoing under our new CEO under the -- for the purchasing side. He is a supply chain specialist, and he is doing a lot of work on the purchasing side, which is not fully reflected in our numbers today.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 25% for FY26
items.quote: Always, I have told in my past call also, we will maintain the margin around 25%, and that will be sustainable over there.

items.statement: Targeting positive cash flow by end of FY26
items.quote: And we have targeted positive cash flow in the end of this financial year of '26.

items.statement: Capex of INR400-450 crores for additional 10,000 machines capacity over 2 years
items.quote: It's close to INR400 crores to INR450 crores capex are going to be on this additional 10,000 machines of capacity to be built over here.

items.statement: Current installed capacity of 6,000 machines at Jyoti and 120 at Huron; 90% utilization in Q4 FY25
items.quote: In terms of manufacturing capacity, we have 6,000 machines installed capacity at Jyoti and 121 machines at Huron, France.

items.statement: Additional 10,000 machines capacity to be completed in next 2 years, ready by June 2026
items.quote: Further enhancement of additional 10,000 machines per annum will be completed in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Consolidated order book of INR4,346 crores as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: Our total consolidated order book as on 31st March 2025 stands at INR4,346 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 order intake of INR530 crores
items.quote: Our Q4 FY '25 order intake comes to INR530 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin at 30.9%, up from 29.7% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has increased to 30.9% in Q4 FY '25 as compared to 29.7% in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin at 27%, up from 22.5% in FY24
items.quote: The EBITDA margin is 27% in FY '25 as compared to the 22.5% in FY '24.

items.statement: Strong demand in aerospace and defense due to geopolitical situation; customers pushing for faster delivery
items.quote: Huge pressures are there. All our existing customers are pushing us like anything today. It already started in Europe largely, in India, even now China.

items.statement: EMS order execution expected from H2 FY26 as customer plants become ready
items.quote: See, basically, our delivery been asked of this order book is starting from this financial year on second half over here there.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue mix: 44% aerospace & defense, 23% auto, 23% general engineering, 4% die & mold, 6% others
items.quote: Our Q4 FY '25 consolidated revenue from operations of INR576 crores consists of 44% from the aerospace and defense, 23% from auto and auto components, 23% from general engineering, 4% from die and mold, and 6% rest others.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 order intake mix: 29% aerospace & defense, 33% auto, 26% general engineering, 5% die & mold, 7% others
items.quote: Our Q4 FY '25 order intake comes to INR530 crores, which consists of 29% from aerospace and defense, 33% from auto and auto components, 26% from general engineering, 5% from die and mold, and 7% others.

items.statement: Launched 7 new products in January 2025 including GU 8, Tachyon Beta, AWT 22, BTM 100, ATM 200, HP 4000/6000, HUMA
items.quote: In 2025, we have designed and developed and launched following new product variants. We call it as GU 8, it is a 5 Axis gantry-type machining center; AWT 22 is alloy wheel turning machines; BTM 100 is twin spindle gantry automation; ATM 200, inverted turning center with automations; HP 4000 and HP 6000 high-performance series of a horizontal machining center; Tachyon Beta is a 5 Axis high dynamic

items.statement: HUMA HMI development to reduce controller cost (currently 10-25% of machine cost) and improve margins over 2-3 years
items.quote: In a middle-level machine, it's close to 15%, and high-end, it's close to 10% or less than 10%, like that. It's a huge big cost, okay? And there is a great opportunity to value addition over here.

items.statement: Inventory days improved from 236 in FY24 to 180 in FY25; targeting 150-160 days in FY26
items.quote: And we are anticipating to touch -- this is going to be around 150 to 160 days in the next coming year there.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in FY25 due to long manufacturing cycles; percentage completion method increasing financial assets
items.quote: So those are the machines are being built up. Let's say, we are starting the percentage completion methods, and that's why it's become -- it's going into financial assets to be there.

items.statement: Sold 1,349 machines in Q4 FY25 and 4,072 machines in FY25
items.quote: 1,349 machines we have sold in quarter 4, and full year is 4,072.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 machine sales breakdown: 1,107 entry-level (INR218 cr), 165 mid-level (INR74 cr), 77 high-end (INR252 cr)
items.quote: Yes. So in entry-level machines, we have done, in terms of value, it's INR218 crores 1,107 machines. On a mid-level, we have done INR74 crores at 165 machines. And high level is INR252 crores and 77 machines.

items.statement: EMS orders from customers building plants in India; execution dependent on customer site readiness
items.quote: Once the plants have been ready, then we are coming to picture and we need to supply from our side there.

items.statement: First mover in EMS/semiconductor equipment manufacturing in India; not worried about competition
items.quote: See, Mayank, I myself am entering on to that and competing to a Japanese there. So it is so large business if any competitors comes today also, I will not be worried about it.

items.statement: US tariff situation unclear; planning US sales office and potential manufacturing if adverse
items.quote: We were just, let's say, in the last couple of months, we were waiting to clarity on that to go to U.S. to open our sales and network there. And if anything is, let's say, adverse, then we will go and start to have some manufacturing there also.

items.statement: Huron subsidiary revenue INR253 crores, PAT ~INR8 crores in FY25; capacity expansion to $80M production
items.quote: So basically, at Huron, we have close to INR253 crores of revenue and close to EUR 865,000, which means close to INR8 crores as a PAT level there.

items.statement: Previous capex of INR310 crores increased capacity from 4,400 to 6,000 machines; new capex INR400-450 crores for 10,000 machines
items.quote: Let's say, you can see that from 6,000 to 16,000. So consolidated, we need INR450 crores like that.

items.statement: Semiconductor foray capital allocation not yet quantified; visibility expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We will quantify this in the next couple of quarters. Let's say, we are expecting, in the third quarter, we are able to see the complete road map ahead on a semiconductor.

items.statement: Center of Excellence trained 325 people in last quarter; skilled manpower identified as biggest growth challenge
items.quote: In the last quarter, close to 325 people have been trained on our center of excellence over here.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target range of Rs 1,000-1,100 crore
items.quote: But at a high level, we are looking at a range of Rs. 1,000 crores to Rs. 1,100 crores for the Financial Year '26.

items.statement: Long-term $500 million revenue target by FY30 with 25-30% CAGR
items.quote: we are still looking at the 500 million, the CAGR still is expected at 25%-30%

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected at 16-17% for next 12-18 months before returning to 17-18%
items.quote: for the next 12 to 18 months, it would be realistic to say that this is the new normal

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin at 16.56%
items.quote: The operating EBITDA for the year stood at INR 146 crores, which grew by 7% year-on-year and the EBITDA margins for the year were at 16.56%.

items.statement: No slowdown across all four verticals; healthy pipeline in BFS and emerging verticals
items.quote: No, no, no slowdown in all four verticals. You know, we have a healthy pipeline in all four, a lot of conversations.

items.statement: Focus on intelligent products (ISV product engineering) and intelligent platforms (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Databricks, Snowflake, HCL Commerce)
items.quote: we have now focused our capabilities on intelligent products and intelligent platforms

items.statement: Added new BFS client with $0.5M annual contract value in FY25
items.quote: A notable highlight of the year was the addition of a new client in the banking and financial services vertical, contributing an annual contract value of approximately USD 0.5 million.

items.statement: 15 customers with $1M+ revenue; focusing on account mining to grow next 10 accounts
items.quote: Saksoft has around 15 customers of USD $1 million plus revenues

items.statement: Investing in AI frameworks, accelerators, sales talent, and centers of excellence
items.quote: we made significant strides by making strategic investments in building AI frameworks and accelerators

items.statement: Employee utilization at 85% for FY25; 85-86% seen as high end for company size
items.quote: the utilization level of the employees excluding trainees, being at 85% for the Financial Year 2025

items.statement: Sales team split into hunters and farmers; low attrition, quick replacement of underperformers
items.quote: we have now divided the sales team into account farmers and hunters. So, no salesperson is doing both.

items.statement: DSO increased from 67 to 74 days; expected to stabilize at 75-80 days due to APAC revenue mix
items.quote: I think we have increased almost from 67 days to 74 days. I think those are short-term blips. We really don't think it will go beyond 75 to 80 days.

items.statement: Short-term debt increased for October acquisition; expected repayment in 6-9 months
items.quote: This debt was taken for the acquisition, which we did in October of last year. But it is short term, and we strongly believe that in the next six to nine months, they should be repaid off.

items.statement: Acquisitions fully integrated per 30-60-90 day plan; synergies now accruing; focus shifting to organic growth
items.quote: by the 90th day, the teams are integrated, the sales team, delivery team, support team. So, I think whatever we have acquired is fully integrated.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 0.40 per share recommended; total FY25 dividend INR 0.80 per share (80% of face value)
items.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 0.40 per share, 40% of face value of INR 1, bringing the total dividend for Financial Year '25 to INR 0.80 per share, 80% of face value

items.statement: US revenue share at 42%; targeting increase with all efforts focused on US market
items.quote: Our focus is all U.S. centric. So, you know, all our efforts is towards the U.S. market and that's where we feel there is great potential. So, you will see an increase in that region.

items.statement: Third-party charges increased due to regrouping of license costs (Salesforce, HCL, Business Objects); treat as new run rate
items.quote: it would be more appropriate to treat this as the basis for your forecasting going forward

items.statement: Guidance conservative due to US policy uncertainty and Trump administration changes
items.quote: we are being a bit conservative on the guidance, but that's due to the headwinds that we are seeing. And I think from a confidence level, we are seeing pipeline build. And as of now, no negative impact.

items.statement: FY25 revenue INR 883 crore, up 15.9% YoY; Q4 revenue INR 240 crore, up 23.1% YoY
items.quote: For the full Financial Year 2025, the revenues were reported at INR 883 crores. This represents a growth of around 15.9% year-on-year.

items.statement: FY25 net profit INR 109 crore, up 13.1% YoY; PAT margin 12.32%
items.quote: The net profit was at around INR 109 crores, which grew year-on-year by 13.1% with the PAT margins being at 12.32%.

items.statement: Management expects at least 25-34% revenue growth in FY26, with order book of INR55 crores at start of FY26 and larger ticket sizes
items.quote: We are very much on. And I think this percentage is, as a company, is the least what we are thinking at the moment.

items.statement: Opening order book for FY26 is INR55 crores, up from INR119 crores last year with INR55 crores executed in FY25
items.quote: With an order book exceeding INR55 crores in the beginning of FY25 -26, we are well positioned to accelerate execution, improve scale and drive consistent growth.

items.statement: Order book was INR119 crores at start of FY25, of which INR55 crores executed in FY25, with 6-10 month project gestation
items.quote: We had an order book of INR119 odd crores last year, out of which 55 have come this year. And then our overall project gestation period ranges from six months to ten months.

items.statement: H2 FY25 margins spiked due to project completion timing; 80-90% of revenue from supplies, 10-20% from erection/commissioning
items.quote: See I'll put it differently because if I understand your question properly, what happens is, for any job for us to supply with, I'll give an example, if there is 100% of the job which has to be done, around 80%-90% is against supplies.

items.statement: ZLD projects offer better margins due to technology differentiation and smaller footprint (10m2 vs 100m2)
items.quote: Suppose something is to be done in 100 m2 and we can do it in 10 m2. So the advantage lies in terms of the overall expense to the client and that is where we can make better margins.

items.statement: Strong demand across 14 sectors including automobile, chemical, pharma, food, beverage, white goods, optical; inquiries from multiple large companies with multi-factory presence
items.quote: The sector which we are talking about is all around, you know, because the Luminous is a battery company and it's a big company. Also, one of our objectives is to work with companies who have multiple factories.

items.statement: Customer base includes MNCs and large listed companies (Toyota, L&T, Luminous, Escorts, Mahindra); 45-60 day collection cycle for supplies, retention 10-20% for erection/commissioning
items.quote: Yes, it generally holds to that because most of the companies that we are working with are, MNCs or established companies of repute So generally, when we invoice the material, by the time it reaches their site, there is a GRN activity which goes on , another 40 to 45 days for the payments to get released.

items.statement: Receivables spiked to INR50 crores in March due to concentrated billing in Feb-Mar; 30% collected by mid-May, INR8 crores from L&T expected next week
items.quote: There has been a jump from INR21 crores to almost INR50 crores, which is equivalent to our last year revenue, almost equivalent to that. So, yes, there was a lot of billing or invoicing during the six months, specifically in the month of February and March.

items.statement: No bill discounting currently used despite availability; sufficient resources; non-fund based limits (bank guarantees) are primary capital deployment
items.quote: No, you do tend to get bill discounting, but we are still not availing that facility because we anyway have the available resources as of today, b ut tomorrow if required, we will be doing that

items.statement: Investing in automation, SAP systems, digital project monitoring, after-sales services; no major fixed asset capex planned; focus on productivity per employee
items.quote: In-house wise, we are also implementing a lot of automation and SAP systems into our company so that we are geared up to take things into consideration with times to come.

items.statement: No incremental manpower increase planned with revenue growth; targeting higher productivity per person; ESOPs planned for employees
items.quote: I don't feel there should be much increase in the manpower. But it will be in line with the industry trend or probably better. I mean, that is the objective. I want to have increased productivity per person of the company.

items.statement: Strategic focus shifting to ZLD, MBR, RO recycling; ZLD currently 20-30% of revenue; targeting larger ticket sizes (INR15-30 crores per project)
items.quote: Definitely. See, ZL D actually is the name of the game and that is what's going to change everything or that's what is the need of the hour

items.statement: Competitors include pan-India players (Thermax, Ion Exchange, Concord), sector-specific and regional players; differentiation via technology, execution quality, consultant relationships
items.quote: You have one or two all India companies like maybe Thermax, Ion Exchange or Concord or anybody. And then you have sector wise. So Luminous being a battery company. So you had, we had Membrane and another company.

items.statement: Exploring partnerships in textile and paper sectors where currently absent; no technology acquisitions planned as global technologies available via partnerships
items.quote: We are talking to one or two people for getting into industrial sector. Like, for example, we are not prevalent in textiles. We are not there in paper.

items.statement: Management committed to quarterly updates despite SEBI SME regulations; will start from subsequent quarters if not current quarter
items.quote: Definitely that is on our anvil. And we'll be, if not this quarter, I can't promise it, but definitely from subsequent quarters, we'll be doing it.

items.statement: International presence expanded in Bangladesh and Vietnam; strategic alliance with Veolia for technology access
items.quote: We successfully expanded our international presence, executing projects and developing a robust pipeline in Bangladesh and Vietnam. Our strategic alliance with the global technology leader Veolia has further deepened.

items.statement: Project gestation period 6-10 months vs 18-24 months for municipal projects; MEP-focused vs civil-heavy; enables faster cash conversion
items.quote: Our ticket size is smaller and it has more to do with the MEP stuff. So, that is one of the primary reasons that the gestation period is lower.

items.statement: No bad debt risk; receivables from reputed MNCs; MSME payment principles followed; spikes in receivables are temporary due to project billing cycles
items.quote: No, there are no bad debts as such. We are, again, like I said, I just want to reiterate that the companies which we are working with are extremely, extremely honorable, established, powerful and I mean, in the sense, they are of repute.

items.statement: IPO proceeds received only in December 2024; one quarter of deployment; bank guarantees (non-fund based) are key capital requirement
items.quote: If you see, we have only been into the market, the proceeds have come only in the month of December. And there is only one quarter we actually ha d the funds with us to perform

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin of 18.2% to be benchmark for next two years
items.quote: For current year, you can put it at FY '25 as a margin benchmark for next 2 years with the investment being made across various business segments.

items.statement: Organic top-line growth target of 15-20% CAGR for next two years
items.quote: So, in top-line growth, we will definitely look at 15-20% growth annually.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin expected around 18% for next two years
items.quote: But the blended margin we are expecting is around 18 percent for the next two years.

items.statement: Core executive search business margin expected at 23-25% for next two years
items.quote: So the original business will be having around 23 to 24 percent margin for the next 2 years. This may be slightly impacted because we will be expanding those teams as well.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected around 22% going forward
items.quote: So we are expecting it to be at around ETR of around 22% going forward.

items.statement: Loan taken to purchase new office repaid from IPO proceeds
items.quote: Finance costs increased during the year due to the loan taken to purchase the new office. This loan has been repaid from the proceeds of the IPO.

items.statement: Added five client-facing consultants in H2 FY25 across India and Dubai
items.quote: Primarily, we have added five client -facing consultants in H2 FY '25 to the executive search team between India and Dubai.

items.statement: Search team size is about 70 people across client-facing, research and middle office
items.quote: It's about 70 people across both client -facing and research and what we cal l it as the middle office team.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contributed 35% of revenue in FY25, consistent with FY24
items.quote: Revenue from top 10 clients in FY '25 contributed 35% of overall top line, which was consistent with FY '24.

items.statement: Top 3 clients contribute around 13-14% of revenue
items.quote: Top 3 clients should be consistent at around 13 to 14 percent.

items.statement: Largest client revenue dropped from ~12.5-13% to 5-5.5 crores due to internal restructuring
items.quote: The last year, the largest client contributed to about roughly about 12 .5, 13 percent of revenues. And this year, so while on a positive note, we have been able to spread it out and also because of their internal restructuring, from that particular client, the revenue dropped to about 5 to 5.5 crores on a gross number based year to year basis.

items.statement: James Douglas RPO and mid-to-senior hiring expected as key growth drivers for 3-4 years
items.quote: And so, search business, we expect to continue the same momentum and if you look at James Douglas, the James Douglas Global business, which is the RPO business, which is the new business, and as well as the mid- to senior-level business is expected to continue to be key growth drivers for us in the next, 3 to 4 years' time frame.

items.statement: New businesses (James Douglas Global RPO and mid-to-senior) could become as large as executive search business in 3-5 years
items.quote: So in a 3 to 5 year time frame, if you like to, if you look at our business, you will see that James Douglas Global, which is the RPO business, as well as James Douglas Professional, as what we call it, will be significant contributors to our top line and bottom line.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 74 crores, up ~10% YoY; core search revenue up 14% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, the consolidated revenue for operations stood at 74 crores, representing an increase of approximately 10% over the previous year. Revenue from our core executive search business in FY'25, excluding MyRCloud technology business, is up 14% year -on-year.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA Rs 13 crores at 18.2% margin; PAT Rs 13 crores at 17.06% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stood at 13 crore s, with an EBITDA margin of 18.2% a nd profit after tax was reported at 13 crores, with a PAT margin of 17.06%.

items.statement: Employee cost (excl. tech and ESOP) grew 18% due to senior hires
items.quote: Employee cost, excluding tech platform and ESOP cost, grew at 18%. This increase stemmed from our strategic decision to bolster our leadership team by onboarding senior management and key management persons in search business.
